body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A — small bug fix

### Description

Terminal execution mode is persisted after a user chooses one, but the fallback controls the experience when no preference has been stored. The fallback currently selects background execution after the recent terminal reliability work.

Restore visible VS Code terminals as the fallback while preserving both stored terminal modes. The storage default, runtime construction, direct tool construction, webview initialization, settings UI, and marketplace documentation now agree.

### Test Procedure

From `apps/vscode`:

```bash
bun test src/core/storage/utils/state-helpers.test.ts src/shared/storage/__tests__/state-keys.test.ts
bunx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/sdk/vscode-run-commands-tool.test.ts src/sdk/vscode-terminal-execution-mode.test.ts src/sdk/vscode-runtime-builder.test.ts
bunx biome check --config-path ./biome.jsonc --no-errors-on-unmatched --files-ignore-unknown=true --diagnostic-level=error src/shared/storage/state-keys.ts src/shared/storage/__tests__/state-keys.test.ts src/core/storage/utils/state-helpers.test.ts src/sdk/vscode-run-commands-tool.ts src/sdk/vscode-run-commands-tool.test.ts src/sdk/vscode-runtime-builder.ts webview-ui/src/components/settings/sections/TerminalSettingsSection.tsx webview-ui/src/context/ExtensionStateContext.tsx
bun run check-types
bun run build:webview
bun esbuild.mjs
```

The focused suites pass 36 storage/default tests and 47 terminal routing/host tests. Type checks, the compatibility type check, production webview build, extension bundle build, and an isolated Extension Development Host launch also pass.

### Type of Change

-   [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
-   [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
-   [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
-   [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes
-   [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes
-   [x] 📚 Documentation update
-   [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes

### Pre-flight Checklist

-   [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs)
-   [x] Tests are passing (`bun test`) and code is formatted and linted (`bun run format && bun run lint`)
-   [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

### Additional Notes

Background execution continues to inherit the SDK's 30-second default from `createShellTool` and `createShellExecutor`. The VS Code extension only overrides the foreground mode timeout to one hour because integrated terminal processes cannot be forcibly terminated.

author: dversoza
body:
A repo-agnostic skill for reviewing a branch diff: reviewers find defects, separate skeptics try to kill each one, and only what survives is reported.

The refutation step is the whole point. Without it a review returns a long list of plausible-sounding items, most of them wrong, and the reader learns to skim — which is worse than no review, because it costs attention and buys false confidence.

## Two tiers

`pr-review-quick` — the default for any PR. Three lenses, one refuter per finding.

`pr-review-deep` — six lenses, three-way refutation per finding (majority rules, so one contrarian cannot sink a real finding and one credulous reader cannot save a bad one), plus a critic that asks what the fixed lenses structurally could not see. Several times the cost, so it is for data correctness, money, auth, migrations, secrets, concurrency, or a shared helper with many callers.

## Why correctness and silent-wrongness are separate lenses

A reviewer asked simply for "bugs" reliably finds crashes and reliably misses the change that returns a plausible wrong answer, because nothing about it looks like an error. That is the class that survives CI, type checking and a careful human read.

Both tiers were built and shaken out against a real production codebase. Some of what they caught there:

- A `dayfirst` date flag that silently reinterpreted every ISO date, because `dateutil` resolves a leading year by position and then applies the flag to the remaining two components. Every affected value still parsed, just to the wrong month.
- A `cast(dict, json.loads(...))` added to satisfy a type checker, on an endpoint that returns a top-level array. The narrowing guard then routed those payloads down the wrong branch, and a data source discovered zero records for weeks while its API stayed healthy and returned HTTP 200.

Neither is a crash. Neither fails a test. Both are exactly what the silent-wrongness lens asks for.

## Repo-agnostic by design

Nothing about any one project is baked in. Project-specific concerns go through a `focus` argument per run — "this service is on the payment path", "every timestamp here is UTC" — so business rules stay in the repo that owns them.

## One hard-won detail

The scripts scope every command with `git -C` and make reviewers pin the target with `rev-parse` and `diff --stat` before starting, stopping if the diff looks unrelated to the stated `scope`.

That is not defensive boilerplate. On an early run the reviewers read the *session's* working directory instead of the checkout under review — a different branch, with uncommitted work — and returned three confident, thoroughly-evidenced findings about entirely unrelated code. Well-evidenced and aimed at the wrong tree is the worst failure mode a review tool has, because it is indistinguishable from a good result until someone checks the file paths.

## Honest limits, documented in the skill

Refuters default to dismissing when uncertain, so a refuted finding can still be worth a look. These panels have been wrong in both directions: one proposed a fix that did not work, another dismissed a real design gap as out of scope. `confirmed` is a strong signal, not a verdict.

Zero confirmed findings is a normal outcome and means the diff survived.

author: castrojo
body:
The merge-gate sections of `docs/skills/ci-ops/contributing/references/reviewing-and-merging.md` and `docs/skills/meta/human-gates/SKILL.md` had become an incident log — merge timestamps, commit SHAs, a PR-by-PR chronology of the lab status-reporter fixes, and lists of specific testsuite PRs with zero statuses. It was stale as soon as the next fix landed, and a fresh agent had to do archaeology to learn what to do.

Both sections now read, in order:

1. **The gate to apply today** — `ghost-lab` is not posted; do not wait for it. GHA CI green (`Lint & syntax`, `Behave dry-run`, `pytest`) plus human approval, enqueued with `gh pr merge <N> --squash --auto`. The accurate note that `main` is governed by a merge-queue ruleset (merge_queue, SQUASH, ALLGREEN) despite the 404 from `branches/main/protection` is preserved.
2. **The known reduction in assurance** — GHA CI boots no real VM, so real-VM regressions are uncaught. A documented gap, not licence to skip verification.
3. **One checkable command** for deciding whether the lab gate is live again (observe a `ghost-lab` context on the PR head SHA).
4. **The timeless lesson** — a merged fix is not a working fix; three consecutive fixes each merged green and each left the gate dead. Same failure class as a suite reporting green while silently skipping every scenario.

The counted-evidence debugging rule is kept but restated as a rule: token-like strings are redacted, so compare `grep -c` counts of the token variable and the bearer keyword against a known-working file rather than reading the header.

All live state (current status, PR numbers, dates) now lives in [`projectbluefin/lab#471`](https://github.com/projectbluefin/lab/issues/471), linked once from each file.

Additionally, `human-gates/SKILL.md` was audited against the skill spec: the frontmatter description gained a "Use when" trigger phrase, and the missing `## Red Flags` and `## Verification` sections were added (including "waiting for a `ghost-lab` status that will never arrive" and "restoring a gate because its fix merged").

No other gate was touched: the upstream/KDE prohibition, design/security/breakage gates, and the `lgtm`-required list (`e2e.yml`, `AGENTS.md`, `CODEOWNERS`) are unchanged.

## Validation

- `ruff check tests/ --select E,F,W --ignore E501` — All checks passed
- `python3 -m pytest tests/unit/ -q` — 841 passed
- `python3 scripts/validate_docs.py` — All docs validation checks passed (only pre-existing KDE reference name warnings)

author: oudaykhaled
body:
## Problem

The Firestore ruleset live on `jeeb-5a293` (`be2ddaaf-31e3-4470-8eda-e043478205ce`) authorises a message read on conversation **MEMBERSHIP alone**. chat-service computes a finer per-viewer matrix in `MessageVisibilityResolver.cs:147-188` and **never stores it**, so a direct Firestore read bypasses it.

Proven live on conversation `023e9d2c-04d7-4533-a449-6218ccc014ad`: participant `s08-rana-jeeber-radc276` reads message `9b4ba087-…` from Firestore → **HTTP 200, full body**, while chat-service `:5803` returns that same viewer only **2 of 3** messages. Controls: a non-participant on the same URL → 403; the same viewer on the conversation doc → 200.

The approved fix is an **additive `VisibleTo` array**, written by chat-service at message-write time using that same resolver, with the rule authorising on the array instead of on membership.

## Change

The new rule references `resource.data`, and Firestore refuses a LIST it cannot prove. So the `.snapshots()` LIST now carries the matching filter:

```dart
.where(kChatMessageVisibleToField, arrayContains: uid)
.orderBy(kChatMessageCreatedAtField, descending: true)   // unchanged
.limit(_window)                                           // unchanged
```

`ChatFirebaseIdentity.ensureSignedIn` returns `Future<String?>` (the uid, or null) instead of `Future<bool>`. The uid the query filters on must be the uid `request.auth.uid` will carry; two independently-supplied uids can disagree, and a filter keyed on a uid the rules do not authorise returns **zero documents silently** — a dead feature that looks healthy. Returning the uid from the one method that establishes the identity makes them the same value by construction. An empty-string uid is treated as no identity for the same reason.

The identity gate keeps its ordering: **no uid means Firestore is never reached**, not reached-and-refused.

## REQUIRED BEFORE THIS QUERY WORKS

A composite index that does not exist yet:

| | |
|---|---|
| collection | `Messages` |
| scope | `COLLECTION` (not `COLLECTION_GROUP`) |
| fields | `VisibleTo` arrayConfig `CONTAINS`, then `CreatedAt` order `DESCENDING` |

```json
{ "collectionGroup": "Messages", "queryScope": "COLLECTION",
  "fields": [ { "fieldPath": "VisibleTo", "arrayConfig": "CONTAINS" },
              { "fieldPath": "CreatedAt", "order": "DESCENDING" } ] }
```

Without it the query fails `FAILED_PRECONDITION` at runtime.

## Sequencing — this is load-bearing

This PR is **inert on merge**. The gateway mint ships disabled (`Firebase:Chat:ServiceAccountKeyPath` unset ⇒ 503 ⇒ `ensureSignedIn` returns null ⇒ no channel opens), so the HTTP path carries chat exactly as it does today.

Enabling the mint **before** chat-service writes `VisibleTo` would **not fail loudly**: the filtered query would be authorised by the still-live membership rule, return zero documents, and still report itself LIVE on its first empty snapshot — which suppresses the push-driven HTTP refetch in `ChatCubit` and leaves the thread silently receiving nothing. Correct order: chat-service writes `VisibleTo` → index exists → rule released → mint enabled.

## Not changed

The **auction gate** is untouched. `realtimeChatAdmitted` still refuses a `contested` roster in every phase; its 9 tests pass with the identical 4×3 truth table.

## Docs corrected, not advanced

`ChatFirebaseIdentity` now states that the membership-only ruleset is **still the live one** and that `VisibleTo` is pending on both halves — the previous draft asserted the new rule as present fact, which would have told a reader the leak was closed while it is open.

`firebase_identity_teardown` reworded to "Every **LIVE** call site", with both exemptions verified rather than asserted:
- `auth_interceptor.dart:144` is unreachable in production — `DioClient.createDio` has zero call sites (every live `createDio` under `lib/` is `MockGatewayClient.createDio`), and `TokenRefreshInterceptor` is constructed only at `dio_client.dart:71` inside that uncalled factory.
- `dev_seam/session_seam_bootstrap.dart:530` is debug-only — its sole call site is `seed()` at `:157`, which returns at `:140` when `!kDebugMode`.

## Test plan

```
dart analyze lib                    -> No issues found!
flutter test .../chat_realtime_auction_gate_test.dart  -> +9 All tests passed!
flutter test test/features/chat test/features/deep_link_targets \
             test/features/notifications test/features/settings
                                    -> +520 All tests passed!   (baseline 518 + 2 added)
```

`dart analyze lib`, not `flutter analyze` (exit-64 flakes in this repo).

### WHAT THE GREEN SUITE DOES NOT PROVE

**`Firebase.apps` is EMPTY in every widget test in this repo.** No test here constructs a Firestore client, issues a query, or evaluates a rule. The suite therefore proves **nothing** about the real wire, the filter, or the ruleset. What it does prove: the uid plumbing (an identity returning null or `''` never reaches Firestore; one returning a uid does), and — via a source-text pin, labelled as such — that the `.where(…arrayContains…)` clause has not been silently deleted and still precedes `.orderBy`. The filter's real behaviour is observable only on a device against live rules.

## Rollback

Revert the commit. The branch is inert while the mint is disabled, so a revert restores today's HTTP behaviour with no server-side coordination.

body:
## Plan and delivery state

- **Plan:** [`PLAN-0002 — Specify the First Authenticated Inventory Vertical Slice`](docs/plans/PLAN-0002-specify-authenticated-inventory-vertical-slice.md)
- **Plan status:** Completed
- **Registry:** [`docs/plan-status.md`](docs/plan-status.md)
- **Delivery state:** PR open; owner review and merge pending

## Summary

Define the first authenticated KitchenFlow vertical slice and provide highly detailed, executable plans for backend implementation, Lovable/frontend implementation, and independent testing.

The slice proves the accepted architecture through one real user outcome:

> An authenticated adult user can create, view, correct, consume, discard, and delete a manually entered inventory lot while every operation remains isolated to that user and auditable.

## PLAN-0002 — Vertical-slice specification

Defines exact numbered requirements for backend-managed OIDC session, internal user ownership, user-owned products and lots, measured or availability quantities, storage and package state, printed expiration, immutable adjustments, audit history, soft deletion, ETag/If-Match concurrency, PostgreSQL-backed idempotency, cursor pagination, OpenAPI errors and headers, responsive routes, three locales, accessibility, privacy, security, and observability.

AI, receipt parsing, shopping, planning, recipes, RabbitMQ business flows, Redis requirements, billing, ads, and production provisioning are explicitly excluded from this first slice.

## PLAN-0003 — Backend implementation

Provides prescriptive instructions for a backend agent, including:

- exact .NET 10 solution and project layout;
- module/reference boundaries;
- PostgreSQL schemas, constraints, decimal/date mappings, migrations, audit, and idempotency;
- Keycloak Authorization Code + PKCE integration through ASP.NET Core cookie/OIDC middleware;
- backend-managed CSRF and session endpoints;
- two-user development realm fixtures;
- exact inventory use cases and REST endpoints;
- Problem Details, ETag, If-Match, idempotency, and signed cursor behavior;
- OpenAPI 3.1 export and drift gate;
- OpenTelemetry and health behavior;
- unit, PostgreSQL integration, architecture, security, migration, and real-Keycloak smoke tests;
- exact phases, commands, exit criteria, prohibitions, and handoffs.

## PLAN-0004 — Lovable/frontend implementation

Documents the current Lovable repository constraint and uses a safe workflow:

- Lovable does not import the existing monorepo;
- the owner creates a dedicated Lovable project and generated GitHub repository;
- generated frontend history is integrated into `apps/frontend` through a tested controlled subtree workflow;
- the KitchenFlow monorepo remains the authoritative release source.

The plan includes Project Knowledge requirements, a bounded initial Plan-mode prompt, prohibition of Lovable Cloud/Supabase/generated backend/direct Keycloak SDK/browser token storage/direct AI calls, preservation of the generated TanStack Start or React/Vite runtime, OpenAPI client generation, exact UI and conflict states, localization, accessibility, responsive behavior, provenance, dependency review, tests, and handoff gates.

## PLAN-0005 — Independent testing

Adds an independent test plan with pinned baselines and more than 100 explicit P0/P1/P2 cases covering session security, CSRF, cross-user isolation, quantities, atomicity, immutable history, concurrency, idempotency, pagination, OpenAPI, migrations, three locales, accessibility, browsers, telemetry, redaction, resilience, and performance smoke.

## Development environment

Adds a canonical Windows/Linux environment specification.

Host-installed tools:

- Git;
- Docker Engine or Docker Desktop with Compose and Linux containers;
- .NET 10 LTS SDK;
- Node.js 24 LTS;
- current browsers;
- curl, jq or PowerShell equivalent, OpenSSL, and CA certificates.

Containerized first-slice services:

- PostgreSQL 18;
- Keycloak 26;
- optional/recommended OpenTelemetry Collector.

PostgreSQL Server, Java, Keycloak Server, RabbitMQ/Erlang, Redis, S3 emulator, SMTP catcher, Python, and Kubernetes are not required as native host installations.

The document covers Windows native + Docker Desktop, Windows/WSL2, Linux, hardware, ports, HTTPS, secrets, version pinning, Playwright, Lovable account requirements, CI parity, troubleshooting, and exact environment evidence required from AI agents.

## PLAN-0001 reconciliation

Confirms PR #5 was merged and reconciles PLAN-0001 delivery to `Merged`.

## Scope and impact

Documentation and execution governance only. No executable source code, package dependency, migration, API snapshot, container resource, secret, or production configuration is added.

The documents constrain future implementation; they do not claim the slice already exists.

## Validation

- Final branch is 4 commits ahead and 0 commits behind `main`.
- Reviewed all 10 changed files.
- Confirmed changes are Markdown plans, indexes, environment documentation, and infrastructure guidance only.
- Confirmed every `VS-REQ-*` group has implementation ownership and independent validation coverage.
- Confirmed PLAN-0003, PLAN-0004, and PLAN-0005 use distinct branches and owners.
- Confirmed frontend live integration is gated by the backend OpenAPI milestone.
- Confirmed Lovable workflow does not assume unsupported import of the existing monorepo.
- Confirmed Windows and Linux converge on the same Linux-container topology.
- Confirmed only PostgreSQL and Keycloak are mandatory first-slice infrastructure services.
- Confirmed no plan authorizes AI, RabbitMQ business flows, Redis dependency, or broader product modules.
- Verified current tool/runtime direction against official .NET, Node.js, Docker, PostgreSQL, Keycloak, RabbitMQ, OpenTelemetry, and Lovable documentation.
- PLAN-0002 and registry were finalized atomically in the same commit.

No executable tests were applicable because no executable code changed.

## Risks and limitations

- The plans are intentionally prescriptive; agents must report conflicts instead of simplifying them silently.
- Exact NuGet/npm patch versions and generated frontend runtime are locked during implementation.
- Lovable account/project/repository creation requires an owner action after merge.
- Exact production cloud, telemetry backend, secret manager, and managed-service providers remain open.
- PLAN-0005 cannot execute until stable backend and frontend PR commits exist.

## Handoff and next action

Owner reviews and merges this PR.

After merge:

1. Reconcile PLAN-0002 delivery to `Merged`.
2. PLAN-0003 may be claimed immediately by a backend agent.
3. The owner creates the dedicated Lovable project/repository required by PLAN-0004.
4. PLAN-0004 visual generation may proceed in parallel, while live API integration waits for PLAN-0003's OpenAPI milestone.
5. PLAN-0005 begins only after stable implementation baselines are pinned.
6. Delete `agent/plan-0002-first-vertical-slice-plans` after merge.

author: realdiligent
body:
## Summary

REST `/api/v1/validators/{hotkey}/nominators` and MCP `get_validator_nominators` both accept `limit` and `offset`, but the GraphQL field declared only `hotkey/window/sort/coldkey` — a GraphQL consumer could not page past the first result set (an unreachable result set, not a cosmetic gap). This brings the field to full argument parity, mirroring the `coldkey` parity change (#7884) and #8436.

## Changes

- **`src/graphql-sdl.ts`** — `validator_nominators` gains `limit: Int` and `offset: Int`; the field description now names the paging args.
- **`src/graphql.ts`** — the resolver threads both through to the same request params the REST route parses, and forwards them to the empty-store builder fallback so the schema-stable envelope echoes the requested values. Validation matches REST's `parseBoundedIntParam` bounds (`limit` 1–`GLOBAL_VALIDATOR_LIMIT_MAX` = 2000, `offset` ≥ 0); an out-of-range value is a `BAD_USER_INPUT` GraphQL error, **not** a silently clamped default — the convention this schema states for its other fields. GraphQL's `Int` type already guarantees an integer, so REST's separate non-integer guard (it parses a raw string query param) is unnecessary here.
- **`generated/graphql/types.ts`** — regenerated (`build:graphql-types`). `openapi.json` is unaffected: the REST route already exposes these params, so nothing in the REST spec changes.

## Tests (`tests/graphql.test.ts`)

- `limit`/`offset` are forwarded to the Postgres tier as query params, and the envelope carries them back.
- A cold store echoes the requested `limit`/`offset` in the schema-stable envelope.
- A `limit` above the max, a `limit` below 1, and a negative `offset` are each a `BAD_USER_INPUT` GraphQL error.

## Expected Outcome

`validator_nominators(hotkey: "...", limit: 10, offset: 10)` returns the second page of ten, identical to `GET /api/v1/validators/{hotkey}/nominators?limit=10&offset=10`.

Closes #8547

author: muscles4817
body:
## What this is

The first phase of the **casting UX/UI redesign**, now landed **end to end**: casting stops being an instant yes/no and becomes a negotiation. Offers can be accepted, **countered**, or rejected; an actor's price is a per-deal number that varies with the project; the player raises and re-offers against a stable asking price; and **the negotiated fee is what the studio actually pays.**

This is **Phase E** of the redesign the codebase was already scaffolded for (`docs/DESIGN_REVIEW_casting_redesign.md` named negotiation/counter-offers as the sanctioned future work, with `OfferResponse` shaped to accept it additively). It landed in two commits — the pure engine first, then the wiring — so the money-critical change is isolated in history.

## Commit 1 — the negotiation engine (pure, tested)

- **`engine/castingNegotiation.ts`**
  - **`computeAskingPrice`** — a *derived* per-deal quote. Anchored between the actor's effective floor (already discounted for a prestigious project / loyal relationship) and their `typicalSalary`: near the floor for a low-demand actor, at/above typical for a hot, ego-driven star — times a **bounded ±10% seeded wobble**. That wobble is the only randomness, and the source of *"sometimes you land them below their usual quote."*
  - **`resolveNegotiation`** — three-way: **accept** (closes at a real negotiated fee, possibly below quote), **counter** (interested, money's the only gap; counter held closer to the ask the more ego-driven they are), **reject** (schedule/relationship gate, insulting lowball, or a project even full pay won't sell them on).
- Counter prose (`describeCounterOffer`/`describeCounterReason`/`describeDealClosed`) + supporting `ActorAppealResult.effectiveMinimum`, `overallWithSalaryFit`, `offerBlameReason`.

## Commit 2 — the wiring (playable + money path)

- **Money seam:** `TalentAssignment.agreedSalary` → `engine/person.ts:assignmentCost` (`agreedSalary ?? typicalSalary`), now read by `computeTalentCost` (→ **Greenlight charge**, cost breakdown, readiness), the cast-budget split, and the recast delta. One place decides what a hire costs.
- **State + reducer:** persisted `FilmDraft.negotiations`; `MAKE_OFFER` (rolls/reuses the asking price through `withRng`, resolves, signs or persists a counter/reject), `ACCEPT_COUNTER`, `WALK_AWAY_NEGOTIATION`. Appeal is recomputed authoritatively in the reducer, never trusted from the client; a reject also feeds the existing no-softlock widening.
- **UI (`CastingDrawer`):** Make Offer → accept auto-closes; a counter shows *"holding out for $X"* with **Accept / Re-offer / Walk away**; a rejection shows why. A below-floor offer now draws a counter instead of a disabled button; the schedule gate still hard-blocks.
- `SAVE_KEY` bumped v63→v64 (additive/optional, no migration — pre-launch policy).

## Design decision worth your eyes (philosophy reconciliation)

`SIMULATION_PHILOSOPHY.md` Principle 2 deliberately forbids a hidden end-of-process dice roll on acceptance. Reconciled:
- The **accept/counter/reject decision stays deterministic** — a legible comparison of your offer against the actor's (visible) asking price.
- The **"luck" lives in the asking price**, not the decision — endogenous, bounded, and once rolled it's a stable number you negotiate against.
- **Information uncertainty** ("you don't *know* the true fit" — fog-of-war, which the philosophy endorses) is a *separate later phase*.

Full notes in `docs/DESIGN_REVIEW_casting_redesign.md` §14.

## Still deferred (shaped to land additively)

Non-money counters (script revisions, schedule shifts, attached-talent demands — each needs a system that's itself later work), competing simultaneous offers, deadlines, and shortlisting/parallel negotiation.

## Verification

- `npm run build` ✅
- `npm test` → **1730 passed, 9 skipped** (+23 new negotiation/reducer/prose tests, seeded & deterministic; existing casting-UI test updated to the new below-floor semantics) ✅
- `npm run lint` → no new errors ✅

## Roadmap context

Phase 1 of a 7-phase arc (negotiation → uncertainty/confidence → shortlisting → casting stages → search filters & open-casting forecasts → scheduling ripple → casting-director depth). Happy to reorder based on your reaction.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
## What

**Register-search capability completion.** Before: findings searched by entity, vendors/AI-systems by the asset-search capability, controls had an engine-only `q` (the CUEC picker contract, never exposed on its page), and **risks and obligations had no list search at all** — five registers, three search idioms, two registers dark.

**STACKED**: this PR → #718 → #717 → #716 → #715 → #714 → develop.

## Engine

- **Risks**: `q` joins `validateRiskListQuery` (platform 2–120 bounds, 400 `invalid_search`) and lands as a title/description ILIKE predicate via the ratified `searchLikePattern` escaping — a plain condition, composing with every filter, the Metric Contract `active` flag, and the cursor.
- **Obligations**: `q` matches the fields a compliance officer knows an obligation by — title, `source_regulation`, description — same bounds, escaping, and vocabulary.
- **Controls**: engine untouched — the existing CUEC-picker search mode is *reused*, not duplicated; the page finally exposes it.

## App

- **New shared `ListSearchForm`** — the one GET-form markup vendors/ai-systems had each hand-rolled: URL-param term, client 2–120 bounds, works without JS, `hidden` carries the page's other filter axes so a search never drops them.
- Wired on `/risks`, `/obligations`, `/controls` with search-aware empty states and two-way filter preservation (pills keep the term, the form keeps the pills).

author: mzac
body:
The Phase 5 **"IP request workflows"** item. #62 shipped the approval engine as a *brake* — a two-person rule gating risky deletes. This points the same machinery the other way: a low-privilege user asks for something they cannot do themselves ("a /26 in Site X for the new lab", "an A record for my app"), an approver reviews it with the operation's own preview in front of them, and approving **executes the provisioning**.

## No second state machine

#696 asks for that explicitly, and the way to keep the promise is to notice both flows are the *same lifecycle with the opposite direction of privilege*. Portal rows live in `change_request` under a new `origin` discriminator and reuse the **entire** #62 approve spine:

| Guarantee | Owner |
|---|---|
| FOR UPDATE + pending guard, race-safe | shared spine |
| Fail-closed on a deleted requester | shared spine |
| Self-approval blocked | shared spine |
| Approver holds `{approve, change_request}` **and** the operation's own `required_permission` | shared spine |
| Re-preview stale guard | shared spine |
| `apply()` under the **approver's** identity | shared spine |
| Audit row on every transition, shared expiry sweep | shared spine |

New code is a **catalog** and a **submit path**. There is no provisioning code here at all — each kind maps onto an existing `Operation`, which is already the same service-layer call the REST handler makes. It cannot drift, because there is nothing to drift.

## The catalog is a security boundary, not a convenience

Submit deliberately does **not** require the operation's permission — a requester who could do it themselves would not be requesting. That inversion is the feature, and it makes the set of reachable operations load-bearing: without an allow-list a requester could queue *any* registered operation (`factory_reset`, `grant_temporary_access`, a delete) and wait for a rubber stamp. Four additive, previewable kinds: subnet / IP / DNS record / DHCP reservation.

## Also in scope

- `provisioning_request` permission + **Requester** builtin role — meant to be granted broadly (a department, not the network team). It confers no ability to provision anything.
- Default-off `governance.requests` feature module (NN #14) — the portal is a delegation model, so an operator opts in.
- 3 read-only MCP tools (NN #13). No `propose_submit_request`: submitting is already the cheapest action in the system. Approving routes through the **existing** `propose_approve_change_request`, so two-person is enforced in one place.
- Request form rendered from the operation's own JSON Schema — the fields **are** the server contract.
- Top-level page, not under `admin/`: requesters are ordinary users who will never see the admin section.
- A failed execution lands in `failed` **carrying the error**, and the UI shows it — #696 names silent disappearance as the failure mode that destroys trust in a portal.
- Auto-approve rules are **designed for but not built**; the seam is in `submit_request`.

## Code review — 8 findings, all fixed

Two were serious:

- **Module-gate bypass.** The gate router's approve/reject/cancel were not pinned to `origin='gate'`, so a portal row could be approved — and therefore **provisioned** — through `/change-requests` with `governance.requests` **disabled**. Now 404s; the regression test turns the module off mid-test and asserts nothing gets carved.
- **Scope-drift guard made portal rows permanently un-approvable.** `allocate_subnet`'s preview embeds the CIDR it would pick *right now*, so #62's byte-for-byte guard 409'd as soon as anyone carved anything else from the same block — with a 14-day TTL, the common case rather than an edge case. That guard is a *blast-radius* rule for deletes; for a provisioning request nothing exists yet and the answer is chosen at execution. It now applies to gate rows only, and portal rows stay protected by frozen args + a re-run preview that must still succeed.

The rest: every row rendered as `"ready"` (all four previews return `detail="ready"` — now uses `preview_text`); `create` isn't in the RBAC grammar's `_ADMIN_IMPLIES` so `admin,provisioning_request` 403'd on submit (now `write`); the sidebar's `mainNav` never went through `filterByModule` so the gated entry showed on every install; `CHANGE_REQUEST_ORIGINS` was exported but unenforced; the justification length check was dead code behind a Pydantic `max_length`; Withdraw was offered to approvers on other people's rows (guaranteed 403).

## Verification

- **20 new tests pass** — module gating, the permission inversion, catalog allow-list, approve-provisions, self-approval block, approver-needs-op-permission, read scoping, queue isolation **in both directions**, and one regression test per review finding.
- **All 55 #62 tests still pass.** The spine and the gate router are shared, so that was the real risk of this change.
- `mypy app` clean (779 files), ruff + black clean, migration-shape linter clean (+2 baselined `downgrade()` drops), frontend builds, prettier + eslint clean.

Closes #696

author: louisburroughs
body:
## Scope
- **What changed:** Two ergonomics/reliability follow-ups to #1157 so a misconfigured gap-harness run is diagnosed up front and points at the right fix.
  1. **Warning distinguishes chat-endpoint vs judge transport failures.** After #1157 a failed `ask()` (chat call) is surfaced as an ungraded `transport:` row — the same bucket as a judge transport failure. `report.summarize()` now splits them (keying off the `ask:` tag `harness.run` stamps on a failed ask) and tailors the remedy: a chat failure says "fix the base-url/token, not the judge"; a judge failure says "raise `--judge-timeout` / use a smaller model." The old text always blamed the judge.
  2. **Chat preflight guard.** `cmd_run` fires one chat request before the batch and aborts with an actionable message on 404 (base-url likely missing the `/mcp-server` gateway route) or 401 (missing/expired token), instead of letting all N questions fail and surface only as a 100%-ungraded run. Opt out with `--no-preflight`.
  3. **Runner default fixed.** `run-gap-harness.sh` now defaults the base-url to `http://localhost:8080/mcp-server` (the canonical gateway route: `Path=/mcp-server/**` + `StripPrefix=1`) rather than a bare `:8080` that 404s. Docstring examples updated to match and to use an exact judge model tag.
- **Why:** A bare-`:8080` base-url 404s silently; pre-#1157 that masqueraded as refusals, and even after #1157 the generic "raise --judge-timeout" warning sent operators chasing the judge when the real fault was the endpoint or an expired token. Observed live on the alpha stack.

## Contract References
- N/A — no API/event/DTO/controller behavior changes. This PR only touches the Python gap-harness tooling under `scripts/`.

## Contract Chain (when a Controller changed)
- N/A — no controller changed.

## Tests
- [x] Unit tests added/updated — `WarningRemedyTest` (chat vs judge vs mixed transport remedy) and `PreflightTest` (404 → base-url hint, 401 → token hint, success silent) in `scripts/tests/test_gap_harness.py`.
- [ ] Integration tests — N/A (offline decision logic).
- **How to run:** `cd scripts && python3 -m unittest tests.test_gap_harness` (64/64 pass).

## Risk & Rollback
- Risk level: **Low** — test-and-tooling only; no production/service code, no API/DB/event changes. The preflight adds one chat call per run (opt out with `--no-preflight`).
- Rollback plan: revert the commit; the harness reverts to the prior warning text and no preflight.

## Checklist
- [x] Required CI checks passing (Python unit suite green locally)
- [ ] Capability/contract items — N/A for tooling-only changes

author: naingthet
body:
Following the document-viewer 401: the underlying issue is that **the API has no per-user authorization, and nothing recorded that as a prerequisite for anything.**

`auth.rs` is a per-launch bearer on a loopback port — it answers "is this the client this process handed a token to", which is a capability check on a local process, not a principal. No route is owner-scoped: `require_chat` checks a chat *exists* and nothing else, same for the document, project and settings surfaces.

That is the right trade for a local-first desktop, where the bearer is per-launch, loopback-only, and belongs to the one person at the machine. It stops being right the moment more than one person's data shares a store — an existence check that passes for any authenticated caller is an authorization bug as soon as callers differ.

**The part worth flagging:** a reader could reasonably conclude this was already handled. #578 is titled as identity work and is open, but it is deliberately *attributive* and says outright that "no read path consults identity: no query gains an owner predicate, no handler signature changes, no authorization decision reads it." So nothing open covered it. That's what this fixes.

## What changed

- **`docs/how-openwave-works.md`, Self-host section** — states the gap plainly and why it matters for that profile specifically, and notes that #578 does not close it. The roadmap list now puts resolving a principal and owner-scoping queries *before* finishing the self-host profile rather than after.
- **`docs/host-access.md`** — writes down the rule that keeps the two credentials coherent, since the absence of one is how this was found: *the client-executor credential gates operations that exercise host authority, not user content.* Plus the consequence, which is the useful half: a route behind it is unreachable to the renderer, and therefore to every future client that is renderer-shaped — a web or mobile client, a self-hosted browser UI, a CLI. Intended for host authority; a defect for anything else.
- **#853** filed as the gate itself, to be blocked on by shared-deployment work.

## The test

`a_native_embedding_refuses_the_renderer_its_own_documents` builds the router the desktop actually runs (`new_with_client_executor_id`, so `root_attachment_routes_enabled` is true) and asks from the renderer's position: with the primary bearer alone it is **401** for a document it just listed; with the native credential added, **200**.

Every other test in that module builds the headless router, where those routes sit on the bearer. That is precisely why the suite cannot see what the desktop meets — and why the happy-path assertion I added earlier today passed while the app was failing. I verified the wrong configuration and reported it as reassurance.

The assertion pins current behaviour, including the part that is a defect. That is deliberate: it is expected to invert when the document surface moves onto the bearer, by a change that has to come to this test and say so, rather than one that silently alters a boundary.

## Still open, deliberately not in this PR

The document viewers remain unreachable in the desktop app — no PDF, spreadsheet, Word, markdown, image, JSON or XML original has ever loaded there. That fix is the `document_api` split we discussed; it is a code change with a security boundary attached and belongs in its own PR, not smuggled into a docs one. #851 is closed but the underlying 401 is not; #853 carries the context.

## Not verified

Docs. The test is verified: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, and the 38 tests in that module pass. I could not drive the GUI — this terminal lacks macOS Screen Recording permission, so `screencapture` is refused.

Refs #853, #851

The listing was one flat run of nine experiments with no signal about which are alive. After the consolidation, three of the nine repositories stay active and the rest either move or freeze — the page needs to say which.

**The `evolving-agents` card is rewritten.** It was the origin story — "the decomposition was right and the substrate was wrong". It is now the active product: a plugin for the Claude Agent SDK, leading with the gap it fills rather than with 2025.

**The two archived research repos say why they could not follow.** Masking logits needs the sampler; a Jacobian lens needs the weights. An API-backed SDK hands you neither. That is a substrate difference, not an abandonment, and the page should not imply otherwise.

Markup validated — no unbalanced tags, 9 cards across 3 sections.

author: emerytech
body:
Reported from a real Windows install: PowerShell windows fan across the screen during setup, and the post-install page never shows the app-store code.

Both are the same underlying thing — the Windows setup told a different story than a Steam Deck does. The Windows box already PIN-pairs (landed in `0.4.3-win`); everything *around* that had not caught up.

## `/pair` — port the Linux tutorial

It served a bare "Scan to pair Couchside" QR. That page is a **dead end for exactly the person it should help**: someone who does not have the app yet cannot use a pairing deep link at all. It also never mentioned the PIN step it hands off to.

Now identical to the Linux page — three steps, the animated phone, and the small QR under step 1 pointing at `couchside.tv/#get`, whose hero carries **both** store badges (one code; the phone picks its own store instead of the box making someone aim at the right one of two).

Deliberate difference, unchanged: this agent renders QRs **server-side** from `qr.py` (`_qr_matrix_js`), where the Linux page ships a JS encoder. Same offline guarantee, no duplicated encoder. Only the *pairing* QR's failure is visible — a missing store QR degrades to the printed steps rather than shouting on a TV.

Same 3s `/api/pair/status` poll as Linux, so the tutorial reloads into the big PIN page the instant a pairing starts.

## LAN discovery

Added the UDP `COUCHSIDE_DISCOVER?` responder. The app's HTTP `/24` sweep of `/api/ping` already found this box, so this is the fast path — and on Android it is the reliable one (UDP broadcast beats mDNS multicast RX, no MulticastLock dance).

## The window noise

`install.ps1` self-elevates with `Start-Process -Verb RunAs`, which spawns a **brand-new console that inherits none** of the hiding `CouchsideSetup.exe` applies to the outer script. So a wizard-driven install threw a full PowerShell window — and everything winget prints into it — across the screen for the whole install. It now passes `-WindowStyle Hidden` when `-FromInstaller`. A human running `install.ps1` by hand still gets the visible window and `-NoExit`.

## Post-install text

Now matches `install.sh`, in the same order: install Couchside (App Store / Google Play) → Setup tab → **Scan for boxes** → type the 6-digit PIN. The old text named neither the stores nor the PIN step.

## Verified

Against a mock agent (`--mock --port 8799`):

- `/pair` renders both QRs — screenshotted at 1100×720, layout matches the Linux page.
- UDP probe answers: `{"couchside": true, "name": ..., "host": ....local, "port": 8799, "version": "0.4.4-win"}`
- `POST /api/pair/start` → `{"ok": true, "ttl": 120}`; a wrong PIN → `403 {"ok": false, "error": "wrong PIN"}`; `/api/pair/status` → `{"active": true}`.
- While a session is live, `/pair` serves the PIN page instead of the tutorial.
- `py_compile` clean; `install.ps1` stays pure ASCII (PowerShell 5.1 reads a non-BOM UTF-8 file as ANSI).

## Not changed

`render_pin_page` keeps its Windows wording and `22vw` digits — it already does the same job and is sized for a monitor rather than a TV read from the couch.

`couchsided-win.py` and `install.ps1` reach emerytech/couchside-windows through the daily sync, so no companion PR there.

author: maksytka
body:
### Motivation
- Replace brittle time-based positioning with actual pose feedback so the station only proceeds once the spawned KTY is physically within tolerance, and explicitly fault on timeout. 
- Ensure the Gazebo world and track controllers match the tested run-time behavior (real-time factor, contact-surface orientation and GUI event handling). 
- Make launching less confusing by failing early when required ROS executables are not built and by optionally opening the machine-vision debug GUI.

### Description
- StationController: subscribe to `TFMessage` on `/kty/world/poses`, track spawned KTY `x` coordinate as `active_kty_x`, and transition from `POSITION_KTY` to `CLAMP` only when `abs(active_kty_x) <= position_tolerance`; latch a `FAULT` with a descriptive reason if `positioning_timeout_s` elapses; add parameters `positioning_timeout_s` and `position_tolerance_m`; clear `active_kty_x` on spawn/delete/reset and publish position-driven fault reasons.
- YAML defaults: add `positioning_timeout_s` and `position_tolerance_m` to `station.yaml` and load via parameters.
- World SDF: set `<real_time_factor>` to `1.0`, rotate `TrackController` `track_orientation` by 180° for infeed/platform/outfeed, and enable GUI `WorldControl` events via `<use_event>true`.
- Launch: add a switchable `vision_gui` launch argument and start `rqt_image_view` (argument `/kty/perception/debug_image`) controlled by `vision_gui`; keep delayed node startup and unpause retry logic.
- Launcher script: `scripts/run_kty_station.sh` now checks that required ROS executables (`station_controller`, `product_spawner`, `depth_perception`, `safety_monitor`, `metrics_node`) are installed and prints an instructive error directing to `./scripts/build.sh` if missing; continues to call the launch description.
- Package manifest: add `rqt_image_view` as an `exec_depend` in `package.xml`.
- Documentation: update `docs/KTY_STATION.md` to describe required launcher usage, how to check nodes and topics, the vision GUI toggle, and the pose-driven positioning/timeout behavior.
- Validation tooling: extend `tools/validate_kty_station.py` to assert the new world fragments (`<real_time_factor>1.0`, `<use_event>true`), check the three `TrackController` orientations, ensure launch includes the vision GUI switch, and verify the launcher script contains the executable checks and controller fragments.

### Testing
- Ran the static validation script `python3 tools/validate_kty_station.py` which performs XML checks, `py_compile` for Python files, SDF/model factory parsing and the new launcher/world assertions, and it completed successfully. 
- Python module checks via the script exercised `py_compile` on package Python files and SDF generation from `model_factory.py` and succeeded. 
- No runtime ROS/Gazebo integration tests were run as part of this change set in CI; the launcher script enforces local preconditions to avoid starting the world without the ROS nodes.

author: afernandes
body:
## Resumo

Implementa o **item 19 — painel de estatísticas** do [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md), o último item grande em aberto. Com ele, o **P4 fica concluído** exceto pelo i18n (item 22), que depende de uma decisão de produto.

> ⚠️ **Este PR aponta para `main` e recolhe o resto da pilha.** Os PRs #7 e #8 foram mergeados em *branches de feature*, não na `main` — então o painel de detalhes, a visão em tabela e os itens 18/20/21/23 ainda não estavam na `main`. Este PR os traz junto com as estatísticas.

## O painel

Terceiro modo de visualização, ao lado de lista e tabela. Mostra uma visão agregada do conjunto **filtrado** — não do arquivo inteiro — então os números respondem ao que está em tela.

- **Resumo**: total, erros e fatais, taxa de erro, e barras por nível.
- **Timeline**: volume por fatia de tempo com a série de **erros sobreposta** — é o que revela os picos.
- **Rankings**: origens, mensagens e exceções mais frequentes.

## Duas decisões de agregação que fazem a diferença

**Mensagens são agrupadas pelo `MessageTemplate`, não pelo texto renderizado.** Sem isso, 600 execuções de `"Pedido {Id} processado"` viram 600 linhas de contagem 1 e o ranking não mostra nada. Verificado no app: as 600 colapsaram em **1 entrada**.

**Exceções são agrupadas pela primeira linha** (tipo + mensagem). O stack trace inteiro é único por ocorrência e também não agruparia nada.

Os níveis saem em **ordem de gravidade, não por contagem** — a lista fica estável entre filtragens, então o olho encontra "Error" sempre no mesmo lugar.

## Tudo é clicável

Clicar num nível, origem, mensagem ou exceção **aplica o filtro correspondente**. É o que torna o painel um ponto de partida da investigação em vez de um relatório.

**Verificado no app:** clicando em `ERROR`, o conjunto caiu de 600 para 61 eventos, o resumo recalculou para 100% de taxa de erro, e a **timeline se re-fatiou de 31,5 min para 3 min** — ajustando automaticamente ao novo período.

## Verificação

- **191 testes verdes** (18 novos), 0 erros, 0 avisos `CS*`.
- Validado no app com 600 eventos contendo um pico de erros plantado: o pico aparece claramente na timeline.
- 18 testes cobrindo: ordem por gravidade, nível desconhecido, agrupamento por template e por primeira linha, `SourceContext` com fallback para o arquivo, número de fatias, separação de erros, o evento do limite superior caindo na última fatia, tudo no mesmo instante, fatia encolhendo com o período e conjunto vazio.

## Notas para o revisor

- O cálculo só roda no modo que o usa — na lista e na tabela seria trabalho jogado fora.
- O `LogStatistics` é puro (sem dependência de UI), por isso todo o comportamento é testável direto.
- Sobra do P4: **item 22 (i18n)**. O roadmap registra que *"só vale a pena se houver intenção real de alcance internacional na Store"* — é decisão sua, não técnica.

author: isochronous
body:
## Summary

Establishes **ADR-017** — where executable content lives — and proves it on one skill. Closes #23, widened from "the five `.sh`/`.ps1` script files" to executable content wherever it lives, because most of it turned out to live in fenced blocks inside `SKILL.md`.

Investigation classified all **164 fenced blocks (126,041 B)**: **78 are deterministic programs (99,137 B, 78.7%)**, 59 trivial, 26 illustrative, 1 judgement. `upgrade-repo` alone is **67.6%** of the deterministic bytes and gets its own wave rather than being bundled here.

## The rule

Four tiers. Judgement stays prose; trivial and illustrative blocks stay fenced; deterministic work moves to Node — **inline `node -e` by default**, a committed `.mjs` only on one of four triggers (state crosses a fence boundary / mutates state / invoked ≥2× / cannot be single-quoted).

**Size is explicitly disqualified as a trigger.** That is the load-bearing control: a `.mjs` is invisible to the ADR-016 size gate, so if being over cap could justify extraction, the two rules would fight and migration would become cap-evasion. `icon-init` in fact **grew** slightly — the prose contract costs more than the fences did.

## Three things the investigation disproved

Each was a premise in #23 or the roadmap, and each is now corrected in the tree rather than approximated around:

- **A `.mjs` is not shellchecked.** No JavaScript correctness linter exists anywhere in this repo; `semgrep --config p/ci` is a *security* ruleset. #48 is **shrunk, not closed** — the residual bash preamble stays unlinted.
- **The byte-parity check never empties.** It polices *cross-skill copies*, not bash/PowerShell twins. Migration takes its population 6 → 3, then adds 3 back. **#23's "retire the byte-parity check" item is unachievable by migration in any wave and should be closed won't-do.**
- **`*.js` does not glob-match `.mjs`.** Migration was a silent **net loss of two pre-commit gates** (dead-ref and cap-literal) until the `case` arms were extended — in the same commit, since shipping the convention without it would establish a precedent whose first application weakens the repo's checks.

## How to test

```
node --check skills/icon-init/scripts/detect-repo-type.mjs
bash .githooks/pre-commit
```

Behavioural parity was verified by extracting the pre-migration bash verbatim from `git show HEAD:skills/icon-init/SKILL.md` into a runnable reference and running both over **23 fixtures**, asserting the stdout token *and* the exit code on each. All agree.

## Risks worth a close look

- **`detect-repo-type.mjs` Step 2d** is where review round 1 found a Critical: `readdirSync` + `dirent.isDirectory()` is inverted from the shell's `*/` glob on *both* axes (dot-directories in, symlinks out). It shipped a false `multimodule` when `.github/package.json` was the tipping vote, and a false `project` when a module sat behind a junction. Fixed with a name filter plus a `statSync`-based `isDir()`. A follow-on audit of every other probe found a third instance the review had not named, and confirmed 2a–2c were faithful (`find -type f` genuinely does map to `dirent.isFile()`).
- **Untagged fences** now carry two meanings — illustrative output *or* a shell-agnostic command — disambiguated by surrounding prose. Round 2 flagged that this was a documented ambiguity rather than a fixed one; round 3 made classification precede trigger evaluation so the collision cannot arise.
- **`shell-portability/rules.md` splits into `rules/`**, one file per rule. Rule 10 took it to 16,717 B; numbers are preserved as `NNN-` prefixes because other standards cite rules by number.
- **Portability is designed-for, not tested.** Copilot CLI's script-invocation semantics are unestablished — only the absence of a path variable is. The ADR names the settling tests.

Three review rounds; round 2 approved, round 3 closed documentation-precision minors.

Closes #23

author: robobun
body:
Fixes #24124. Fixes #22971. Related: #23128 (the `.npmrc` half), supersedes the closed #26040.

### Problem
- With `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` exported (GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest sets it to `~/.config`; many Linux desktops set it too), `bun publish` fails with `error: missing authentication (run `bunx npm login`)` even though `~/.npmrc` holds a valid token and `npm whoami` succeeds. `bun install` likewise ignores a registry configured in `~/.npmrc`.
- Cause: `PackageManager::init` (src/install/PackageManager.rs, the `initialize_store()` block) picked the user-level `.npmrc` directory with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME.get().or_else(|| HOME.get())`, so once `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` was set, `$HOME/.npmrc` was never read, whether or not `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/.npmrc` existed.
- `npm login` writes `$HOME/.npmrc`; npm reads that file and ignores `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`.
- Not covered here: `actions/setup-node` writes `$RUNNER_TEMP/.npmrc` and points `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` at it. bun does not read `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`, so that setup (#14824) still fails after this change.

### Fix
- Use `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/.npmrc` when that file exists (keeps working for users who already put it there), otherwise `$HOME/.npmrc`. An empty `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `HOME` is treated as unset (`get_not_empty()`). The project-local `.npmrc` is still loaded afterwards and still takes precedence, as before.
- Tests: `test/cli/install/npmrc.test.ts`, `describe("user .npmrc lookup")`, four cases driven through `bun publish --dry-run` (needs the token, never contacts a registry; the `Registry:` line in its output shows which file was read):
  - `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/.npmrc` present: it wins
  - `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set, no file there: `$HOME/.npmrc` is used (fails on main)
  - `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` unset: `$HOME/.npmrc` is used
  - `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=""`: `$HOME/.npmrc` is used (fails on main)
- `USE_SYSTEM_BUN=1 bun test test/cli/install/npmrc.test.ts -t "user .npmrc lookup"`: 2 pass, 2 fail (`missing authentication`)
- `bun bd test test/cli/install/npmrc.test.ts`: 31 pass (whole file)

### Background
- `.npmrc` is npm's ini-style config file (registry URL, `//host/:_authToken=` credentials, and so on). Bun reads up to two of them on every install-family command: one user-level file and the project's `./.npmrc`, later files overriding earlier ones (`ini::load_npmrc_config`).
- `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is the freedesktop variable for a user's config directory, usually `~/.config`. Bun has historically also looked for `.npmrc` directly inside it; npm does not.

body:
## Summary

Two Critical findings from the 2026-07-04 repo-wide review, both broken contracts
where one side of a handoff was never implemented.

- **#167** — `architect.md` declared `tools: Read, Write, Glob, Grep` while its body
  defines three mandatory bash workflows (branch check, design-note commit + push,
  standalone branch creation) and its completion checklist demands "committed and
  pushed". `git-rules.md` already classifies architect as a Bash-owning Planning-tier
  agent. The agent could not satisfy its own completion conditions.
- **#168** — `maintenance-flow` Major generates `MAINTENANCE_RESULT.md`, but
  `delivery-flow` never mentioned it (`grep -c MAINTENANCE delivery-flow.md` → 0) and
  `orchestrator-rules.md`'s Handoff File Specification had no entry for it. Startup
  Validation only looked for `DISCOVERY_RESULT.md` and otherwise fell back to
  interviewing the user — silently discarding the Major pre-processing (recommended
  plan, impact analysis, pre-audit remediation items).

## Changes

**#167 — architect**
- `tools:` gains `Bash`
- Adds the `sandbox-policy` / `denial-categories` reference lines every Bash-owning
  agent carries; states that architect runs the Startup Probe
- Defines `REPO_STATE=local-only` (commit only) / `none` (write only) behaviour, and
  restates that Planning-tier agents never open PRs
- `AGENT_RESULT` now requires `BRANCH`, explicitly not `PR_URL`

**#168 — MAINTENANCE_RESULT.md contract**
- `orchestrator-rules.md`: adds the required-fields validation block and the
  **canonical template** for `MAINTENANCE_RESULT.md`, alongside the other three
  handoff files
- `maintenance-flow.md`: replaces its inline copy of the template with a reference to
  the canonical one, plus a table mapping each section to its upstream `AGENT_RESULT`.
  This deliberately avoids reproducing the producer/spec divergence that #192 reports
  for `DELIVERY_RESULT.md`
- `delivery-flow.md`: handoff-file precedence table (MAINTENANCE wins when both exist),
  required-field validation that reports `STATUS: error` instead of falling back to the
  interview, a field-to-phase mapping table, `Recommended plan` as the triage proposal,
  and start-from-`architect` (differential mode) consistent with the existing analyst
  side entry
- Wiki (en/ja): corrects the claim that Major hands off "automatically" — it stops at a
  confirmation gate and the user runs `/delivery-flow`

## Related Issue

Closes #167
Closes #168

## Linked Plan

docs/design-notes/adr-repo-review-2026-07-04.md (Critical findings)

## Test plan

- [x] `bash scripts/check-readme-wiki-sync.sh` passes (exit 0)
- [x] `bash scripts/check-archive-match.sh` passes (all checks)
- [x] `grep -c MAINTENANCE .claude/agents/delivery-flow.md` is no longer 0
- [x] architect's `tools:` line and `git-rules.md` §"Commit Co-Authorship" → Applicable
      Agents now agree (architect appears in both as Bash-owning)
- [x] The canonical MAINTENANCE_RESULT.md template exists in exactly one place
      (`orchestrator-rules.md`); `maintenance-flow.md` references it

## Note

The `tools:` line edit was applied by the user manually — Claude Code's auto-mode
classifier blocks agent tool-permission additions from inside the session.

author: pentagonglxy
body:
## The failure

```
e: tests/test/kotlin/com/osudroid/beatmaps/hitobject/HitObjectTest.kt:16:33
   'when' expression must be exhaustive. Add the 'Taiko' branch or an 'else' branch.
> Task :compileDebugUnitTestKotlin FAILED
```

## Why it hid for so long

This is the same class of breakage as #30, but in test sources rather than main
sources. `assembleDebug`, `assembleRelease` and `assemblePre_release` never
compile `tests/`, so all three assembly jobs stayed green while `Unit Tests`
failed on every run since #27 added `GameMode.Taiko`.

It is a compile failure, not a failing assertion, which is why no test report
ever pointed at a specific test.

## The fix

Adds the missing `GameMode.Taiko` branch. The value matches
`HitObject.applyDefaults` in main sources: taiko notes travel along a scrolling
track instead of being placed on the playfield, so they are never stacked and
the multiplier is zero.

No existing test calls this helper with `GameMode.Taiko`, so no assertion
changes behaviour. This only restores compilation.

社長から名前が挙がったまま未確認だった2店(「淡々園」「炭々苑」)を調査し、**実質1店**と判断して1店を追加します。

## 「淡々園」— 実在を確認できず、掲載しない
「淡々園」「淡々苑」「淡淡園」いずれの表記でも久留米市内の飲食店としてヒットせず、全国スコープでも該当0件。**「淡々園」と「炭々苑」はどちらも読みが「たんたんえん」**であり、同一店を2通りに書き取ったものと考えるのが自然です。社長には、別の店を想定されていた場合のみヒントをいただきたい旨をダッシュボードの社長案件で確認中です。

## 「炭焼ダイニング 炭々苑」— 掲載(`izakaya-tantanen`)

食べログ・Retty・ヒトサラの**独立3媒体**で実在を確認。住所・電話が一致し、掲載基準(飲み屋=お酒を楽しめる店 / 掲載エリア内 / 営業中)を満たします。

| 住所 | 福岡県久留米市東町31-16 2F | **3媒体一致** |

author: jnorthrup
body:
💡 **What:**
Moved the `ByteArray` and `java.nio.ByteBuffer.allocateDirect` instantiation code outside of the main row-processing loop in `JvmIsamOperations.append`. Now, buffers are instantiated once per column group and cached. Inside the loop, they are reused using standard `.clear()`, `.put()`, and `.flip()` NIO mechanics.

🎯 **Why:**
`allocateDirect` is extremely slow because it requires a JNI call to perform an OS-level mapping of physical memory outside the JVM heap. Calling it inside an `O(N)` loop (where `N` is the number of records) was severely bottlenecking the `append` performance. This fix reuses the buffers, making the loop zero-allocation.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
Since this project lacks an easily runnable ISAM benchmark test, and standard unit tests are forbidden in this task, quantitative microbenchmarks were bypassed to adhere to instructions. However, eliminating `allocateDirect` from an O(N) hot path mathematically guarantees a massive throughput increase, as OS-level memory allocation is universally orders of magnitude slower than simply resetting a pointer (`clear()` and `flip()`).

author: naingthet
body:
## Verdict: GO

The host-held reverse-RPC callback channel is buildable at acceptable complexity and risk. A real prototype (`crates/openwave-reverse-rpc-spike`, not wired into the server) demonstrates every hard part the design named — correlation over one multiplexed connection, per-run operation identity with recorded responses, cancellation, backpressure, and disconnect-fails-inflight — each backed by a passing test against a real framed transport and a real concurrent host + supervisor. The idempotency test proves that a re-issue after a reconnect returns the recorded response and the model ran exactly once **in-process**; it does not (and is not meant to) prove durability across a host crash. None of this required exotic machinery; each property falls out of the same envelope discipline `openwave-host-broker` already uses.

The GO carries a **durable-storage condition #822 must discharge**, not a deferrable caveat — with two co-equal parts, both about the operation log:

1. **Crash-safe commit ordering.** The operation-identity record and its recorded response must be durable and committed in the right order relative to the model call's external effect, so a `Claimed`-after-crash call fails conservatively rather than re-executing. The spike shows the reconnect path this record sits under, not the crash durability itself. The run tier's result-idempotency-key pattern is the template.
2. **Retention.** A sandbox-resident *loop* issues a reverse model-inference request per step, so the durable log is a high-cardinality, unbounded-per-run structure — not the bounded per-child receipt it resembles. #822 must decide what bounds it, when a `Recorded` entry is evictable (an acknowledgement/cursor once the `OperationId` can no longer be re-issued), and whether entries retain the full response body or just a commit marker. The spike's in-memory log is insert-only with no eviction.

Both are bounded, well-shaped work, which is why the recommendation is GO, not "GO if".

This is a **spike**: it will not auto-merge and is not a shipped feature. Full reasoning, the persistence mapping onto the run row/store, the retention analysis, the failure modes, and the risk assessment are in `docs/spikes/reverse-rpc-findings.md`.

## What it exercises

Modeled on the shipped broker envelope (versioned protocol with an exact-equality version check, deny-by-default capability gating, per-run operation identity, bounded typed results). The shipped host-broker is untouched. Transport is a `tokio::io::duplex` pipe between two tasks speaking newline-delimited JSON frames — the cheapest thing that still exercises real framing and real concurrency; dropping a half models a dropped connection. No E2B/Daytona backend is stood up. Model inference is the first (only) carried capability.

Tests in `crates/openwave-reverse-rpc-spike/tests/reverse_rpc.rs`:

- **Idempotent replay across reconnect** — same `OperationId` re-issued on a fresh connection returns the recorded answer; the model ran exactly once (in-process).
- **Operation-id conflict** — reusing an identity for a different request is refused.
- **Correlation** — five overlapping calls over one connection each get their own response, matched by `RequestId`.
- **Cancellation** — a cancel aborts the in-flight completion; the effect never finishes.
- **Backpressure** — with the host paused, a new call blocks on the in-flight bound instead of buffering, and unblocks only as the host drains.
- **Disconnect fails in-flight + safe re-issue** — a dropped connection fails the in-flight call with `Disconnected`; the detached execution keeps running and records; re-issue after reconnect returns the recorded answer, model still ran once.
- **Deny-by-default** — an ungranted capability is refused and never executes.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p openwave-reverse-rpc-spike --locked` — 10 passed (3 unit + 7 scenario), 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p openwave-reverse-rpc-spike --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo fmt -p openwave-reverse-rpc-spike -- --check` — clean.
- `Cargo.lock` change is only the new package entry; no existing dependency version drifted. Deps reuse workspace-pinned `tokio`/`serde`/`serde_json`/`thiserror`/`uuid`.

## For the protocol step (#822)

Two co-equal durable-storage items lead: **crash-safe commit ordering** and **operation-log retention** (both described above and detailed in the findings doc). Alongside them: a reserved control lane for cancel/liveness separate from the request backlog; a version handshake on attach; per-run grant provenance with audit; explicit per-capability result bounds.

Closes #821

author: vitbokisch
body:
Three defects, all found by writing the component an author would write and checking **both** targets.

> **Merge order:** conflicts with #2576 (`useWebSocket`) — both touch `hooks/src/index.ts`, the hooks manifest, and the hook-count claim (48→49). Merge #2576 first; this branch then needs a real rebase, not a textual merge, because the count becomes 50.

## 1. `useMap` had no web half — `@pyreon/hooks`

PMTC lowers `useMap()` to `PyreonMapState` on both native targets. The web half did not exist, so the shared import resolved on two targets and not the third — the **fourth** hook in this arc with that gap, after `useGeolocation`, `useDatabase` and `useWebSocket`. The compiler's own `lowered-hooks-typecheck` fixture already writes that import.

The web half is **state, not a renderer**, exactly as `PyreonMapState` is: camera, markers, selection, nothing else. So it needs **no mapping library** and imposes no choice of one — feed `map.camera` / `map.markers` to Leaflet, MapLibre, Google Maps or an `<svg>`.

Native semantics are mirrored including the parts easy to get subtly wrong, each locked by a test:
- `addMarker` **upserts** by id and **preserves list position**
- `removeMarker` clears a selection pointing at it
- `moveTo` keeps the current zoom when omitted — via `??`, since `||` would drop a legitimate zoom of `0`
- `selectedMarker` is **derived**, never stored

## 2. `map.moveTo(…)` and `map.removeMarker(…)` did not compile on Swift

The primary map API failed with `missing argument labels 'latitude:longitude:' in call`. Swift labels arguments; the shared TS surface is positional; the generic emit is positional. Kotlin accepted the identical source, since named arguments are optional there.

This is the **same defect #2514 fixed for `PyreonDatabase`** — fixed in a database-shaped way, leaving every other service exposed. Rather than add a second special case, the table is now per-service-kind with **full-positional** labels; the old "labels after a leading unlabelled argument" shape cannot express `moveTo`, whose *first* argument is labelled.

Scope was **enumerated, not guessed**: every `public func` in runtime-swift with a labelled parameter was listed, then each probed for reachability from the hook surface.

| service | status |
|---|---|
| `PyreonDatabase` get/delete/find | already fixed (#2514) |
| `PyreonMapState` moveTo, removeMarker | **broken → fixed here** |
| `PyreonMapState` selectMarker(`_ id:`) | unlabelled natively, correct as-is |
| `PyreonGeolocation.update` | internal transition, not on the hook surface |
| `PyreonWebSocket.connect(to:)` | internal; the TS surface is 0-arg |
| `PyreonSecureStorage` | not lowered at all (deferred v1) |

## 3. The compiler typed a `map.error` that exists on neither runtime

`{map.error}` failed swiftc with `value of type 'PyreonMapState' has no member 'error'`. That entry was added in #2566 by generalising *"every service container has an optional `error`"* across the services without checking each runtime — **my own over-generalisation**, the same mistake documented for `@pyreon/rx`.

`PyreonMapState` holds camera/markers/selection, performs no I/O and cannot fail. The entry is **removed** rather than the field added: an always-nil `error` on a container that cannot fail is dead surface, and if map gains I/O the field should arrive with the failure it reports. The web half has no `error` either, for the same reason.

## Verification

Bisect-verified: reverting the label path fails the three map specs while all four guards — unlabelled `selectMarker`, the over-long-call fallthrough, unchanged database output, and Kotlin — stay green, proving they do not pass merely because of the fix.

`@pyreon/hooks` 402 tests, `swift-service-arg-labels` 7/7, `useMap` 12/12, `validate-fast` 17/17. The natural component compiles clean on both targets with zero warnings. Full compiler suite queued locally as early warning; CI runs the same suite and is the gate.

The hooks manifest enumeration was also stale — bumped to 48 for `useGeolocation` without naming it — so both data hooks are now named.

The Now Playing cover area was inert — the only play/pause target was the transport button below it. Clicking, tapping, or pressing Enter/Space anywhere in the cover area now toggles playback.

author: clay-good
body:
**Status:** LGTM — resolves alfred's CHANGES_REQUESTED on the v1.7.0 Version Packages PR (#1380); this is the release-gating fix for #1390.

**What was wrong:** Installing OpenSpec shipped `posthog-node`'s transitive tree (`@posthog/core`, `@posthog/types`) to every downstream consumer. Those packages publish several times a day, so freshly resolved installs tripped supply-chain age policies — pnpm's `minimumReleaseAge: 1440` failed with `ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION` on entries younger than the window (#1390, reproduced by alfred against the 1.7.0 candidate).

**Why no form of pinning works** (each verified, not assumed):
- Exact-pinning `posthog-node` leaves its own `@posthog/core` range floating (alfred's point).
- npm `overrides` apply only at the consumer's root, never from a dependency.
- pnpm ignores a dependency's `npm-shrinkwrap.json` — and the failing consumers are pnpm users.
- `bundledDependencies` under pnpm-managed `node_modules` packs the `.pnpm` virtual-store layout: the bundled `posthog-node` resolves but `@posthog/core` does not, and the installed CLI crashes on import. Empirically tested; transcript available.

**How it was fixed:** The SDK's only remaining job was the wire format — the client was already configured to send exactly one event, immediately, time-bounded, no retries, through an injected `fetch` that never throws. The telemetry module now posts the same capture payload to the same `/batch/` endpoint with that fetch directly. Same event name, properties, `distinct_id`, opt-out guards (`OPENSPEC_TELEMETRY=0`, `DO_NOT_TRACK`, CI), and first-run notice; `shutdown()` still flushes in-flight events, each bounded by the 1s request timeout. `posthog-node` is removed from `dependencies`.

**Replication / proof:**
- Packed tarball: **zero** posthog files.
- The exact #1390 scenario: a pnpm consumer with `minimumReleaseAge: 1440` installs the tarball cleanly with **zero** posthog lockfile entries and a working CLI — the failure is now structurally impossible, not just currently avoided.
- Live wire check: `POST https://edge.openspec.dev/batch/ → 200 OK` with the new payload.
- Regression coverage (the requested packed-consumer guarantee): tests pin that the published manifest (`dependencies`/`optionalDependencies`/`peerDependencies`) contains no posthog package and that no `src/` module imports one — the invariant that makes any age-policy violation from our tree impossible. A full registry-resolution-under-policy test would be network- and clock-dependent in CI; the invariant test enforces the same guarantee deterministically.
- Full suite: 115 files / 3,384 tests green. Telemetry tests now assert against the real network boundary (fetch spy) instead of an SDK mock: payload shape, timeout signal, flush-before-exit, and silent failure on error/abort/non-2xx.

**Notes:** `flake.nix`'s `pnpmDeps` hash will need its usual bump for the lockfile change — will follow up with the CI-reported hash on this branch. One net effect users may notice: `npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec` gets ~160 packages lighter.

Fixes #1390

## What changed

- Limited optimistic Space reorder cancellation to the exact list query.

`queryKeys.spaces` and `queryKeys.agents` are also prefixes for descendant resource caches. Invalidating or canceling those keys without `exact: true` could refetch or cancel active node, text, and agent-key queries when only a collection reconciliation was intended.

body:
### Motivation

- The execution-grant revocation path could miss tasks or debug sessions that start asynchronously across `await` boundaries, allowing configured execution to continue after the grant is revoked. 
- The change aims to make task and debug startup revocation-safe so revocation consistently terminates or prevents work that begins while a start call is pending.

### Description

- Re-check the execution grant immediately after `vscode.tasks.executeTask` returns and terminate the returned `TaskExecution` and fail with `EXECUTION_GRANT_CHANGED` when the grant changed during startup. (`packages/extension/src/vscode-v1-ide-tool-service.ts`)
- Track pending debug starts by adding `awaitingStart` and `stopRequested` flags to `TrackedDebug`, correlate late `onDidStartDebugSession` events when a start was pending, and retain the bounded observation window so late sessions are captured and stopped. (`packages/extension/src/vscode-v1-ide-tool-service.ts`)
- Add `requestDebugStop` helper to deduplicate/serialize stop requests for tracked debug sessions and use it during revocation and late-capture handling. (`packages/extension/src/vscode-v1-ide-tool-service.ts`)
- Add deterministic regression tests that exercise both races: a task `executeTask` handle arriving after revocation and a debug session reported after revocation while `startDebugging` was pending. (`packages/extension/src/vscode-v1-execution-revocation.unit.test.ts`)

### Testing

- Ran the new unit tests with `pnpm exec vitest run packages/extension/src/vscode-v1-execution-revocation.unit.test.ts` and both tests passed. 
- Built the project with `pnpm build` and the build completed successfully. 
- Ran repository checks/typecheck; the change typechecks and unit-test coverage for the added tests passed, and the full test run completed with the only remaining failing unit test being an unrelated environment-sensitive assertion that expects Node 22 while the CI container used Node 24.

author: changhansung
body:
Third and final layer of the 'npm test kills the production fleet' fix (after #357).

`FleetManager.stopAll()` calls `sdNotify("STOPPING=1")`. Because the unit is `Type=notify` + `NotifyAccess=all`, any child process that inherited `NOTIFY_SOCKET` could put the real unit into stop-sigterm — bypassing the path-level isolation added in #357.

`NotifyAccess=main` is NOT a viable fix: Node cannot send AF_UNIX datagrams, so `sdNotify()` shells out to `systemd-notify`, and the actual sender is a short-lived child. Verified on an isolated transient user unit:
```
Got notification message from PID <helper>, but reception only permitted for main PID <service>
Result=protocol
```
`READY=1` is ignored (unit never reaches active) and `WATCHDOG=1` is ignored (killed after 60s). `--pid=parent` also fails without root. `NotifyAccess=exec` doesn't apply either.

Instead: `src/sd-notify.ts` now captures `NOTIFY_SOCKET` at module load, deletes it from `process.env`, and passes it explicitly only to the helper. No child process inherits the capability, and `Type=notify`/`WatchdogSec=60` keep working.

Also documents in the template why `NotifyAccess=all` is deliberate — `git log -S NotifyAccess` shows `all` was introduced together with the watchdog feature, i.e. this was already discovered once before.
