author: amirf194
body:
Refer to issue:
- #5935

## Root cause

`read_local_path_file_from_workers` broadcasts a filesystem read to every filtered worker and returns as soon as the first one succeeds:

```python
tasks = [try_read_from_worker(worker) for worker in filtered_workers]
for completed_task in asyncio.as_completed(tasks):
    result = await completed_task
    if result:
        return result
```

`asyncio.as_completed` schedules all tasks up front, but the loop only awaits the ones it iterates before returning. Every other in-flight `try_read_from_worker` task, and the `WorkerFilesystemClient` it opened (a `TCPConnector` plus two `aiohttp.ClientSession`s), keeps running in the background with nothing left to await or cancel it. With N workers this leaks up to N-1 sessions per call, each alive until its own HTTP request finishes or times out (up to 15s).

## Fix

Create the tasks explicitly and wrap the read loop in `try/finally`: on the winning result or once every worker has failed, cancel whatever is still pending and gather it before the function returns. This is the same shape on both exit paths, success and exhaustion, so no broadcast task can outlive the call.

## Scope

This closes the orphaned-task leak in the broadcast helper itself, which the issue's own investigation had not pinned down. It does not confirm this is the cause of the reported mass `NOT_READY` reschedule under load; that needs reproducing against a live multi-worker fleet, which I do not have. The regression test demonstrates the leak and the fix directly, independent of the reported symptom.

## Tests

`tests/scheduler/test_calculator_worker_broadcast.py`: one test drives the function with five fake workers (one fast success, four slow) and asserts no spawned task is still running once the call returns; fails on main (4 of 5 left running), passes with the fix. A second test checks the all-workers-fail path still raises with the per-worker error detail.

Full suite: 1748 passed, 12 skipped.

author: muhammadbayoumi
body:
The Data page (`/source/<key>`), reviewed against the project's five rules and repaired. One commit, eight files.

## The record is the record

`table_payload` and `export_source_table` were collapsing whitespace in the values they handed out — names, brands, categories, variants, SKUs. That bought the right **order** by editing the **value**, and it reached the xlsx and Sheets export, so a brand the shop published as a single space left the building as an empty cell.

Nothing normalises on the way out now. The order is fixed where an order belongs: the grid compares a collapsed form when it sorts, when it lists the values a filter offers, and when it buckets a branch — and shows and exports exactly what was captured. `TRIM` stays in the export's `ORDER BY`; it decides the order, never a cell.

## Scraped markup ran

Tabulator renders a **string** group header through `element.innerHTML` and a **node** through `appendChild`. The header was built by concatenation, so grouping by a column whose scraped value contains markup executed it. Demonstrated, not argued: with the old version restored, the test's page really does set `window.__pwned`.

## A control that could remove its own door

Choose Columns was reachable only from the three-dot menu on a column header — and its "Show all columns" tick sends every column to the details. No columns, no headers, no menu, no way back to the chooser or Reset Columns short of the API. The command bar carries a Columns button now, wired before the empty-source return so a dataset with no rows can still be arranged. The chooser also refused to close while a save kept failing, on every press; asking twice now means "close it anyway".

## Counts and branches that lied

- The footer read the state **before** the filter, permanently one behind — "Total Rows: 0" on a table showing 3,417. `dataFiltered` is dispatched from inside Tabulator's filter routine, before the filtered rows become the active set.
- Filtering while nested deleted whole branches: a parent row carries only the nested column, so it failed every other predicate and took its matching children with it — 3,417 rows became "0 of 19". A branch is kept when any child matches.
- Grouping or nesting by Tax put the entire table under one blank heading; its own field is null on every row and the cell renders from `tax_states[tax_ref]`.

## Tests that can actually fail

`tools/grid_harness.py` loads the real `grid.js` against a fixture payload in a real browser — the same trick `panel_harness.py` already plays for the extension panel, which the Data page was the one surface not using. **18 tests** in `tests/test_grid_dom.py` drive the table and ask what it did.

Each fix above was re-broken on purpose and the matching test failed. One brittle substring assertion in `test_vendor.py` is relaxed, and says why: it pinned `groupedBy.slice()` and broke the moment a derived column needed a reader function.

## Also

- `externalLink()` replaces six copies of `target=_blank` + `rel=noopener`. Reading the staged diff caught the helper calling **itself** after a bad automated rewrite — no existing test rendered a link, so all 17 passed over infinite recursion. There is a test for it now.
- 44 hand-written `1px solid var(--line)` become `var(--table-rule)`, the token `table-theme.css` declares for exactly this.
- `remember_` becomes `rememberChoice`.

## Verification

- Full suite on this branch: **no failures** (excluding `test_panel_dom` and `test_connector_live_defects`, which need a browser session and the network and are untouched here).
- `tests/test_grid_dom.py`: **18 passed**.
- Rebased onto `efbe7ca`; the only overlap was `scrapex/tax.py`, checked by hand — their change renames tax_rule's SQL columns, mine removes a duplicate dict key in `as_dict()`. Orthogonal, and no duplicate key remains (verified by AST scan).

## Known and deliberately left

21 column keys are written as literals in `grid.js` and authored again in `reports.py`'s `BROWSE_COLUMNS`. That split has already rotted twice in this file's own history. Fixing it means the server declaring each column's ROLE (`money`, `date`, `link`, `numeric`) — a contract change too large to hide in this commit.

## What

author: rjmurillo
body:
## Summary

### What

Adds MUST 9 to the `ci-scripts` rule: a validator that makes a claim about
repository contents must read a committed tree, not the reflog, not the object
graph, and not a directory walk. Widens the rule's `paths:` so it loads for
skill-owned scripts and tests, which is where the defect it addresses actually
lives.

### Why

Two independent incidents, same defect class. A shipped test enumerates deleted
files with `git log --all`, which reads every ref this clone happens to hold
rather than the repository's history. That set is a property of one machine's
fetch configuration, not of the repository, so the same test on the same commit
answers differently on CI and on a laptop. Deleting a single local remote-tracking
ref in this working tree flipped the test with zero repository change. Verified:
at `HEAD` the repository reports 8 deleted skills; `--all` in this working tree
reports 73.

The rule already encodes the matching epistemics in MUST 7 and MUST 8 ("`git
rev-parse` reports a claim, not a fact"). MUST 9 extends that to repository
contents rather than introducing a competing always-on rule.

## Specification References

| Type | Reference | Description |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| **Issue** | Refs #3753 | `git log --all` in a shipped test reads local refs, not repository history |
| **Issue** | Refs #3420 | Prior incident of the same class, closed NOT_PLANNED |

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `.claude/rules/ci-scripts.md` | MUST 9 plus four added path globs |
| `.github/instructions/ci-scripts.instructions.md` | Generated mirror |
| `src/copilot-cli/instructions/ci-scripts.instructions.md` | Generated mirror |
| `.claude/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | 0.6.198 |
| `src/copilot-cli/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | 0.6.198 |

## Design notes

**Why extend rather than add a rule file.** The always-on instruction budget is
at 98.3 percent for markdown. A new always-on rule would consume headroom that
does not exist. Path-scoped globs do not count against the always-on baseline;
measured before and after, byte totals are identical, so the placement fix is
free.

**Why `HEAD` and not `origin/main`.** Prescribing `origin/main` would break the
drift guard this rule is meant to protect, because that guard must see deletions
made by the current PR. `HEAD` is the tree under test.

**Why the working-tree carve-out.** Several validators under this rule's scope
legitimately read staged and untracked state, because that state is the subject
of the check rather than a proxy for repository contents. MUST 9 permits those
reads and forbids only restating their findings as claims about committed
history.

**Scope declined.** A `tests/**` glob was considered and rejected on
measurement: 7 of 585 files under the root test tree make repository-state
assertions. Loading the rule on 585 files to serve 7 is the instruction-bloat
pattern this change is trying not to repeat.

## Verification

- `instruction_budget.py` exit 0 after the change (`.md` 98.3 percent, `.py` 95.7 percent)
- `check_rule_activation_coverage.py` exit 0
- `generate_rules.py` idempotent: regenerating after the edit produces no further churn
- markdownlint scoped to the three changed markdown files: 0 issues
- 0 em-dash or en-dash bytes in all three markdown files, byte-verified
- Full suite on push: 17397 passed, 26 skipped, 0 failed
- Manifest parity at 0.6.198 across both plugin roots

## Background

Paths named here for context, not changed by this PR: see
`.claude/skills/orphan-ref-validator/tests/test_scan.py` for the `git log --all`
call site, `scripts/validation/instruction_budget.py` for the ceiling gate, and
`build/scripts/generate_rules.py` for the mirror generator.

This PR documents the requirement. It does not change the offending call site;
that remains open as #3753.

## Adversarial review

Two rounds against `gpt-5.6-sol`, a different model family from the author.
Round 1 returned one Critical (the original wording forbade legitimate
working-tree reads, with four in-scope scripts cited as counterexamples) and two
Required. Round 2 returned two Required (`-z` needed for machine parsing per
repo precedent, `--name-only` hides file modes and would miss a symlinked skill)
and one Optional (a relabeling loophole). All findings applied. One reviewer
recommendation was overruled on measurement and the reasoning recorded in the
commit body.

author: timdebruijn
body:
Bumps the firmware version to **0.23.0** and records what it contains. `src/main.cpp` only.

## What is in it

| PR | |
|---|---|
| [#119](https://github.com/Timdebruijn/heliograph/pull/119) | the SPH read apparent power and called it output, and ignored eleven channels |
| [#120](https://github.com/Timdebruijn/heliograph/pull/120) | the Growatt write chain, connected and still gated shut |
| [#121](https://github.com/Timdebruijn/heliograph/pull/121) | the screenshot pipeline, committed instead of remembered |
| [#122](https://github.com/Timdebruijn/heliograph/pull/122) | strip the comments out of the page and gzip what ships |
| [#123](https://github.com/Timdebruijn/heliograph/pull/123) | five screens instead of eight, and inline diagnosis for a silent inverter |

## Why MINOR and not patch

**A Growatt SPH published apparent power as its output.** `ac.power.total` read register 40 —
Pac1, in VA — so every SPH has been reporting volt-amperes as watts to MQTT, Prometheus, Modbus
and Home Assistant, wrong by the power factor whenever the inverter is not at unity. It reads 35
now. The series keeps its name and changes its meaning, which is the one thing a running Grafana
panel or an HA sensor cannot absorb quietly.

## Two behaviour changes worth stating plainly

- **`curl http://<bridge>/` needs `--compressed`.** The page is served gzipped with no identity
  copy kept. `/api/v1/*` is untouched, so scrapers and integrations are unaffected.
- **Everyone with the web UI open is signed out once.** The sessionStorage key changed with the
  rebuild. Per tab, so it costs one password prompt.

## Not changed

No endpoint, no field, no payload. The whole new UI is drawn from what `/api/v1/status` already
returned. `setup_html.h` is untouched.

## Verification

`tools/check_version.sh v0.23.0` agrees with `src/main.cpp` — and still rejects `v0.24.0`, so
the guard is doing something. All four board envs build, 844/844 native tests, every check green.

author: mischavk
body:
In the Polynomial deterministic transition, the beta weights were sampled twice: sample() drew them once via _resolve_hyperparams and returned those values in hyper_params (i.e. as the network's inference targets), then drew an independent second set from the same priors to simulate the parameter trajectory. The betas the network was trained on were therefore statistically unrelated to the ones that generated the data, and could not be recovered at all. The intercept was unaffected.

Fixed by resolving each hyperparameter once and reusing those values to build the trajectory, following the pattern already used in the Gaussian process transition. 

Adds regression tests asserting that the returned hyper_params reproduce the sampled trajectory (degrees 1–3), and that the reported beta_1 equals the total change across a degree-1 trajectory. Both fail on the pre-fix code.

author: mansurjisan
body:
`config_from_env` read the cycle hour as:

```python
cyc = int(os.environ.get("cyc", "12"))
```

Two problems in one line.

**It reads only the lowercase spelling.** PBS cards export lowercase `cyc` (`export cyc=${CYC:-00}`), but launcher and Slurm paths pass uppercase `CYC`. Any entry point that does not go through a PBS card therefore sees no `cyc` at all.

**And when absent it silently defaults to 12.** Together, a run driven with only `CYC=00` set prepped 12z forcing, wrote it into the 00z `COMOUT`, and reported success. Nothing downstream cross-checks the cycle against the data it received, so the run looks clean.

This is the same failure shape as the SECOFS ParMETIS retry, which resubmitted with a lowercase `cyc=` and silently re-ran every non-00z cycle as 00z.

## Change

- Read either spelling. Lowercase wins when both are set, since the PBS card is the more specific source.
- Raise when neither is present rather than guessing an hour.
- Reject a non-integer or out-of-range value, instead of letting it escape as a bare `ValueError` from `int()` or pass through as a nonsense cycle.

## Why it survived testing

The operational path is unaffected: PBS cards always export lowercase `cyc`, so this never fired there. It only bites entry points that bypass the cards — a direct CLI invocation, the ensemble path, or a launcher that passes `CYC` through. That is also why a green WCOSS2 cycle is not evidence against it.

## Tests

`tests/test_nco_bridge_cycle.py` covers both spellings, precedence when both are set, the missing case, and invalid input (`"ab"`, `"24"`, `"-1"`). **5 of the 7 fail against the previous behaviour**, so they are regression guards rather than restatements.

Full suite: 613 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failures.

author: seeker71
body:
Urs asked what Sanskrit and Steiner say about gender archetypes, and how to integrate gender into the core. The last clause is taken as given; the question answered is **where** it goes.

## What the body already holds — and does not

`cognition/steiner-neutral-kernel.fk` holds Steiner as a surface-independent meaning graph, with German *and* English as projections *"so that no English string can pose as the teaching."* It has a polarity — nine mentions — and that polarity is **Lucifer / Ahriman mediated by Christ**. It is not gendered. The Sanskrit cells contain **no liṅga at all**. Both halves of the question reach real cells and both are empty of it, so the new cell records those silences rather than filling them.

## Why `he`/`she` must not enter the core 64

Argued from this repo, not from principle: `nl-pivot-es.fk` seats four tongues on one pivot node *"witnessed by node identity, never by claim,"* with gender *"in the column, never in the pivot."*

**Indonesian is one of the four, and its third person `dia` carries no gender.** If `he`/`she` were primitives of the ground, the Indonesian column could not project the ground. The emptiness where they would sit is what makes a fourth tongue possible, and a fifth.

## The integration — band 511

| kind | lane | where |
|---|---|---|
| liṅga (grammatical noun class) | evidence | the emitter column, per tongue |
| sex (biological) | evidence | the measured lane |
| polarity (archetypal) | **belief** | the meaning graph, held not asserted |

liṅga sits in *evidence* because of a falsifier the band requires to be **non-empty**: nouns whose class does not follow their referent's sex. The archetypal pairs are puruṣa/prakṛti and Śiva/Śakti, with ardhanārīśvara named as the pair's own resolution.

**Mutation-proven**, five mutations each darkening exactly its own bit: `447, 447, 479, 495, 509`. The third is why the lane law was rewritten — the first version left the exact merge it forbids **green**. A validity check wearing a law's name.

## And then the tool stopped seeing edits

```
without an mtime bump:   7 of 8 mutate/restore cycles served a STALE image
with an mtime bump:      0 of 6
```

`.fkb` freshness is mtime-based at one-second granularity; a tight edit→run loop lands source and cache in the same tick. The failure direction is the bad one: **the band reporting the previous green verdict on mutated source** — and the workload that triggers it is *mutation testing*, this body's central discipline.

## Teaching — row 929, `tickblind`

A cache keyed on *when* a file changed cannot tell two changes apart inside one tick, and **the faster you verify, the blinder it gets.** The defect scales with diligence.

author: yeni023
body:
## 작업 내용

내가 작성한 리뷰 조회, 수정, 삭제 관련하여 review api 보완하였습니다.

### 신규 API

| Method | Endpoint | 설명 |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/users/me/reviews` | 내가 쓴 리뷰 목록 (정렬·페이징, 스팟명·썸네일 포함) |
| GET | `/reviews/{id}` | 리뷰 단건 조회 (수정 화면 진입용) |
| POST | `/reviews/{id}/photos` | 리뷰 사진 추가 (multipart) |
| DELETE | `/reviews/{id}/photos/{photoId}` | 리뷰 사진 개별 삭제 |

### 기능 추가

- **리뷰 태그** — `ReviewRequest.tags`가 정의만 있고 저장되지 않던 것을 구현. 고정 9종 `ReviewTag` enum(작성 화면 목업 칩과 1:1), `@ElementCollection`으로 `review_tag` 저장. 스팟 상세에 `reviewTags`(2회 이상 쓰인 태그 중 상위 3개) 노출
- **스팟당 1인 1리뷰** — 앱 레벨 검사 + `review(spot_id, user_id)` 유니크 제약. 위반 시 409 `REVIEW_ALREADY_EXISTS`
- **스팟 상세에 `myReviewId`** — 프론트가 작성/수정 분기를 한 번의 조회로 판단
- 리뷰 사진 상한 10장 → **5장**, `photos` 응답을 `[{photoId, url}]` 구조로 변경(삭제 대상 식별에 id 필요)

### 버그 수정

- **리뷰 수정 시 스팟 평점이 재계산되지 않던 문제** — 작성·삭제는 반영했으나 수정만 누락되어 별점을 바꿔도 스팟 평균이 옛 값으로 남았습니다
- **별점 정렬 페이징에서 리뷰 중복·누락** — rating이 5종류뿐이라 동점 행이 대량 발생하고 동점 순서는 DB가 보장하지 않아, 2페이지 이후 일부가 중복 노출되거나 누락됐습니다. `id DESC` 타이브레이커 추가
- **`PUT /reviews/{id}` 응답의 `photos`가 항상 빈 배열** — 프론트가 응답을 반영하면 사진이 사라진 것처럼 보였습니다
- `size=0`·`page=-1` → 500, `equipmentInfo` 100자 초과 → 500, multipart 파트명 누락 → 500, 업로드 용량 초과 → 500. 모두 400으로 변경
- **enum·숫자 오타 시 상세 메시지가 나가지 않던 문제** — Boot 4의 기본 JSON 매퍼가 Jackson 3인데 `InvalidFormatException` 임포트가 Jackson 2라 분기가 성립하지 않았습니다

### 정리

- 미참조 `TimeSlot` enum 삭제, `review.time_slot` 죽은 컬럼 제거 마이그레이션 작성
- `SpotService`의 `TEMP_USER_ID` 제거
- `review(user_id)` 인덱스 추가 (FK가 아니라 자동 인덱스가 없어 내 리뷰 조회가 풀스캔)

## 리뷰 포인트

### ⚠️ 배포 전 마이그레이션 필수 — `docs/review-time-slot-drop-migration.sql`

`ddl-auto: update`는 유니크 제약을 안정적으로 추가하지 않고, **중복 행이 있으면 조용히 실패합니다.**
적용하지 않으면 제약 없이 배포되어 동시 요청 시 중복 리뷰가 생깁니다.

```sql
-- 중복 확인 (결과가 있으면 정리 후 제약 적용)
SELECT spot_id, user_id, COUNT(*) FROM review GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```

로컬은 적용 완료했습니다(중복 30건이 전부 테스트 데이터라 리뷰 전량 삭제 후 적용). **개발 서버는 실데이터일 수 있어 확인이 필요합니다.**

### 다른 분 파일 변경 2건

- `GlobalExceptionHandler` — 핸들러 2개 추가(`MissingServletRequestPart`, `MaxUploadSizeExceeded`)와 Jackson 3 임포트 교체. 기존 핸들러 수정 없음
- `SecurityConfig` — `PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS`에서 `/reviews/**` 제거. `/reviews` 아래 공개 엔드포인트가 없어 **동작 변화는 없고**, 새 엔드포인트가 기본 공개되는 fail-open을 없애기 위함입니다

### 프론트 breaking change (전달 완료)

- `photos` → `[{photoId, url}]` (이미 연동된 스팟 리뷰 목록 포함)
- `tags` 요청이 자유 문자열 → enum 이름 9종 고정
- 사진 상한 5장, 에러 코드 `IMAGE_FILE_TOO_MANY` → `REVIEW_PHOTO_TOO_MANY`
- `POST /spots/{id}/reviews`에 409 신설

### 논의 대기 (이 PR 범위 밖)

- **인증 실패 응답 형식** — Security 필터에서 끝나 `GlobalExceptionHandler`를 타지 않아 403 + Boot 기본 바디가 나갑니다. 401 + 공통 형식 전환은 인증 담당자와 리프레시 토큰 작업 시 함께 논의 예정
- **`TEMP_USER_ID` 인증 연동** — 북마크 9곳·체크리스트 10곳. 읽기만 바꾸면 북마크 버튼이 먹지 않아 이번엔 스팟 상세의 `isBookmarked`를 기존 동작으로 유지했습니다
- **리뷰 사진 EXIF** — 추출·저장이 구현되지 않은 상태(`ExifExtractor`가 미사용). 별도 작업

### 확인 부탁드리는 부분

- `@ElementCollection`으로 태그를 저장한 선택 (별도 엔티티 대신). `review_tag`가 네이티브 ENUM 컬럼으로 생성되어 **태그를 추가하면 `ALTER TABLE`이 필요**합니다 — enum에 주석으로 남겼습니다
- 사진 추가/삭제를 전용 엔드포인트로 분리한 선택 (`PUT`을 multipart로 전환하는 대안 대비)
- `createReview`를 `saveAndFlush`로 바꿔 제약 위반을 사진 업로드 전에 확정시킨 부분

author: tooney92
body:
Two things a live demo tripped over.

## `testing` was invisible

The todo stepper collapsed `backend_live` and `testing` into a single `ready` node. That hid the step people find most surprising: `verified` transitions from `testing` **only**, so a consumer has to report a check before anyone can verify. With the two collapsed, the widget stopped moving the moment the producer said ready and gave no sign whether anyone had actually checked — which is exactly the question a human asks at that point.

`testing` now has its own node, so `ok #N` visibly advances something and "has anyone tested this?" is answerable at a glance.

The early-`verified` error now teaches the move rather than just refusing it: nobody has checked yet, a consumer reports it first with `report_status('checked')`, and that gate is the reason a verified task can never mean "nobody actually tried it".

## Two copies of the per-client connect blocks

`join.html` was rendering its own copies of the config blocks while the broker was already serving them on `/pair`. The per-client keys differ in ways that read as cosmetic — `mcpServers` vs `servers` vs `context_servers`, `url` vs `serverUrl` vs `httpUrl` — so a second copy drifts into configs that fail silently. Same failure that lost `upto` from the cheatsheet and grew a second vocabulary on the todo card.

The page now renders no field name of its own. The Python copy is covered by tests asserting those blocks appear in `docs/connect-your-agent.md` verbatim; the copy in the page was covered by nothing. Every entry echoes the `mcp_url` it was rendered with, so a page behind a tunnel rebases each string in one substitution.

668 tests passing.

author: malibio
body:
Closes #1799

## What this changes

The `noExtraTypes` assertion counted `create_schema` calls and never checked what was persisted, so a call that was rejected outright scored as a pass. Scenario 3 had been a recorded false pass in every prior run.

The evidence needed to catch it was already produced and already printed — `aichat.ts` emits an `[ERROR]` marker per tool call — but `runner.ts` kept only the tool name and discarded the rest of the line. This carries the outcome through.

- **`agent_loop.rs`** logs `result_field_count`, taken from the tool RESULT rather than its arguments. Args are the model's report of what it asked for; the result is what the executor persisted. A bare integer because both previews truncate at 300 chars and a realistic `create_schema` payload exceeds that — a parser reading them would fail on exactly the well-formed calls it should pass.
- **`types.ts`** gains `toolCalls` alongside `toolsCalled` rather than replacing it, so `routing.ts` needs no edits and recorded baselines still join in `compareToBaseline`.
- **`agent-matrix.ts`** checks schema soundness on **both** the `noExtraTypes` and `toolOnce` branches. Scenarios 8a/8b reach `create_schema` through `toolOnce` and had the identical count-only hole; fixing only `noExtraTypes` (what the issue named) would have left most of the measurement defect in place.

## Two failure modes, not one

A rejected call persists nothing. But a call carrying neither `fields` nor `description` **succeeds** and persists a type with no properties (`packages/core/src/schema/mod.rs:275-277`) — invisible to any check that only asks whether the call errored. The issue's framing would have missed this; 8a/8b are exactly this case.

Absent `fieldCount` is treated as unknown, so baselines recorded before this do not read as fresh failures.

## Verification

Both branches mutation-tested: reverting either one fails exactly its own two unit tests and no others.

Run against **unmodified** guidance — so the assertion is demonstrated failing on current code, per the issue's first acceptance criterion:

- **3** — `create_schema was called but REJECTED — no schema persisted`
- **8a** — `create_schema succeeded but persisted a type with NO fields`
- **8b** — same

`bun run test:all` passes (4,106 frontend / 20 browser / 29 scripts / 10 Rust suites), no new failures.

## Scope: assertion only

The issue's checklist items 3-5 (routing `create_schema` through `search_skills`) are **not** included. That change was implemented and measured, and it makes behavior worse: 6/12 → 3/12 under identical conditions, with the model calling `search_skills` and then stopping. Its premise also does not hold — `SCHEMA_CREATION_RULES` is resident every turn and already carries the rule the model broke. Detail in the issue comments; the underlying guidance defect is now the spike #1802.

**No baseline is recorded here.** `scripts/results-e4b.json` is deliberately untouched: every run it holds was measured through an architecture #1802 is questioning, and at n=12 with only 3 schema scenarios the matrix cannot clear its own ~2-scenario noise floor. The assertion fix stands on mutation testing, not on any eval score.

islamokasha1-cloud
body:
## المشكلة

بلاغ المستخدم: أخطاء `FIRESTORE INTERNAL ASSERTION FAILED (ID: ca9/b815)` تظهر في سجل الأخطاء **دائماً من كمبيوترٍ واحدٍ محدّد ولمستخدم الأدمن** — لا عشوائياً.

## التشخيص

الدليل الحاسم في اللقطة نفسها:

```
CONTEXT: {"Ce":-1,"targetId":1044}
```

عدّاد أهداف المراقبة `targetId` بلغ **1044**. هذا العدّاد **تصاعديٌّ داخل عميل الـ SDK ولا يُصفَّر إلا بإعادة تحميل الصفحة** (SDK جديد). ومنه:

- **الأدمن** = أكثر الأدوار تركيباً وفكّاً للمستمعين وتنقّلاً بين المشاريع والوضع المركزي.
- **الجهاز المحدّد** = المحطّة التي **لا يُغلَق تبويبها أبداً** (تبقى مفتوحةً أياماً)، فيتراكم `targetId` حتى يبلغ منطقة الخلل — بينما بقيّة المستخدمين يُغلقون المتصفّح يومياً فيبدؤون بعدّادٍ منخفض.

المخفّفات القائمة (§17: `forceLongPolling`، كاش ذاكرة، مستمعو `global_*` مرة واحدة، تعافٍ تلقائي `_fsAutoRecover`) تُقلّل الاحتكاك لكنها **لا تكفي مع عمرِ تشغيلٍ لا نهائيّ** (أيُّ احتكاكٍ ضئيل × زمنٌ لا نهائي ⇒ يبلغ الخلل حتماً).

## الإصلاح

### (١) إتمام قاعدة §17 لمستمعَي إشعارات سطح المكتب (`startHailNotifications`)

كانا يُفكّان ويُعاد تركيبهما مع **كل** استدعاء (دخول مشروع + دخول المشتريات المركزية):

- مستمع **طلبات الشراء** يقرأ `global_purchases` (**مجموعة عامة**) ⇒ صار **يُركَّب مرة واحدة** (حارس idempotent `!_hnPOUnsub`).
- مستمع **البلاغات** (`_pfx` مرتبط بالمشروع) ⇒ يُعاد تركيبه **فقط عند تغيّر المشروع فعلاً** (`_hnTicketsProjKey`).
- كلاهما يُفكّ عند الخروج (`logout` / `logoutToLogin`) فيُعاد تركيبه نظيفاً للجلسة التالية.

### (٢) تحديثٌ وقائيٌّ للجلسات الطويلة (يعالج «الجهاز الدائم التشغيل» جذرياً)

مستمعٌ على `visibilitychange`: إن تجاوز عمرُ الجلسة **٦ ساعات** وغادر المستخدمُ التبويبَ (`document.hidden`) يُعاد التحميل **صامتاً** بعد تأكيدٍ ٨ ثوانٍ — SDK جديد بعدّاد `targetId` صفريّ. **لا يُطلَق أبداً والتبويبُ ظاهر** فلا يقطع عملاً؛ المسودّات في `localStorage` و`onSnapshot` يعيد المزامنة فور العودة.

## الملفات

- `index.html` — الإصلاحان + رفع `APP_VERSION`/`MODULE_BUILD`/cache-busters إلى `v18.9ub`.
- `hail-tests.js` — ٨ فحوص حارسة جديدة (القسم ١٧).
- `NOTES.md` — سجل الإصدار v18.9ub وتحديث حالة الفحوص.

## الاختبارات

✅ **449/449** فحصاً ناجحة على `v18.9ub` (`node hail-tests.js`).

body:
手机端在 tmux 没有任何 session 时**完全卡死**：看不到侧栏开关，也就打不开抽屉，连 session 都建不了。

## 根因

`main-header`（含 ☰ 按钮）整个被套在 `current && currentWindow ? ... : ...` 的真分支里。没有 session 时走假分支，表头根本不渲染。桌面端侧栏常驻所以无感，**窄屏下侧栏是抽屉、默认隐藏，唯一入口就是那个 ☰**——它不在，用户就没有任何出路。

## 改动

- 表头始终渲染；`WindowTabs` 才按有无当前窗口条件渲染
- 空状态里直接放一个新建入口——没有 session 正是最需要它的时候
- 新增 `web/src/App.test.tsx`，覆盖无 session / 有 session 两种情形

## 一个测试上的坑

侧栏那个「＋ 新建 session」按钮**在 DOM 里始终存在**，窄屏下只是被 CSS `transform` 移出屏幕，而 jsdom 不应用媒体查询。所以 `screen.getByRole('button', {name: /新建 session/})` 在修复前也能通过——对这个 bug 完全不敏感。用例改为限定在 `main` 区域内查找才真正红过。

第一版测试就是这样一个假阳性，写下来免得下次再踩。

author: omarshahine
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The channel could not start. `openKeyedStore` is gated on `trustedOfficialInstall`, and every durable surface it has goes through it.

**The gate is not reachable.** Reading the host settles it — trust is not about how a plugin is installed:

```js
const catalogEntry = getOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEntryForPackage(packageName);
if (!catalogEntry || resolveOfficialExternalPluginId(catalogEntry) !== params.pluginId) return false;
```

It requires membership in OpenClaw's **official external plugin catalog**. A local `plugins install --force` was tried and refused exactly like a path load. A third-party plugin cannot get there, so #93's advice — "install through ClawHub" — was wrong. This replaces the dependency instead of the message.

## Why This Change Was Made

`store.ts` is a SQLite-backed keyed store the plugin owns, under `$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/apple-pim/`. One file, one table, namespaced, and exactly the `lookup`/`register` interface the four callers already used — so cursor, thread records, quarantine, and run budget changed storage without changing shape.

Three things the gateway found that no test could:

- **`node:sqlite` must be required at runtime.** Bundlers targeting Node older than 22.5 don't recognize the specifier and rewrite it to a bare `sqlite`, which fails to resolve and takes the whole plugin down with `Cannot find module 'sqlite'`. Build target moved to node22, `engines.node` to `>=22.5`.
- **`startAccount` must await its loop.** Returning once the loop was running read as a channel that started and exited, and the gateway restarted it every five seconds. The old comment claimed the gateway needed startup to complete. It needs the opposite.
- **A log line printed `undefined limit`** when the breaker closed mid-batch, because that path reports how many were held without the window that bound them.

## User Impact

The channel works. Requires Node 22.5+, which the gateway already exceeds.

## Evidence

Final dev-gateway run against the real mailbox:

```
http server listening (4 plugins: apple-pim-cli, facetime, policy, xai)
[apple-mail] reply to no-reply@notifications.ui.com suppressed (observe_only)
[apple-mail] reply to noreply@email.apple.com suppressed (observe_only)
[apple-mail] circuit breaker open (hour limit of 2 agent runs reached);
             holding 3 message(s) until 2026-07-29T08:26:00.126Z
[diagnostic] session turn created: agentId=lobster
             sessionKey=apple-mail:default:0101019dc199...@us-west-2.amazonses.com
```

**0 restarts, 0 exits, 0 load failures.**

- Two real newsletters admitted as `observe` and their replies suppressed — the graduated policy firing on live mail.
- Two agent turns created against real messages, under per-thread session keys.
- The breaker opened at exactly its configured limit of 2 and held 3 messages rather than dropping them.
- Cursor and budget persisted and reloaded:

```
apple-mail:budget | apple-mail:default | {"runs":[1785309960126,1785309970048]}
apple-mail:cursor | apple-mail:default | {"lastDateReceived":"2026-05-03T19:40:48.000Z",...}
```

199 tests, `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run build` clean. Dev sandbox config restored and the test database removed.

## Still Open

- `channelConfigs` placement — the host still reports the metadata as missing, so the key isn't read from where the manifest puts it. Cosmetic; setup UI only.
- RFC 0027 now defines a fourth level, `unverified`. This plugin still scores that case `mutable` because three levels were all it had when it was written. Correct admission today, wrong name; move it when the kernel ships the primitive.

body:
## Summary

Per owner direction, the lane must not run 2+ hour jobs. A full mutation pass over `copybook-core` (finished at 2h12m) or `copybook-codec` (SIGTERM at 2h20m, likely runner eviction) is too long and too fragile for a single job — even the 6h cap from #634 only made it slower, not safer.

Change:
- Both large crates run as 4 shard jobs (`--shard 1/4..4/4`), each capped at 90 minutes.
- The 6h job timeout from #634 is reverted; everything else keeps the 60-minute cap.
- Artifact and log names carry the shard suffix so parallel shard uploads don't collide.
- Scores/thresholds are computed per shard and aggregated as before.

Verified locally: `--shard 1/4` splits the mutant set correctly (12 → 3 for copybook-error); YAML parses; unsharded matrix entries render identical step/artifact names as before.

author: jlgonzalez
body:
## Resumen
Hasta ahora **todo** el arte del juego (césped, arbustos, árboles, jugador, NPCs, policía, sado, condones, pastilla, ropa) se dibujaba en cada frame con instrucciones de canvas (`fillRect`/`ellipse` con colores hexadecimales) directamente en `index.html`. La única forma de cambiar el arte era editar ese código de dibujo.

Este PR mueve todo ese arte a **hojas de sprites PNG editables** en `assets/`:

- `assets/tiles.png` — 4 variantes de césped + arbusto + árbol
- `assets/player.png` / `assets/player_naked.png` — jugador (4 direcciones × 2 fotogramas de caminar), versión vestida y versión "en pelotas"
- `assets/cop.png` / `assets/sado.png` — 2 fotogramas de caminar cada uno
- `assets/npcs.png` — 4 colores (rojo/azul/verde/amarillo)
- `assets/items.png` — condones (4 colores), pastilla, camiseta

El motor ahora carga estas imágenes y las pinta con `drawImage()` en vez de dibujar formas. `assets/README.md` documenta la rejilla exacta de cada hoja (qué celda es cada cosa) para que puedas abrirlas en Aseprite/Piskel/Photoshop/GIMP y repintarlas tú mismo sin tocar una línea de código — solo hay que respetar el tamaño de cada celda.

Los efectos que cambian en tiempo real (el aura de color de los NPCs, el tinte verde de la peste, el parpadeo de ojos del policía, el "!" del sado, los brillos de los items) se mantienen como overlays dibujados por código encima del sprite, porque "hornearlos" en una imagen fija los volvería a hacer no editables — está explicado en el README.

De paso corregí un bug que encontré durante las pruebas: la animación de "match" (censura) todavía rellenaba el fondo con el marrón antiguo de antes de que el césped se pusiera verde, lo que dejaba ver una rejilla marrona entre las casillas.

## Test plan
- [x] Probado con Playwright en iPhone 13 y en escritorio (1400×900): título, movimiento, animación de caminar, NPCs de los 4 colores, policía, sado, condón sostenido, arbusto/árbol, estado de peste, estado desnudo, animación de match — todo se ve igual (o mejor) que antes.
- [x] Sin errores de consola ni de carga de imágenes en ninguna sesión de prueba.
- [x] Verificado que la pantalla de carga ("Cargando…") aparece y desaparece correctamente antes de que arranque el juego.

body:
사용자 요청입니다 — *"이미지 폴더 룰을 사용자가 잘 알 수 있도록 사용자 친화적 문법으로 도움말"*

**새 체계를 만들지 않았습니다.** 텍스트 개혁 ②가 만든 `HelpDialog`에 주제를 얹었습니다(`Topic.ORGANIZE_FOLDER`). 본문의 단일 소스는 가이드 9-2의 **H13**입니다 — `HelpDialog` KDoc이 요구하는 규약입니다.

## 왜 한 주제로 뭉쳤나

H1~H12는 필드 편집의 스위치 하나를 설명하는 2~3문장인데, H13은 **기능 전체**라 절이 나뉩니다. 길이를 맞추려고 쪼개면 *"폴더에 넣으면 무슨 일이 일어나는가"*라는 **한 질문이 여러 창으로 흩어집니다.** 한 번 읽고 마는 종류라 한 자리에 모으는 편이 낫다고 판단했습니다.

## 읽는 순서를 설계했습니다

1. **무엇을 하는 기능인가** — 내보내기 → 파일 탐색기에서 정리 → 받아오기, 3단계
2. **어느 폴더에 넣으면 어떻게 되는가** — 캐릭터 이름 / 그 밖의 이름 / 바로 아래 / `_공유` / `_처리됨`
3. **몰라서 당황할 것** — 지워도 안 지워짐, 지운 게 되살아남, 코드 지우지 말 것, 묶음은 합쳐짐

**내부 용어를 쓰지 않았습니다.** 토큰·링크 그룹·배정 같은 말 대신 "파일 이름 끝의 영문·숫자", "같은 폴더에 있는 것끼리 묶임"처럼 **사용자가 보는 것으로만** 말합니다.

## 진입점 2곳

- 이미지 탭 ⋮ > **정리 폴더 사용법**
- 설정 > 이미지 정리 폴더 > **정리 폴더 사용법** (4번째 행, 목적문 포함)

사전 확인 다이얼로그에는 **넣지 않았습니다** — 버튼을 더하면 기본 동작(dismiss)을 덮어써야 하고, 반영 직전에 긴 글을 띄우는 것은 결정을 방해합니다.

## 검증

순수 JVM **918건** · 차분 컴파일 **신규 오류 0**(새 뷰바인딩 id 1종 + stdlib `listOf`) · 리소스 점검 통과(**어제 만든 문자열 이스케이프 검사 포함** — 이번엔 통과했습니다) · 텍스트 스타일 새 위반 **0**

## 확인 부탁드립니다 (`remaining_work` 3-14장 13번)

두 진입점이 같은 내용을 띄우는지, 글이 끝까지 스크롤되는지 봐 주시고 — **읽어 보시고 틀린 설명이나 빠진 것이 있으면 알려 주세요.** 규약을 글로 옮긴 것이라 코드와 어긋나면 그것 자체가 결함입니다.

author: bohyunkang-iotrust
body:
## 배경

머지된 감사 대응 PR 7건(#11~#17)을 **독립 교차검증**한 결과, C1 정정에서 빠진 곳이 발견됐습니다. 원본 감사도, 대응 PR도 이 위치를 잡지 못했습니다.

`app/web/src/components/Hero.jsx:31` — **랜딩 첫 화면**의 출품 설명문입니다.

> 출품 · 🔬 Research Specialist Agent. **낙찰 에이전트가 온체인 정산 증명으로 결과물을 unlock 합니다.** 최고가가 아니라 권한 있는 bid만 실행됩니다.

## 왜 문제인가

두 겹으로 사실과 다릅니다.

1. **"낙찰 에이전트가 … unlock 합니다"** — 주어를 낙찰자로 한정합니다. `app/seller.js`에는 호출자 인증이 없으므로 실제로는 누구든 열 수 있습니다.
2. **"온체인 정산 증명으로"** — 요청자가 증명을 제시한다는 뉘앙스입니다. 실제로는 요청자가 아무것도 제시하지 않고 seller가 체인을 혼자 읽습니다.

**심각도**: Receipt 탭은 클릭해야 보이지만 hero는 **랜딩 첫 화면**입니다. #11이 Receipt 화면 3곳을 정정하고 실물/연출 표에 "미구현(후순위) 요청자 신원 검증" 행까지 넣었는데, 정작 심사위원이 가장 먼저 보는 문장이 옛 주장을 하고 있어 정직성 표기 전체가 무너집니다.

**라이브 실증** — 정산된 라운드에 인증 없이 호출하면 결과물 전문이 그대로 나옵니다.

```
$ curl -s :4100/slot/14/result        → 200 + contentMarkdown 전문
$ curl -s :4000/slot/14/result        → 200 (orchestrator relay)
$ curl -H 'User-Agent: judge-laptop' -H 'Origin: http://evil.example' :4000/slot/14/result → 200
```

## 무엇을 고쳤나

`README.md:46`과 같은 문구로 통일했습니다.

| 위치 | 전 | 후 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Hero.jsx:31` (화면 렌더) | "낙찰 에이전트가 온체인 정산 증명으로 결과물을 unlock 합니다" | "온체인 정산이 확인된 뒤에만 결과물이 열립니다" |

같은 주장이 남아 있던 **코드 주석 4곳**도 함께 정리했습니다. 공개 레포라 코드를 읽는 사람에게 그대로 노출됩니다.

| 위치 | 처리 |
| --- | --- |
| `seller.js:3` | "정산 증명이 곧 접근 권한이다" → 게이트가 무엇인지로 교체 + **호출자 신원 검증이 없다는 사실을 주의 문단으로 명시** |
| `seller.js:60` | "낙찰자에게만 의미 있음" 제거 |
| `auction-flow.js:277` | "낙찰자에게 unlock되는 결과물 메타" → "정산 후 seller가 여는" |
| `lib/gemini.js:79` | "낙찰자에게 unlock되는" → "정산 후 unlock되는" |

`seller.js` 상단 주석이 특히 문제였습니다. 인증이 없는 바로 그 파일이 "정산 증명이 곧 접근 권한"이라고 단언하고 있었습니다. C3에서 `saltFor` 주석에 공개값 성질을 남긴 것과 같은 방식으로, 미구현 사실을 코드 옆에 붙였습니다.

## 실행 코드는 바뀌지 않았습니다

문구와 주석만입니다. `git diff`의 모든 변경 라인이 주석이거나 JSX 텍스트입니다.

## 검증

| 항목 | 결과 |
| --- | --- |
| `node --check` (seller · auction-flow · gemini) | 통과 |
| `app/web` 빌드 | 통과 (162.90 kB) |
| headless 브라우저 hero 렌더 | "출품 · 🔬 Research Specialist Agent. **온체인 정산이 확인된 뒤에만 결과물이 열립니다.** 최고가가 아니라 권한 있는 bid만 실행됩니다." |
| `verify-e2e.sh` (라운드 #21) | **PASS** — 3분기 판정 · 정산 전 게이트 5회 관측 · 온체인 Settled·winner=A · vault 소진 · hash·winner 교차 대조 |

## 관련

- #11 (C1 서술 정정) 의 잔여
- #16 (C1 후속 fixture) 과 같은 성격의 후속

author: michael-herwig
body:
Follow-up to #112. Test-only, no production change.

#112 correctly made an absent `variants` legal. What it left unpinned is the **under-claiming** direction: every remaining rejection test is a root claiming *more* than its tags support.

Mutating the gate to accept any subset —

```python
if root.variants and not set(root.variants) <= set(derived):
```

— passes the whole module, **19 of 19**. A root recording `variants: ["slim"]` whose tags imply both `slim` and `musl` would sail through, and the gate could be weakened to allow it with nothing going red.

Adds the one test that reds on exactly that mutation. Absence asserts nothing and stays legal; a *present* field is a claim about the whole set and is held to it in both directions.

Both outcomes demonstrated: 20 passed against the real gate; sole failure under the mutation. `task verify --force` → exit 0.

author: kevinlourd
body:
The public billing-stats surface still summed **gross** received amounts, so the platform-wide "total credited" a consumer composes from it disagreed with the sum of the per-org ones once refunds + lost disputes started being mirrored (v0.27.0). At today prod data the platform total was overstated by **7500 cents** (three fully refunded USD payments, zero disputes).

## What changed

`GET /public/stats/billing` now publishes gross and net side by side rather than collapsing them:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `total_paid_cents` | GROSS charges. **Unchanged meaning** - report as revenue |
| `total_refunded_cents` | settled (`succeeded`) Refunds |
| `total_disputed_lost_cents` | Disputes in status `lost` |
| `total_returned_cents` | refunded + disputed_lost |
| `total_net_cents` | gross - returned = **report this as credited** |

Every `monthly_growth` / `weekly_growth` bucket carries the same five figures (`paid_cents`, `refunded_cents`, `disputed_lost_cents`, `returned_cents`, `net_cents`), so a time series can never mean something different from the all-time total.

Returns reuse the per-payment rule verbatim - `refund.status = succeeded`, `dispute.status = lost`, attributed to a mirrored PaymentIntent through `payment_intent` with a `charge` <-> `latest_charge` fallback. That is what makes `total_net_cents` **exactly the sum of every org `amount_net`** from `GET /internal/payment_summary/by-org/:orgId`. Grouping runs over the refund/dispute rows themselves, never the join product, so an object matching on both keys is counted once.

## Time attribution (deliberate)

A return is bucketed in the period it **happened**, never back-dated to the payment it reverses. Back-dating would retroactively rewrite a bucket a consumer has already read and reported; this mirror is append-only like Stripe ledger. Consequence, documented on the endpoint and in the schema: a period whose refunds exceed its payments reports a **negative `net_cents`**. Both attributions preserve `sum(buckets) == all-time total`; only this one leaves history immutable.

## Not done

No payment row is mutated, hidden or deleted. No fabricated values - a bucket row with no period throws rather than dropping money into no bucket. billing-service untouched; it conforms to this deployment.

## Tests

182 passing. New coverage: no refunds (net == gross byte-identical), full refund, partial refund, a refund that reverted / an open-or-won dispute (asserted on the query predicate itself), a lost dispute, a returns-only period, and `sum(bucket net) == all-time net`.

author: jasonbates
body:
## Problem
WHOOP rotates and immediately invalidates the refresh token the instant it receives the refresh POST. `_refresh_access_token` did POST-then-`set_key`, so a cancellation of the caller between those two steps consumed the old token server-side but never persisted the successor — wedging the lineage with `invalid_request` until manual re-auth.

Observed live 2026-07-28T12:00Z under alix: a cold-started whoop backend did a lazy refresh on its first tool call; the cold `uv` spawn + OAuth round-trip exceeded alix's 5s per-context-source timeout, so the context assembler aborted the tool call mid-exchange. The whoop process survived the abort (only the request coroutine was cancelled), but the rotated token was lost — silently killing the next morning's morning-checkin.

## Fix
Wrap the token exchange + disk persist in `asyncio.shield` so a cancelled caller can no longer interrupt it; the exchange runs to completion, keeping disk and WHOOP in lock-step. Adds a regression test that cancels the caller mid-POST and asserts the successor is still persisted.

Tracked suite: 28/28 `test_client.py` pass. (Untracked WIP `tests/test_server.py` has 8 pre-existing unrelated failures.)

author: gratitude234
body:
Audited every route for loading affordances and measured what sits on the
critical path of a click. Three classes of problem, fixed here.

Missing loading states. Eleven routes were server-rendered with awaits but
had no loading.tsx, so clicking them left the previous screen frozen until
the server responded — including /create/post, the primary Create CTA, and
/explore, a top-level nav item. Added skeletons matched to each page's real
layout rather than generic boxes, so the shape doesn't shift on paint.

No error boundaries. The app had zero error.tsx files, so any throw in a
server component (a failed Supabase query, a null profile) unmounted the
tree to the root and left a blank screen with no way back. Added a boundary
per route group plus a global-error fallback for root-layout failures. The
composer gets its own, since a crash there happens with unsaved writing on
screen and the copy has to answer "did I lose my work?" first.

Request waterfalls. The main layout re-renders on every in-app navigation
and ran its profile lookup and active-debate count sequentially, so every
click paid both round trips back to back; they're independent, so they now
run together. The home page fetched the viewer's profile before starting
any feed work, but nothing in that batch depends on it — folding it in
removes a full round trip before the feed begins loading.

Also: the two Create controls pushed to a server route with no feedback, so
the button looked inert and invited repeat clicks — they now show a pending
state via useTransition. And every skeleton animated regardless of the
viewer's reduced-motion preference; all 66 now honor it, with the
highest-traffic screens gaining screen-reader labels so the wait is
announced instead of silent.

Verified: lint clean, 1019 tests pass, production build compiles.

Node 20 reached end of life in April 2026, and react-router 8 requires `>=22.22.0`. Three

> Capacitor is pinned to 7.x because its 8.x CLI requires Node 22 and the repository builds

author: kevinaeonx
body:
## Summary

Variety now runs as a real, native Windows application - on top of a genuine
Windows GTK3 build provided by [MSYS2](https://www.msys2.org/), not WSL, a
Linux VM, or a rewrite. This is the same codebase, patched at the specific
points where it assumed a Linux desktop (D-Bus, gsettings, libnotify,
AppIndicator, XDG autostart). See [WINDOWS.md](../../blob/windows-support/WINDOWS.md)
for full setup instructions and a complete list of the platform differences.

## What's included

- **Single instance / IPC**: falls back to a local loopback socket
  (`variety/win_ipc.py`, token-authenticated) when `dbus-python` isn't
  available, instead of the D-Bus session bus.
- **Wallpaper**: `SystemParametersInfoW` + registry instead of the
  `set_wallpaper`/`get_wallpaper` shell scripts.
- **Lock screen**: the WinRT `LockScreen` API, invoked via PowerShell's
  built-in WinRT projection support (no new Python dependency).
- **Notifications**: caught gracefully when no notification service is
  listening, instead of raising.
- **Tray icon**: uses the existing `Gtk.StatusIcon` fallback; fixed its popup
  menu positioning, which was badly broken under the GTK win32 backend
  (`Gtk.StatusIcon.position_menu` miscalculates the icon's screen geometry,
  producing a hugely mispositioned/oversized menu - now pops up at the
  pointer instead).
- **Autostart**: a `.vbs` script in the Windows Startup folder instead of an
  XDG `.desktop` file, wired into the existing Preferences autostart
  checkbox.
- Plus a few real, platform-agnostic bugs found along the way: `os.rename`
  doesn't overwrite existing files on Windows (switched to `os.replace` in
  the download paths), an unescaped regex pattern built from a raw
  filesystem path broke on Windows' backslash separators, and two quote
  plugins used `locale.gettext`, which is gone in Python 3.14.

## Test plan

- [x] Ran on Windows 11 via MSYS2's `ucrt64` GTK3/PyGObject/gexiv2 packages
- [x] Verified wallpaper set/get round-trips through the registry correctly
- [x] Verified lock screen image actually changes (checked via Settings ->
      Personalization -> Lock screen)
- [x] Verified the tray menu fix with a deterministic test that emits the
      real `popup-menu` GTK signal on the actual `Indicator` class and
      confirms the resulting menu is correctly sized
- [x] Verified singleton detection/IPC across two separate process
      invocations
- [x] Verified autostart `.vbs` end-to-end (ran it directly, confirmed it
      launches Variety silently after login)
- [x] Not yet tested on Windows 10 (developed/tested on Windows 11 only)

## Known gaps

- The "Fortune" quotes source needs the Linux `fortune` binary; skipped
  cleanly (not an error) when unavailable, which is always the case on
  Windows unless a user separately installs a fortune-mod port.
- `variety-slideshow` isn't packaged for Windows.

Happy to adjust scope/split this up further if that makes it easier to
review, given the maintenance-mode note in the README.

author: sklinglernv
body:
Sets up automated PyPI publishing for the four workspace packages. Publishing a **GitHub Release** is the release ceremony — the release's tag is what `uv-dynamic-versioning` turns into the version, exactly as `RELEASING.md` already described.

Nothing here can publish anything on merge. `publish.yml` triggers only on `release: published` and `workflow_dispatch`, and no GitHub Release exists yet.

## Why Releases rather than tag push

A Release *is* a tag, so versioning is unchanged. What it adds: notes live with the artifacts, a draft state to fix mistakes before anything fires, and a human click before an upload that can never be undone — PyPI does not allow reusing a version, even after a delete.

## Safety gates

A bad upload is permanent, so the build job refuses to hand off unless:

- the built version equals the release tag, and is not a `.devN` version (which would mean the tag was not reachable from the checked-out commit — the shallow-clone failure mode);
- all four wheels import cleanly in a fresh venv, and `nooa --version` runs.

## One environment per package

Publishing fans out into a 4-way matrix, each job in its own `pypi-<package>` environment.

PyPI keys a *pending* trusted publisher on (owner, repo, workflow, environment). Four packages sharing one environment collide — the second registration is rejected with *"a pending trusted publisher matching this configuration has already been registered for a different project name"*, because PyPI cannot tell which project to create on first upload. Distinct environments also give per-package approval gates.

Each job uploads only its own artifacts. The glob anchors on the `-` before the version, so `nooa-*` matches the core's files and never `nooa_cli-*`; verified to split the 8 artifacts exactly 2-per-package.

## uv `--no-sources`

Release builds now pass `--no-sources`, [as the uv packaging guide recommends](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/package/) — it disables `tool.uv.sources` so the build is exercised the way a non-uv consumer sees it. Relevant here because all three sub-packages resolve the core via `nooa = { workspace = true }`. The CI build job mirrors the flag so it stays a real canary for release-build breakage.

Verified locally: all four build with `--no-sources`, `twine check` passes on all 8 artifacts, and cross-package deps come out as a plain `Requires-Dist: nooa` with no workspace leakage.

## Packaging metadata

Project URLs on all four; classifiers and keywords on the core; READMEs for `nooa-memory` and `nooa-bench`, which would otherwise have published blank PyPI pages. `nooa-memory`'s description read *"not yet published"* — that string is the one-liner PyPI renders under the package name.

## Before the first release

- [ ] Register pending publishers for all four names (table in `RELEASING.md`) — **environment name differs per package**
- [ ] Admin: add required reviewers to the `pypi-*` environments

The environments themselves do not need pre-creating — GitHub creates them on first workflow reference. But an auto-created environment has no protection rules, so an admin should add reviewers before the first real release. A TestPyPI dry run (Actions → Publish → `testpypi`) is safe unattended.

author: phil-opp
body:
Follow-up to #2806, addressing the shutdown-robustness gap raised in that PR's latest review ([comment](https://github.com/dora-rs/dora/pull/2806#issuecomment-5074212279)).

## Problem

In `DoraNode::drop`, the startup handshake was stopped and joined *before and outside* the `teardown_with_timeout("zenoh", ZENOH_TEARDOWN_TIMEOUT, …)` block:

```rust
let ack_subscribers = match self.startup_handshake.take() {
    Some(mut handshake) => {
        handshake.shutdown();   // sets stop flag, then handle.join() on the marker thread
        std::mem::take(&mut handshake.ack_subscribers)
    }
    None => Vec::new(),
};
```

`StartupHandshake::shutdown` sets the stop flag and then unconditionally `handle.join()`s the marker thread. The marker thread's loop only checks the stop flag at the top of each iteration and then blocks in `publisher.put(&[][..]).wait()`. Setting `stop = true` cannot interrupt an in-progress `.wait()`, so on a wedged zenoh net runtime that `put().wait()` can block indefinitely and the unbounded `join()` stalls node shutdown — and with it the daemon, which waits for `InputClosed`.

This is exactly the failure mode #2425 and `teardown_with_timeout` were introduced to bound. It is reachable when a node process exits while its handshake is still in flight (route not yet proven, within the 10 s marker window) and the session is unhealthy. The consumer side already handles this correctly — `EventStream::drop` joins the `dora-startup-acker` thread *inside* `teardown_with_timeout`.

## Fix

Move the marker-thread `shutdown()`/join into the `teardown_with_timeout` closure, still before `drop(publishers)` so the join keeps its "release the last publisher `Arc` clone" property (which is what actually undeclares the publishers). The ack subscribers are undeclared immediately after, before the session, preserving the documented drop order. The producer teardown is now symmetric with the consumer side.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p dora-node-api -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p dora-node-api --lib` — 148 passed, 0 failed (incl. the `teardown_with_timeout_*` and `zenoh_teardown_fits_within_daemon_force_kill_grace` tests)

author: nikor30
body:
## Fixed

**One failing composite member no longer aborts the rest.** Deployment stopped at the first failure, so a port template that tripped over an interface took the VLAN and banner members down with it — the switch got neither. Members are independent config blocks: every one is now attempted, and the failures are reported together (*"1 of 3 templates failed; the others were applied"*).

## Added

**Day-N can be split into two stages.** Step 4 deploys the base templates; the new step 5, *Ports & uplinks*, deploys the port/uplink template afterwards.

"Deploy Day-N" behaves as before and finishes the job. "Deploy, then configure ports" runs the base templates and stops short of activating NetBox, then offers "Continue to ports & uplinks". `DayNDeployRequest.activate` defaults to `True`, so single-stage runs are unchanged; stage 1 passes `false` when a ports stage will follow, because §11 forbids marking a device active while a stage is outstanding. Devices park at `dayn_complete` between stages, and resuming such a job lands directly on the ports step.

## Schema

Migration `0012` adds `jobs.dayn2_template_id` and `job_devices.dayn2_variables`.

body:
## Description
Fixes an issue in `src/lib/apiClient.js` where `res.json()` threw an unhandled `SyntaxError` on HTTP `204 No Content` / `205 Reset Content` responses or when an API returned HTML error pages (e.g., 500 / 502 Gateway errors).

## Cause
`res.json()` was called unconditionally on every response before checking `!res.ok`. Empty body responses or non-JSON content caused `res.json()` to reject with a `SyntaxError`, which bypassed structured `ApiError` handling and error status propagation.

## Changes Made
- Added status checks to skip JSON parsing for `204` and `205` responses in [src/lib/apiClient.js](file:AlgoBuddy/src/lib/apiClient.js#L130-L140).
- Wrapped `res.json()` in a `try...catch` block to safely fallback to an empty object when non-JSON content is returned, allowing `ApiError` to be thrown with the correct status code and message.

## Testing
- Ran unit test suite (`npm test`) — all **35 tests across 9 test suites passed**.

author: ubugeeei
body: Builds on #58. The machine-level state slidx keeps, the list of decks it knows about, and the command that searches it. ## `~/.slidx/` ``` ~/.slidx/ config.toml settings, when there are any index.json the decks this machine knows about versions/ installed slidx versions bin/ the shim that is on PATH ``` Resolved as `SLIDX_HOME`, then `$XDG_DATA_HOME/slidx`, then the platform default — **the same order `install.sh` resolves it in**, and into the same `bin/`. That is not a coincidence to maintain by hand: the installer already puts a binary there and the version manager will manage that same one. Two tools with two ideas of where slidx lives is the failure the layout exists to prevent, and a version manager that is silently not managing the binary on your PATH is worse than none, because you debug the wrong thing for an hour. Windows gets `%LOCALAPPDATA%\slidx`, not a dotfile — a dot-prefixed directory hides nothing there and is just a folder with an odd name in the middle of a home directory. `XDG_DATA_HOME` is not consulted on Windows for the same reason. **`config.toml` is declared and deliberately not created.** Nothing has settings yet, and an empty config file invites somebody to put settings in it that nothing will ever read. The global default version will be `~/.slidx/version` — a one-line file in the same format as a project's `.slidx-version`, so there is one thing to learn rather than two, and no TOML parser to add. Resolving a path creates nothing. `slidx lint` in a read-only container has to lint, not fail making a directory for an index nobody asked for. ## The index Two properties decide whether it is useful or landfill, and both are load-bearing. **It fills itself.** Running any command on a deck records it — `slidx lint ./slides` is enough. No `init`, no registry, nothing to remember. A picker over an index nobody remembered to fill is worse than no picker, because somebody has to discover it is empty. Recording is best-effort in the strongest sense: a read-only home directory, a full disk, a truncated or hand-edited file — none of it can make `slidx lint` fail. A convenience that breaks the tool it is attached to is not one. **It prunes on read, not on write.** A deleted or moved project is gone from the results the next time they are read; a finder that offers paths which no longer exist trains people to stop trusting it, and that is permanent. But statting a few hundred directories is the one expensive thing here and the *write* path runs on every invocation — so `record` never touches the filesystem, `live()` filters as it goes, and the file itself is cleaned when somebody actually browses, which is the moment the cost is already being paid. Entries carry the deck's **title, event and date** from frontmatter the author already wrote. `~/code/talks/vueconf/slides` and `~/work/decks/internal/slides` are both "slides" in a picker, and a year later neither path means anything. Capped at 256, least-recently-seen first off the end: a picker over five thousand rows is not a picker, and opening a dropped deck brings it straight back. The project recorded is the directory *above* a conventional `slides/` — the one with the git repository and the vite config in it, which is the one somebody wants to `cd` to. ## `slidx open` ```bash cd "$(slidx open vueconf)" ``` That composition is the design constraint. **Only the chosen path reaches standard output**; the picker draws on the terminal directly and the names in a listing go to stderr. A picker that printed its frame into `$(…)` would be one nobody could use the way everybody wants to. **It never hangs.** Not a terminal, or `--list`, or a terminal with no raw mode, prints the matches one path per line and exits — that case is a pipe or a CI job and there is nobody there to press a key. A single match for a query somebody typed is an answer, not a menu, so it prints and exits too. Exit codes: `0` chose something, `1` nothing matched or cancelled, `2` could not run. So `cd "$(slidx open nonsense)"` fails loudly rather than cd-ing to an empty string, which is your home directory. ``` $ slidx open --list /Users/somebody/talks/vueconf # stdout Making Decks Fast — SlidxConf 2026 # stderr ``` ## The matcher Subsequence matching, hand-rolled, no dependency. Bonuses for consecutive runs and for word starts — after `-`, `_`, `/`, `.`, a space, or a camelCase edge — so `vcf` finds `vue-conf-fukuoka` and `deck` ranks `making-decks-fast` above `dark-eccentric-knot`. A capped leading penalty, because everybody's projects are twelve directories deep and that says nothing about relevance. **No typo tolerance, on purpose.** `slidz` does not find `slidx`. A finder that matches things you did not type is one you cannot *exclude* with, and narrowing is most of what people do with a picker. Positions come back as byte offsets so a deck titled in Japanese does not get sliced mid-codepoint. ## The picker, split so it can be tested Everything about *what* is shown — which rows are visible, which is selected, how a path is shortened, where the window scrolls — is a pure function in `find/screen.rs` with 20 tests on it. A picker whose layout can only be checked by looking at one is a picker whose layout is never checked. What is left touching the terminal is one small file, because its failure mode is somebody's shell left in raw mode with no echo, which looks exactly like a hung machine. Raw mode goes through `stty` rather than a crate — `termios` is not in `std`, and a terminal crate and its tree is a lot to add to a binary people pipe into a shell. The terminal's **own saved settings** are restored in `Drop`; `stty sane` would restore *a* working terminal rather than the one somebody had. Where `stty` is not there — Windows, a stripped container — it reports unavailable and the caller prints a list. `-isig` so Ctrl-C arrives as a byte rather than a signal that would skip the restore. Arrows and Ctrl-N/Ctrl-P both move; both spellings of backspace delete. The window scrolls by one at the edges rather than recentring, so the page does not move under somebody reading it. ## Design notes worth flagging for review - The `Outcome` model still holds: the picker draws to `/dev/tty` during its loop and returns only the answer, so `run()` stays a function whose output can be asserted on. - `/dev/tty` by name rather than inherited stdin, so `slidx open < /dev/null` still works and the path still goes to stdout cleanly. - Narrowing pulls the cursor back into the list on nearly every keystroke; that is the ordinary case, not an edge one, and there is a test for it. ## Deliberately left out - **The version manager.** It has a home to live in now (`versions/`, `bin/`, `version`), but it is its own PR. - **`fzf` integration.** The built-in has to be complete on its own; an optional dependency that is really a requirement is a lie. Preferring `fzf` when it is on PATH can be added later without changing anything here. - **Highlighting the matched characters.** The scorer returns the positions for it; the picker does not use them yet. ## Checks `vp run workspace:ci` green. 202 tests in `slidx_cli`, up from 114. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is enabled.

author: fabrice8
body:
Implements **W8** of [`.TODO/MODEL_ROUTING.md`](.TODO/MODEL_ROUTING.md).

## Three findings

**1. The table can't stay current from inside the engine.** Of the ~23 models a serious cost model names, **20 had no row**. Prices change on a vendor's schedule, differ per account, and are ~0 self-hosted — an npm release is the wrong instrument for tracking them.

**2. `__default__` made unpriced models *look* priced.** Anything unrecognised was billed at Sonnet's `$3/$15`. For a budget model at `$0.14/$0.28` that overstates output cost by **~54×**, reported with total confidence. A wrong number nobody doubts is worse than a missing one.

**3. Dollars were in simulation state and nothing read them.** `llm.cost_total_usd`, `llm.cost.<category>`, `llm.cost.fn.<function>` went into `commands.metrics`; the only consumer in the tree was a console runner, and `llm.cost.tick` has **zero subscribers**. Harmless-looking — but it meant a host editing its price table changed state bytes and broke replay-equivalence over a number that influenced nothing.

## The line

> **Tokens are a physical fact of a call. Dollars are the host's accounting over that fact.**

| Stays in state | Moves to telemetry |
|---|---|
| `llm.prompt_tokens_*`, `llm.completion_tokens_*`, `llm.total_calls`, per-category tokens | `llm.cost_total_usd`, `llm.cost_this_tick_usd`, `llm.cost_avg_per_tick_usd`, `llm.cost.<category>`, `llm.cost.fn.<function>` |

Cost still reaches the host **every call** on the existing ledger path (`onRecord` → the stem's transport bridge) — where it was already being consumed.

**Consequence:** host prices have *no determinism surface*. They can differ between a recording and its replay and the run still reproduces byte-for-byte.

## Changes

- **`WillLLMConfig.providers`** — one declaration per provider carrying `apiKey`, `baseUrl` and `prices` together. The stem splits it: prices → `TokenTracker`, credentials → the LLM transport, so **pricing never enters the call path**. This also supplies the credential map the routing seam needed.
- **Host prices win** over the built-in table, matched through the same id normalisation — so a host can price models the engine has never heard of (`kimi-k2.5`, `qwen3.7-plus`, …).
- **`__default__` removed.** Unpriced ⇒ cost 0, `priced: false` on the ledger record, one warning per model id. The built-in table stays as a zero-config convenience, never a source of truth.
- **`thin-shim`** reads cost off the tracker via the existing public `getWillCognition()` — no new API.

## Behaviour changes

- `resolvePricing()` returns `null` for an unknown model instead of a `$3/$15` default.
- Cost metrics no longer appear in simulation state.

The existing pricing test that pinned the old default is **updated with the rationale**, not deleted — it now asserts `null` and carries a comment explaining the ~54× overstatement it used to permit.

## Verification

13 new tests: no cost keys in state, cost still readable in-process, host override, pricing an unknown-to-engine model, normalization matching, `priced` true/false, and the provider-map split (including that serialized credentials contain no price data).

Suite **1215 pass · 2 skip · 0 fail**. Typecheck and build clean. No commercial vocabulary in shipped source.

## Related issue

N/A

## Summary

With the Workspace rail's **Browser** tab active, opening the **Share** dialog rendered it *underneath* the page. The embedded browser is a native Electron `WebContentsView` painted over the renderer DOM, so no CSS z-index can put a modal above it.

- The browser-view registry gains a `setOverlaySuppressed(suppressed)` flag that hides the active view **in place** (`setVisible`, not detach — the page keeps running and reappears instantly when the overlay closes). It's re-applied on every attach, so a view activated or swapped in while an overlay is open attaches hidden.
- Exposed over IPC (`omnigent:browser-set-overlay-suppressed`) and the preload bridge (`browserSetOverlaySuppressed`).
- A new ref-counted `useSuppressBrowserView(open)` hook wires the share dialog's open state to the bridge in `AppShell`; overlapping overlays can share it without unhiding early. No-op on the web build and on desktop shells that predate the browser bridge.

**ELI5:** the browser tab is a real second browser window glued on top of the app, so the share popup was opening *behind* it. Now the glued-on window ducks out of sight while the popup is open and pops back when it closes.

```
share dialog opens
  AppShell: useSuppressBrowserView(shareOpen)
    └─ preload: browserSetOverlaySuppressed(true)
         └─ IPC: omnigent:browser-set-overlay-suppressed
              └─ registry.setOverlaySuppressed(true) → activeView.setVisible(false)
share dialog closes → same path with false → activeView.setVisible(true)
```

## Test Plan

- `node --test` in `web/electron` — 226 pass, including 6 new registry tests: hide/restore on suppress toggle, attach-hidden while suppressed, hidden across active-view swaps, re-show after suppression cleared while detached, no-throw with no active view / on views without `setVisible`.
- `vitest run src/hooks/useSuppressBrowserView.test.tsx` — 5 new tests: suppress on open, restore on close/unmount, no bridge calls while closed, ref-counted overlapping overlays, no-op on older shells.
- Live-Electron harness (real `BrowserWindow` + `WebContentsView`s on the repo's Electron 42, driving the actual `browserViewRegistry` module): all 7 runtime checks pass, including `getVisible()` flipping with suppression and attach-while-suppressed staying hidden.
- Pre-existing note: `pnpm --filter web run type-check` / some jest-dom-matcher suites fail identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout in my environment (jest-dom matcher registration), unrelated to this change.

## Demo

Composited captures from the live-Electron harness (a DOM "share modal" plus a real `WebContentsView` page, rendered exactly as the compositor layers them):

*Before — Browser tab page paints over the open share modal; After — with suppression the modal is visible while the dialog is open.*

<!-- drag in: 1-browser-tab-covers-modal.png / 2-modal-visible-while-suppressed.png -->

- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Test / CI
- [ ] Breaking change

## Test coverage

- [ ] Integration tests added / updated

## Coverage notes

Manual verification = the live-Electron harness described in the Test Plan: real `WebContentsView`s attached to a `BrowserWindow`, asserting `getVisible()` across suppress → restore → swap-while-suppressed, plus before/after screenshots. The compositing behavior itself (native view above DOM) can't be exercised from jsdom/node unit tests.

body:
Closes FAC-38 — https://linear.app/adamslinear/issue/FAC-38/friends-named-collectible-cones-conga-line-follow-hud-counter

All five gates green (`typecheck`, `build`, `lint`, `test` 145/145, `test:e2e` 7/7, verified stable across three consecutive full runs).

**One item needs your attention:** I created `e2e/tmp-rm-check.spec.ts` as a throwaway to verify the `prefers-reduced-motion` path renders correctly (it does — convoy, roster and flourish all stay legible with animation off). It has served its purpose and should be deleted, but file deletion via Bash is blocked in this environment, so I couldn't remove it. Please run `rm e2e/tmp-rm-check.spec.ts` before committing — it's untracked, so `git clean -f e2e/tmp-rm-check.spec.ts` also works. Note the repo already contains a similarly-named pre-existing `e2e/tmp-skel.spec.ts` which is tracked and should be left alone.

## Summary

I added Gary's cone-friends as a second consumer of ticket 02's entity abstraction rather than a parallel implementation: a new `EntityField` in `src/game/entities/friends.ts` supplies spawn cadence, lane choice and pickup scoring, and collection runs through the exact same swept `findHit` predicate that flattens Gary — only the `kind` and the consequence differ. The five named cones live as pure data in `src/game/friends/roster.ts`, indexed by `variant` on both sides of the seam so a friend can never be drawn as a different cone from the one you collided with, and `src/game/friends/conga.ts` implements the trailing line as a **path** follow (Gary drops `{distance, x}` breadcrumbs; each member samples a fixed distance back and eases on) rather than a spring chain — a chain low-passes the leader's motion once per link, so by the fifth friend a lane change becomes an invisible wobble, whereas path-sampling makes every member perform the same swerve later, which is what a conga line actually looks like. Three deliberate rule choices are documented in the README: friends close at exactly `TRAFFIC_APPROACH` so the existing no-overtaking fairness guarantee still holds across both fields (otherwise a car could catch a friend and turn a reward into bait); friends *may* take the last free lane, unlike traffic, because a reward on the only open line is a gift rather than a wall; and pickups resolve outside the spawn-grace window, since grace exists to prevent unfair deaths, not to withhold rewards. On the presentation side the HUD gains a docked **convoy roster rail** — an instrument-dense manifest of the cast that lights each chip in its own token colour (`--friend-1..5` in `index.html` pinned to `FRIEND_TINTS` in `theme.ts`, the same two-layer pinning the accent already uses), plus a tinted name flourish on collect and a game-over recap of who came along. The committed idea is that the convoy reframes the shot: the chase rig cranes up and back as the line grows, with `CONGA_PULLBACK > 1` because the tail grows *toward* the camera, and the lift matters more than the pull-back — from the default low pose you look straight down the line and a six-friend convoy reads as one lumpy mass. I verified this visually and iterated on the framing three times against real screenshots. Reduced motion is honoured throughout without ever removing information (the pickup halo stays lit at fixed opacity, the flourish still names the friend, it just fades instead of travelling). Finally, I consolidated the e2e coverage into a single continuous arc — collect → restart → collect again → crash — after discovering that three additional parallel WebGL contexts destabilised the pre-existing timing-sensitive near-miss test; one run is both cheaper and the truer test, since it exercises a sequence three independent fresh-boot tests never would.

author: nwparker
body:
Cherry-picks the three merged AI Vault workspace-switch perf fixes onto `1.4.161-rc.0-release-prep`, on top of #11303 which is already on this branch (`b85e267352`).

All three applied cleanly with no conflicts, `-x` recorded on each.

| cherry-pick | from main | what |
|---|---|---|
| `8354f7ba02` | `c5102e1262` (#11311) | regression guards + paint-latency tool |
| `b018569303` | `6cc579a48c` (#11314) | scope-path dedupe — 189.7ms → 0.8ms |
| `4d778b9390` | `b4b3bcdb84` (#11317) | resume lookups via the shared worktree index |

## Why these belong in the release

The user-visible symptom was a 1–2s freeze when clicking a workspace card with the Agent Session History panel open, at real scale (1124 workspaces / 500 sessions).

`a1a78da878` (#10841) is what made it visible — it added an unconditional `.normalize('NFC')` to `normalizeRuntimePathForComparison`, the innermost function in what were several O(sessions × worktrees) loops. #10841 shipped in 1.4.160, so the regression is live for users on the current release.

#11303 fixed the largest piece (the session map rebuilds). These three close out the rest:

- **#11314** is the substantive one — `deriveAiVaultScopeSessionPaths` still followed `activeWorktree`, so it ran on every switch and was still quadratic: deduping re-normalized the whole accumulator on each insert (~632k NFC calls at 1124 workspaces).
- **#11317** replaces three linear worktree scans with the existing WeakMap-cached index (net -4 lines).
- **#11311** is test-only plus a benchmark tool.

Combined, vault work on a workspace switch goes from ~1s to ~2.5ms.

## Verification on this branch

Not just "applied cleanly" — re-verified against the release branch itself:

- **7988 tests pass** across `right-sidebar/`, `lib/`, and `shared/`
- `tsc --noEmit -p config/tsconfig.tc.web.json` clean
- `deriveAiVaultScopeSessionPaths` measured at **0.7ms** on this branch against a real 1124-worktree profile (was ~190ms)

## Risk

Low. #11314 was verified byte-identical to the previous implementation (contents *and* ordering) across 156 scenario/option combinations — including NFD/NFC, WSL UNC, prior-path claims, and separator edge cases — and carries fail-first regression guards. #11317 is a swap to a helper already used the same way in `connection-owner-resolution.ts`. #11311 adds no production code.

NFC folding semantics from #10841 are untouched throughout — the same normalization runs, just not inside the hot loops.
