author: florianmousseau
body:
`el.store = handle` on an element whose class does not exist yet writes an **own property** on the instance. Once the class is defined, that own property answers first and shadows the accessor for good: the setter never runs, the widget never learns it has a store, and it sits there shut, or open and empty, with nothing in the console to say why.

Any host that loads `defineSelfstoreWidgets()` lazily hits this - a dynamic import, a framework effect, a script at the end of the body - and the symptom points nowhere near the cause. The workaround each host reinvents is a boolean that gates every assignment until the definitions have landed; that boolean should not exist.

Widgets now hand those properties back on connect: each own property a prototype accessor was meant to answer is deleted and set again through the accessor. Only those, so a field a host hangs on the element is left alone.

Two deliberate choices, both commented where they bite:

- a plain function rather than a method, because happy-dom calls `connectedCallback` without swapping the prototype, and a function is a harmless no-op there instead of a crash;
- called from `connectedCallback` rather than the constructor, because on an upgrade the base constructor runs BEFORE the subclass field initializers, which would wipe whatever the setter had just stored.

The end-to-end version cannot be tested here: happy-dom does not upgrade elements created before `customElements.define`, it merely calls their callback on a plain HTMLElement. So the test drives the mechanism on the state a real upgrade leaves behind, across all six widgets and each one's main property (not all of them take a store). The real path was verified in a browser against a host that loads the widgets from an effect.

Version bumped to 1.7.3 with its CHANGELOG section. No API change, no new dependency.

author: dash0-dev[bot]
body:
## Summary

Introduces a `reviewer-comment-relevance` LoreKit memory bucket that lets the `reviewer` and `pr-reviewer` agents learn — from resolved and dismissed PR comments — which finding patterns are actually relevant for a specific repository. The pipeline continuously gets better the more PRs it reviews.

This mirrors Cursor's improvement loop: each outcome (fixed, won't fix, ignored at merge) writes a scoped signal to LoreKit. On the next review run in the same repo, those signals suppress recurring noise and reinforce reliably-resolved patterns before any comment reaches GitHub.

## Changes

- **`agents/shared/rules/comment-relevance-memory.md`** — new shared rule defining the schema, read path (Step 2.2 in both agents), write path (from `implement-suggestion` Phase 7 / `--watch` and from `outcome-learning.md` gh-api fallback), and promotion rule (3× concordant signals → surface a `.review.yaml` filter suggestion)
- **`agents/reviewer.md`** — loads `reviewer-comment-relevance` memories at Step 0.7 alongside `reviewer-lessons`; new Step 2.2 (relevance-memory filtering) runs before filter suppression; Quality Gate table gains three new rows
- **`agents/pr-reviewer.md`** — loads memories at Step 1.0; new Step 2.2; Quality Gate summary updated
- **`skills/workflow/implement-suggestion/SKILL.md`** — Phase 7 outcome-emit now writes both the existing `review-outcomes` bus AND a new `reviewer-comment-relevance` record per comment; `--watch` mode emits both per iteration; prerequisites table updated
- **`agents/shared/rules/outcome-learning.md`** — fallback gh-api path (signals a/b/c) also writes `reviewer-comment-relevance`
- **`agents/shared/rules/review-outcomes.md`** — documents coexistence with the new bucket
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — inventory updated for `implement-suggestion`, `reviewer`, `pr-reviewer`, and `persistent-memory` (bucket list)

## How the loop works

```
PR reviewed by reviewer / pr-reviewer
      ↓
implement-suggestion applies / dismisses comments
      ↓  (Phase 7 outcome-emit)
reviewer-comment-relevance written to LoreKit (repo::{owner}/{repo})
      ↓
Next review run on same repo
      ↓  (Step 0.7 / Step 1.0)
Memories loaded → Step 2.2 applied
      ├── not-relevant ≥ 3×  → DROP the finding
      ├── not-relevant 1–2×  → DOWNGRADE to nitpick
      └── relevant ≥ 2×      → PROMOTE (terminal annotation)
```

Three resolution outcomes carry signal:
- **Fixed** (`relevant`) — author pushed a commit addressing the comment, or `implement-suggestion` applied it
- **Won't fix** (`not-relevant`) — explicit decline in thread (`won't fix`, `by design`, 👎) or `/critical` Must-fix raised
- **Ignored at merge** (`weak-not-relevant`) — PR merged with thread open, no fix, no decline

LoreKit is optional — if `memory.*` tools are not connected the entire loop is a silent no-op.

## What changed

Behavior-preserving refactor across `src/`, `test/`, CI, and docs — 19 commits, one concern per commit.

### src/ (10 commits)

- New shared modules: `error-chain.ts` (cause-chain walking previously duplicated in `cli.ts`/`index.ts`, plus the 6× repeated `err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)`), `metadata/renderable.ts` (renderable-entity predicate previously repeated 4×), `render/column-markers.ts`, and `defaults.ts` (single source for the `'Database Schema'` default title)
- Decomposed the three 100+ line functions: `buildColumns`/`buildConstraints` (`model/diagram.ts`), `buildDocumentModel` (`model/build.ts`), `loadOrmOptions` (`cli.ts`) — call order and output pinned by existing tests
- Dropped the dead `EntityModel.isPivot`/`isEmbeddable` flags (not re-exported from the public API)
- Unified the duplicated JSDoc block parsers behind one adapter and replaced the O(n×m) source-binding scan with prebuilt lookup maps

### test/ (7 commits)

- Moved the 14 `buildDiagramModel` describes out of `render/mermaid.test.ts`/`model/build.test.ts` into `test/model/diagram.test.ts`, matching the documented layout
- New `test/helpers/`: `makeTempDir` (8 hand-rolled temp-dir setups), fixture pipeline, `makeEntityMeta`/`pkProperty` (59 inline metadata literals), `makeJsDocResult`, `inMemorySqliteOptions`, shared fixture paths
- Centralized mock cleanup via `restoreMocks: true`, standardized `node:` imports

### CI / docs (2 commits)

- Removed the inline e2e smoke step duplicated by `test/e2e/cli-smoke.test.ts`
- AGENTS.md now documents `model/diagram.ts`, `source-path.ts`, the new modules, and the full test layout

## Why

`src/` and `test/` had accumulated duplicated logic and oversized functions that made focused changes risky; the test suite re-implemented the same fixtures and temp-dir handling per file.

## Impact

No behavior change. Public API exports, CLI stdout/stderr/exit codes, and warning/error strings are unchanged.

## Validation

- `npm run lint` / `npm run format:check` / `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run test` — 334 tests (baseline 316 + 13 new helper unit tests + 5 from #89 after rebase)
- `npm run build` && `npm run test:pack`
- `npm run example:erd` then `git diff examples/ERD.md` → empty diff (generated output is byte-identical)
- Branch rebased onto latest `main` (includes #89 atomic-write; its new tests adapted to the shared `makeTempDir` helper)

author: matlan1
body:
Repo-wide sweep of every regex applied to model output or remote/fetched text,
authorised after the six `py/polynomial-redos` alerts closed in #852 turned out
to under-cover the defect class.

**CodeQL flagged 6 patterns. The sweep found 11.** The extras are not a long tail
of the same thing - three of them say something about how this class hides.

## Measured, end to end through the real functions

| site | witness | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jobs/webtool.py` `_WRAP_RE` | `<tool_call>` + 4,000 spaces | 30.0s | 0.0002s |
| `jobs/webtool.py` `_THINK_RE` | `'<r >'` x 8,000 (32 KB) | 1.22s | 0.0017s |
| `jobs/webtool.py` `_top_level_objects` | `'{'` x 16,000 | 2.84s | 0.0000s |
| `jobs/webtool.py` `_FENCE_RE` | ` ``` ` + 50,000 tabs | quadratic | 0.0049s |
| `rag/extract.py` docx attribute spans | `'<w:br'` x 20,000 (97 KB) | **16.21s** | 0.0021s |
| `rag/extract.py` docx run extraction | `'<w:t'` x 20,000 (78 KB) | 1.69s | 0.0011s |
| `_log_digest.py` `_LOG_LINE_RE` | 8,000 spaces, no colon | 0.594s | 0.0002s |
| `coder/parser.py` marker-variant body | `'<tool_call>{{'` x 5,000 | 2.08s | 0.0060s |
| `coder/tools/files.py` edit fallback | 16 KB file vs 8 KB `old` | 0.646s | bounded |

## The three that matter beyond the numbers

**`_top_level_objects` is not a regex.** It is a hand-rolled brace scanner in
`webtool.py` with the identical many-start-positions defect - every unmatched
`{` scans to end-of-text. No regex-shaped query could ever have flagged it, which
is the concrete reason "close the six alerts" was not the same job as "fix the
class".

**`rag/extract.py` had already been hardened for exactly this.** Its comments
describe fixing a quadratic `<w:p\b.*?</w:p>` that burned ~135s. That pass fixed
the CONTENT group (`[^<]*` instead of `.*?`) and left the ATTRIBUTE group
(`[^>]*`) with the same shape. A hardening pass that fixes one class in a pattern
and not its sibling is how this survived a round of this very work. It is also
the only site here reached by a crafted **.docx** rather than by model output - a
DoS on document ingestion.

**`webtool.py` was a second copy** of two patterns the coder's parser had already
been fixed for, in a different package. Nothing flagged the copy.

## Also fixed: a regression from #852

The marker-variant (`<|tool_call>`) body was tempered against the marker in #852,
which silently dropped a real case - the coder editing its own parser docs or
test fixtures emits a `write_file` whose CONTENT contains `<tool_call>`. The body
is now brace-matched with a string-aware scan bounded by the last `}`, so a
marker inside a JSON string is understood rather than excluded. A differential
fuzz over 19,914 cases confirms no call the previous pattern recovered is lost.

Two wrong turns are recorded in the code comments because both are easy to
repeat: a per-marker forward scan (19.3s - **worse** than the regex it replaced)
and a global brace map (poisoned by a stray quote in prose, losing real calls).

## Not in this PR, deliberately

`tool_grep` and `tool_search_replace` compile a regex **the model supplies**,
which is exponential rather than polynomial and needs a timeout plus input caps -
a different remedy, already authorised, shipping separately. You cannot
de-ambiguate a pattern you did not write.

## Verification

`tests/test_redos_sweep_bounds.py` (new) carries two assertions per site: a
wall-clock bound on the witness, and a semantic check that real input still
parses - well-formed .docx, real log lines with colons in the message, wrapped
and fenced and bare tool calls, `<think>` stripping. The edit-fallback test
asserts the **decline** rather than the speed, since a bound that happened to be
fast for another reason would pass a timing-only check, and a companion test
proves the exact-match path is still uncapped so the bound costs a convenience
and not a capability.

author: rjbruin
body:
## Summary
Implements [docs/story-dedup-spec.md](docs/story-dedup-spec.md), following on from #195. Editions were re-reporting stories earlier editions had covered.

The cause is structural, not carelessness: ingest creates several `NewsItem` rows per story (four for one Claude Cowork story, two with byte-identical titles from different sources), so an item can be a genuinely new row while the story is old. The agent's only defence was a wall of its own prose headlines — fuzzy recall that fails silently.

**Part A — coverage becomes a first-class record**
- `coverage.document_references` / `norm_url` promoted to public.
- New `AgentMemory` `coverage` kind mirroring `quick_hits` — **no migration** — written alongside it in `build_summary` from the scope and document already in hand. Retained on the dedup lookback rather than the shorter headline window, which would delete half the corpus the matcher needs.
- `manage.py backfill-coverage` so the feature works immediately instead of after a retention window accumulates.
- Surfaced as an `ALREADY COVERED` prompt section and a `read_coverage` tool.

**Part B — continuing stories flagged on the items themselves**
- `app/services/story_dedup.py` scores in-scope items against recent prior coverage with TF-IDF + cosine, the same classical approach as `app/tagging/nb.py`. Two tiers: `likely_duplicate` at ≥0.52 or title-only ≥0.90, `possible_follow_up` at ≥0.35 — calibrated with `scripts/dedup_report.py` (10/10 precision at 0.52, ~2.5 flags per edition at 0.35).
- Flags are **pushed** onto every item in `list_scope_items` rather than exposed as a tool, since an optional lookup reproduces the silent-recall failure this exists to remove. Items with no match are omitted entirely, so they cost no tokens.
- Any internal failure degrades to no flags — a broken deduper must never block generation.

## Two fixes found by running against a copy of production
- **Revisions exclude their own edition chain.** `revise_edition` re-runs over the same window when the parent's coverage record already exists, so every item the parent featured came back flagged as a duplicate of itself — which would have told the agent to drop the whole edition. Records now carry `run_id`; `revise_edition` excludes `revision_chain(parent_run)`.
- **The backfill respects the retention window.** It was writing records for every edition ever generated, which startup pruning then deleted, making repeat runs look non-idempotent (9 written, 9 skipped, every time). Now genuinely idempotent.

## Test plan
- [x] Full suite passes (540, up from 521) — 19 new tests in `tests/test_story_dedup.py`
- [x] Regression fixture built from the real production failure (two rows, identical titles, both ran)
- [x] Backfill run twice against a copy of production: 9 records written, then 0 written / 9 skipped
- [x] End-to-end against production data: 7 of 68 in-scope items flagged on the latest edition, 61 carrying no flag; verified the exact JSON the agent receives

Part C (a cheap LLM arbiter over flagged pairs) remains deliberately out of scope — B's output is shaped as its input if we want it later.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: jolars
body:
Claude Code on the web starts from a container with Rust, Python, and Node but none of the tooling `devenv.nix` provides locally, so every session paid for a cold `cargo fetch` and had no R, task runner, mdbook, or air. This adds a `SessionStart` hook so a web session lands in a working dev environment deterministically, mirroring the one fatou already uses.

## What it does

`.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`, registered in `.claude/settings.json`. It gates on `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE`, so a local devenv shell exits immediately and is untouched. Tiers:

| Tier | Provides | Pinned by |
|---|---|---|
| CLI tools | go-task 3.45.4, mdbook 0.5.4, air 0.11.0 | release tag + SHA-256 |
| Rust | `cargo fetch`, `cargo build --all-targets`, clippy warm-up | `Cargo.lock` / `rust-toolchain.toml` |
| R | R 4.6.1 with roxygen2 8.0.0, jsonlite, commonmark, styler | nixpkgs snapshot URL |
| Dev tools | hyperfine, jq, jarl, cargo-audit, cargo-deny | nixpkgs snapshot URL |
| Node | `editors/code` dependencies | `package-lock.json` |

Only `cargo fetch` is treated as required; every later tier warns and continues rather than failing the session. Each step is idempotent, so a cached container image short-circuits it — a second run finishes in ~17s.

## Notes on the pins

- **air is pinned deliberately, not incidentally.** The air-compat gauge's numbers move with the comparator's version, so leaving it floating would make `AIR_COMPAT.md` non-reproducible. Bumping it should be a conscious act. This is the air *CLI*, distinct from the `air_r_parser` crate the parser harness uses, which `Cargo.lock` pins by rev.
- **Pinning the nixpkgs snapshot pins roxygen2.** That matters more here than convenience: the oracles compare against pins minted by a specific roxygen2, and a floating one would drift silently.
- **The R package set mirrors `devenv.nix` minus `languageserver`**, which only serves interactive R editing.
- **`api.github.com` returns 403 here** (GitHub access is scoped to this repo), but release *asset* URLs are reachable — so tags are pinned exactly rather than resolved through `latest`.
- **`nix build --print-out-paths` emits one line per output.** The R wrapper splits off a `-man` output, so the hook picks the store path that actually carries the probe binary instead of taking the first line.

R stays firmly optional: every R-backed test is already `#[ignore]`d, and `task roxygen-projector` — the CI-safe conformance gate — is pure Rust and needs no R at all.

## Validation

Run in a web container, from a clean cache:

- `cargo fmt -- --check` clean; `task lint` clean.
- `cargo test --test formatter` (21 passed).
- `task roxygen-projector` passes (pure-Rust gate).
- `task roxygen-oracle` passes **212/212 Rd-preserving** against the nix-provisioned R — the tier this PR exists for.
- `task air-compat` runs against the pinned air.
- `task docs-gen` + `mdbook build docs` render the book.
- The `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` gate exits cleanly when unset.

## One thing worth a look, unrelated to this change

Running the gauges surfaced two stale generated artifacts, which I reverted to keep this PR focused:

- `AIR_COMPAT.md` records 122 corpus files against today's 181, and regenerating it with air 0.11.0 shows a **third unexplained divergence** (`air_pipelines`, 95.8% line similarity) alongside the two already queued. Per the triage rule that is either a bug to adopt or a deviation to record — your call.
- `docs/src/version.md` still says v0.12.0 (current is v0.13.0); `task docs-gen` refreshes it.

author: sidharth1027
body:
## What this is

**Story 2.0-D1 — Financial Services Cloud Pack, subtask T2 (Detector set over FSC objects).**

Five FSC detectors, the ingest surface they read, and the externalised configuration holding their firing thresholds. Composed from existing detector machinery — four of five are recompositions, one is new.

## The detector set (~80% reuse, as the story intends)

| Detector | Composed from | What carried forward |
|---|---|---|
| `FSC_SERVICING_REQUEST_RECURRENCE` | `repetition.py` | the repeated-unit-of-work shape + breadth qualifier |
| `FSC_REFERRAL_HANDOFF_FRICTION` | `handoff_friction.py` | **`THRESHOLD = 1.5` unchanged** as `min_avg_hops` |
| `FSC_APPROVAL_REVIEW_CYCLE` | `approval_delay.py` + `approval_bottleneck.py` | dwell time *and* pending depth, as two threshold legs |
| `FSC_SERVICE_QUEUE_AGEING` | **new** — but modelled on `cloud_ops_queue_ageing` | the per-queue-own-baseline departure rule |
| `FSC_CROSS_OBJECT_REWORK` | `cross_system_echo.py` | **`THRESHOLD = 0.15` unchanged** as `duplicate_rate_threshold` |

Each module's docstring records what it was composed from *and what deliberately did not transfer* (e.g. `handoff_friction`'s `MIN_CASES = 50` is an org-wide case floor; the unit here is a referral *type*, of which an org has a handful, so 50 would mean the detector never fires — that rescaling is engineering judgement, not measurement).

**Two findings worth reviewing:**

1. **`approval_delay.py` and `approval_bottleneck.py` both declare `DETECTOR_ID = "APPROVAL_BOTTLENECK"`** on dev. Since UI labels are keyed by detector id, registering both under FSC would collapse their labels into one entry — so their two ideas ride one detector as two threshold legs rather than two detectors.
2. **Queue ageing has no global fallback.** A queue with no established baseline does *not* fire: there is nothing for it to be elevated against, and inventing a global mean is precisely the mistake the per-queue rule exists to prevent.

## The ingest surface — the real work

Before T2 there was **not a single `FinServ__` reference anywhere in the backend**. `discovery/ingest/fsc.py` reads `FinServ__Referral__c`, `FinServ__FinancialAccount__c` and their histories alongside the standard `Case` / `Account` / `ProcessInstance` reads, normalising them into ONE detector-visible block at `sf_data["fsc"]`.

**Tolerant field reads.** The documented ServiceNow failure mode — `sysparm_display_value=all` returning `{value, display_value}` while fixtures held plain scalars, so tests passed either way and the bug surfaced only in production — has a Salesforce analogue: parent traversal returns a *nested object* and is `null` whenever the lookup is empty. `_field()` resolves dotted paths, tolerates a null at any level, and unwraps a `{value, display_value}` envelope if a proxy ever introduces one. A record whose `RecordType` will not resolve is **counted as unresolved**, never assumed in *or* out of scope.

**Offline is now DB-free.** The vault lookup is a database read, so attempting it offline made an offline run wait on (and be shaped by) database reachability. `_get_client()` short-circuits before any credential resolution when not live — offline stays deterministic and fast.

## Calibration is provisional, and says so at runtime

Every threshold lives in `financial_services_cloud_pack_config.json` with a `_basis` recording where it came from, and the file's `calibration_status` is readable via `is_provisional()` rather than only in a comment.

⚠️ **Passing AC1 does not validate these numbers.** The seed and the thresholds were authored together, so the test proves the wiring fires — not that the calibration is right. The config's own `_meta` states this and lists the outstanding SME dependencies.

The config also carries an **org-configurable `scope` block** (service-process/household record types, closed statuses). The task asks to confirm the record types and picklist values the detectors branch on; that cannot be confirmed without a live FSC org, so rather than hardcoding a guess these are config — a differing customer org becomes a config edit. The *closed* set is matched rather than the open set, so an unrecognised org status reads as OPEN, the conservative direction for an ageing detector.

## The fixture is a scaffold, and says so

`fsc_sample.json` is **structurally faithful**: real query envelopes (`{totalSize, done, records}`), `attributes` blocks, nested relationship objects, real `FinServ__` API names, Salesforce datetime formats, and deliberate `null` relationships. Its `_meta` states plainly that it is not evidence the connector reads correctly.

Person fields (owners, contacts, actor names, household names) are present **on purpose** — a fixture scrubbed of them would make the AC5 leak test vacuous, and a test guards against exactly that.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — all five detectors fire on the seeded estate (9 findings), each carrying the four-part criterion. Enforced at the pack boundary in `runner.py`, deliberately **not** wrapped in `try/except`: a finding missing a part must fail the run rather than reach a report.
- **AC3** — FSC terminology is pack config. A test pins the config glossary against T1's label-file `_terminology` so the machine-readable and user-visible vocabularies cannot drift.
- **AC4** — zero engine changes: detectors emit the standard `DetectorResult`, a test asserts none imports a scorer/template/materialize module, and `calibration.impact_weights` is left **empty** for T3 rather than guessed (an invented weight silently ranks findings).
- **AC5** — absolute, and *tested rather than assumed*. The strongest available form: every person literal **present in the fixture** is asserted absent from every finding and from the normalised block. Plus narrative-level checks, since AC5 applies to prose as much as to structured fields.

`fsc_finding.py` exists separately from `cloud_ops_finding.py` for exactly one reason: **the aggregation floor**. The ITSM denylist (`assignee`, `caller`, `opened_by`…) contains none of FSC's person fields — no relationship manager, advisor, household member, `OwnedById`, `FinServ__PrimaryOwner__c` — so importing it would have produced a *passing* test that leaked every FSC person field that matters.

One subtlety the tests caught: `FinServ__TotalNumberOfMembers__c` matched the "…member…" person shape, but a **count** of people is exactly what AC5 permits (households as counts, never names), so `is_person_field` now treats aggregates as permitted.

## Also in this PR

- `packVersion` **1.0.0 → 1.1.0** — the first time T1's fingerprint guard fired in anger; pins updated in the same commit, which is the workflow that guard exists to force.
- The five detector ids mapped into `FOCUS_AFFINITY`, so the pack is first-class rather than invisible to Discovery Focus.
- `CLAUDE.md` kept in sync.

## Verification

- **201 tests pass** across the two FSC suites.
- **End to end:** an FSC run produces 9 opportunities from 5 detectors stamped `1.1.0`, with T1's labels resolving into titles/categories and the approval detector's compliance guardrail reaching the finding.
- **Multi-pack regression:** FSC + nCino stays separate — `{financial_services_cloud: 9, ncino: 5}`, own `packVersions`, no cross-pack merging — and nCino alone is unchanged at 5.

author: yashasviyadav30
body:
No tests, no CI, no licence, and a README making a claim that works against the repo. This fixes all four.

## Tests

**56 tests** over `tictactoe` and `minesweeper`, the two projects that are pure Python.

The minimax tests are properties, not examples:

- optimal play against itself **draws from every opening**
- optimal play **never loses** to an opponent playing the first legal square
- a position with exactly one saving move must find it
- a lost position must lose from *every* move

That last one came from a test of mine that failed. I asserted O blocks at `(0,2)` in `XX. / O.. / ...`, and got `(1,2)`. Checking the engine rather than my own reasoning:

```
['XX.', 'O..', '...']  O to move
    (0,2) -> value for X: 1
    (1,1) -> value for X: 1
    ... every move -> 1
```

O is already beaten there whatever it plays, so minimax's pick among equal moves is arbitrary — `actions()` returns a set. The position where blocking is genuinely forced is `XX. / .O. / ...`, where `(0,2)` is the only reply valued 0. Both cases are now tested, the second asserting the value rather than the square.

Minesweeper coverage: `Sentence` inference rules, mine subtraction from later counts, subset inference, empty-sentence pruning, and that `make_safe_move` never returns a played cell.

## CI

Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12. `traffic` and `attention` are excluded — TensorFlow, transformers and the GTSRB dataset don't belong in a CI run, and the README says so rather than leaving it unexplained.

## README

The old one called these "production-quality implementations" built "not to copy, but to truly understand", and never mentioned CS50AI.

`traffic`, `attention`, `minesweeper`, `tictactoe` are the CS50AI problem sets, in order. Anyone who has taken the course spots that immediately, and at that point the "production-quality" line costs more credibility than the repo gains.

Rewritten to say where the projects come from and what I added on top, which is the test suite. Also replaced the `capsule-render.vercel.app` banner: it's an external image that breaks the page whenever that service is down.

## Also

MIT `LICENSE`, `.gitignore`, `pytest.ini`, package markers.

## Verification

```
56 passed in 5.99s
```

body:
# Dynamic genre conditioning + conditioning monitor

**Part 1 of a 5-part training-core series** (#67 → #68 → #69 → #70 → #71). Merging in order keeps every diff small — each later PR currently shows its predecessors' commits until they merge.

**Dynamic genre conditioning.** Preprocessing now encodes BOTH the caption and the genre-tag text variant into each `.pt` (new optional keys — old tensors keep loading, `genre_ratio` semantics unchanged for them). Training then selects caption vs genre *per sample per step* according to `genre_ratio` (auto-detected from `preprocess_meta.json` when unset), replacing the old static per-sample choice frozen at preprocess time. This removes the systematic bias where a sample was forever caption-only or genre-only for the whole run. Requires re-preprocessing to benefit; degrades gracefully without it.

**Conditioning monitor.** `conditioning_type` flows from the dataset through collate into ProgressWriter events, and the training monitor shows live caption-vs-genre usage per batch. Also ports the target-loss scale/EMA telemetry to the Fabric trainer path (previously basic-loop only).

author: jjurado2026
body:
## El webhook de Seal no ha funcionado nunca

Ninguno de sus topics, desde que existe. Todos los handlers leen `payload.subscription`. Seal no manda eso: manda el objeto de suscripción **plano en la raíz** (`id`, `email`, `status`, `items`, `billing_attempts`, `log`, `failed_billing_attempt`, `customer_id`). Así que `payload.subscription` era siempre `undefined`, `syncSubscription` salía por su primer `if` y no hacía nada.

**Las dos pruebas, ambas de la columna `webhook_log.payload` que se añadió el día anterior:**

- **59 de 59** payloads guardados son planos. Cero tienen la clave `subscription`.
- **Tiempo medio de proceso: 7 a 16 ms** en todos los topics. Un handler que llama a Shopify por GraphQL y hace un upsert en Supabase no corre en 9 ms.

Sin esa columna esto era invisible: el webhook devolvía 200 y rellenaba `processed_at`.

**Qué llevaba años sin pasar en silencio:** la caché de suscripciones solo la escribían las visitas al Hub, el re-anclaje de cadencia solo aterrizaba por el drenaje del Hub y el cron, y la retirada del descuento del 15% solo por el barrido diario. Todos tenían red de seguridad por otro lado, y por eso nadie lo notó. El dunning del PR #75 no la tenía, y por eso salió a la luz.

## Cambios

**1. `subFromPayload`**, resolutor único. Acepta la forma plana y sigue aceptando la anidada por si Seal manda algún día lo que su doc implica. Si no reconoce la forma, **avisa por Slack**: el pecado original no fue la forma del payload, fue que fallar en silencio era posible.

**2. `customer_id` del payload**, verificado como el de Shopify (6 de 6 contra nuestra caché). Ahorra una llamada GraphQL por evento, ~4.000 al mes, y elimina el modo de fallo en que un hipo de Shopify tumbaba el webhook. **Pero solo como atajo:** `subscriptions.customer_id` es la clave de autorización del portal, así que si contradice la fila que ya tenemos se cae al lookup por email. Sin ese límite, el re-home 23505 escrito para reparar la reasignación de email la habría deshecho.

**3. `number_of_tries` (1..4).** `daysUntilCancel` se calcula, ya no está clavado en 3: la ventana de dedup hace que el primer evento que vemos pueda ser el intento 2 o 3, y prometerle tres días a quien se le cancela mañana es peor que no decir nada.

**4. `gatewayMessage`** sale del `billing_attempts` del mismo payload, que es donde Seal pone el texto real de la pasarela. Permite segmentar tarjeta caducada frente a rechazo de pasarela.

**5. Alertas a #incidencias**, pedidas por Juan. Al **tercer** cobro fallido ("Seal cancela al cuarto, mañana") y cuando Seal **ya** ha cancelado. No en cada fallo: hubo 41 en una mañana. La cancelación por dunning se detecta por el array `log`, porque `cancellation_reason` viene vacío en todas las guardadas. Requiere `SLACK_INCIDENTS_WEBHOOK_URL` en Vercel; mientras no esté, caen en el canal de alertas para no perderse.

**6. Evento `payment_method_updated`**, para que el flow de dunning deje de perseguir a quien ya arregló la tarjeta.

## Verificación

`tsc` limpio, `next build` correcto, `eslint` con los mismos 3 errores que la rama base.

Revisión adversarial de 17 agentes en 3 dimensiones: 0 confirmados por unanimidad, 5 descartados, y **2 divididos que resultaron reales** al comprobarlos y están corregidos en este PR (el fast path como clave de autorización, y `number_of_tries` leído y tirado).

**Three slots, and the count is forced rather than chosen.** The region reads as one contiguous block and is not: `CheckSlot::Database` (stage 4) already runs between the secret-dir leg and the inbox one, and `CheckSlot::Retention` (stage 2) between the inbox leg and the endpoint URLs. Constraint (b) fixes output order by slot ordinal, so one slot cannot span a slot already sitting inside it — **the two earliest migrations decided this stage's shape.** A reader who has now seen 5b add zero slots, 5c add one and 6 add three must not read a trend: each number is a property of its region's interleave.

`warnIfDirInsecure()` was **extracted, not copied**, into `DirectoryPermissions::warnIfInsecure()` — it had exactly two call sites and both migrated in this stage, so the alternative was two copies of one permission verdict (canon #5, at the threshold rather than past it).

Both dir checks read `config()` **raw** rather than `CheckContext`. The context field is narrowed for its consumers (`is_string($v) ? $v : null`) and is wrong for a leg reporting on the *setting*: the empty string is a string, and a `BRIDGE_CONFIG_DIR` of literal `true` reaches `env()` as a bool and arrives as null. It is also simply **empty at `Install`-slot time** — `handle()` assigns it later, while building the per-agent scan.

## Verification

- **Full suite green at the head commit** — `1644 + 24 = 1668` tests, `3916 + 66 = 3982` assertions, exit 0. The delta is exactly the five new test classes; no existing test file was modified or deleted.
- **Golden byte-identical with `UPDATE_GOLDEN` unset** — 33 tests / **66 assertions** (the assertion count is the load-bearing half: a regenerating run reports green with fewer).
- **14/14 mutation proofs**, each reverting one load-bearing guard: mutant RED on its named test, restored byte-identical, tree clean after the run.
- **Real-surface** stdout+stderr diff against `origin/dev`: byte-identical, sentinel-controlled.
- phpstan L7 (`-c phpstan-laravel.neon`) 0 · pint clean · `bin/check-doc-refs.php` clean.
- Coverage artifact regenerated on a detached copy: **35 → 29 predicates** (`28 observed · 0 observed-via-abort · 1 UNOBSERVED`), 9 depart / 3 arrive, conservation `35 − 9 + 3 = 29` passed, zero surviving predicates changed status.

`observed-via-abort` reaches **zero for the first time in the program — by departure, not promotion**. Both its entries were this stage's own migrations; the golden harness did not learn to tell their branches apart, they left the region it measures. What stands behind them now is a unit test with a mutation proof per predicate, which is strictly stronger.

## Doc-sync

`docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md` gains the Stage 6 result section; **its stage table's `6–7` row is corrected in this PR** and split into `6 ✅` + `7`. The old row enumerated two units and would have left **five** legs inline forever — and stage 8's whole premise is an exact inventory, so an under-enumerated row would hand it a green inventory over legs it had never looked at: the precise defect this program exists to remove, re-minted one level up. `CLAUDE.md`'s subfile-index row advances to "Stages 0–6 built". `CheckSlot`'s enum docblock gains the three cases.

## The measurement defect this stage found in itself

The card's own fixture accounting was written from the fixture *builders* rather than the *rendered corpus*, and was wrong twice. That shape — **a claim stated at a strength its evidence did not support** — recurred in this stage's own docblocks and in a **merged** prior stage, so it is filed as its own root-cause item, **card#5551** (8 instances, 7 corrected), which also corrects card#5547's prescribed fix wording because that wording propagates the same defect.

Two further instances were found by the post-fix adversarial pass and fixed here (`fc1e587`), both measured against the rendered corpus:

- `InstallConfigDirCheck` justified "no fixture renders the unset message" with *"every golden fixture resolves a config dir"* — measured **32 of 33**. The operative reason is set-ness, not resolution; read literally the old text also denied the one fixture the `does not exist` branch does have.
- `InstallSecretDirCheck` claimed the split-layout guard is *"false in all of them but one"* — measured **31 false, 1 true, and `secret-dir-unset` never reaches it at all** (the resolvability branch returns first).

**The datum that outranks the count: the shape survived a deliberate fix attempt.** An earlier replacement docblock re-minted it, caught on re-read before commit. So the fix is **mechanical, not a wording rule**: a sentence naming a test, fixture, or scope is unwritable until the measuring command has been run and read, and it then states the **selector**, not a conclusion. This supersedes card#5547's prescription.

## Filed, not fixed here

Output-neutral root-cause items deliberately kept out of a migration PR: **#5546** (shared-identities read twice), **#5547**, **#5548** (instrument launders a failed write), **#5549** (`CLAUDE_ARCHITECTURE.md` omits the `Check` package), **#5551**. 5547 + 5549 + 5551 are one doc batch after stage 7, 5551's rule first.

Noted, deliberately not edited: `CLAUDE_DECISIONS.md` B-17 still names `warnIfDirInsecure` by its pre-extraction name. The log is append-only, `check-doc-refs.php` passes, and the decision it records (warn-not-fail, both dirs, one shared helper) is unchanged — only the helper's name moved.

author: andrebrait
body:
Fixes #77

## What

Test-only. Three review findings against #35's coverage, all of them "verified by hand during review, pinned by nothing":

1. The equality premise asserted `assertNotEquals(System.identityHashCode(a), System.identityHashCode(b))`. Identity hash codes are not guaranteed distinct, so that was a proxy for the thing meant — now `assertNotSame`.
2. The round trip never called `XMLValidator.validateLogiqxDat`, which every other DAT round-trip test in the repo uses. A schema-invalid `header` emission would have passed.
3. Only a four-byte header was round-tripped, and only the parsed value was asserted — never the attribute text as written.

The round trip is now a matrix over the shapes a header can take, each asserting the emitted attribute text *and* the parsed value, and each validating the emitted document against the Logiqx schema:

| Shape | Emitted |
| --- | --- |
| absent | no `header=` attribute at all |
| empty | `header=""` |
| one byte | `header="1A"` (unspaced, as the old serializer's special case also did) |
| several bytes | `header="4E 45 53 1A"` |
| bytes a text format would have to escape (`0x0A`, `0x0D`) | `header="0A 0D"` |

## Behaviour-preserving, so no red run

Per `.agents/policy/testing.md`'s first principle, this is the refactor/prep case: it pins *existing* behaviour as an oracle and stays green across the change. There is no production change in this PR, so there is nothing that could have failed before it.

```
$ mvn -B -pl core -am test -Dtest=RomTest
[INFO] Tests run: 8, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 -- in RomTest
```

## Gates

```
$ sh scripts/agent/run-gates.sh --diff origin/master
GATE PASS: mvn -B -q verify
GATES: PASS
```

## Still open, deliberately

The issue also asks whether spaced upper-case hex is what real No-Intro DATs actually put in `header=`. No fixture in the tree carries the attribute and the Logiqx DTD/XSD declare it as unconstrained `CDATA`, so nothing here can settle it — these tests pin what the tool currently emits, which is the most that can be pinned without a real sample. If a real DAT says otherwise, the serializer and this matrix change together.

body:
Item 7 of the red-team review, plus a correction to one of my own errors in the same doc.

## The recess window is about a week

| | |
|---|---|
| **Senate** | State work period **Aug 10 → Sep 11**. In session the first week of August. Returns **Sep 14**. |
| **House** | In districts for *"nearly all of August and October"* ahead of the midterms. One session week **Aug 31 → Sep 3**, then the Labor Day week off. |

Sources: [Roll Call — Senate](https://rollcall.com/2025/11/19/senate-calendar-2026-midterm-election/), [Roll Call — House](https://rollcall.com/2025/11/18/house-2026-calendar-midterm-elections/), [Bloomberg Government](https://news.bgov.com/bloomberg-government-news/house-releases-2026-calendar-with-august-october-recesses).

The exact first day of the House district period is **not pinned** — pressgallery.house.gov blocks automated fetches. The [official PDF](https://www.majorityleader.gov/uploadedfiles/119_legislative_schedule_2026_houseofrepresentatives.pdf) has it.

## It conflicts with the five-send pilot, and the conflict is real

Waiting for pilot replies costs several days — the entire remaining staffer window. You can't do both. Either send twenty unpiloted emails into the pre-recess crush from a domain with zero sending history, or hold them.

**Recorded recommendation: hold the twenty until Sep 14.**

## The two lists separate cleanly

Librarians aren't on the congressional calendar — their constraint is fall-semester prep, which argues for *sooner*.

| When | Who | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Now** | 5 librarians (pilot) | Learn the reply shape while timing is flexible |
| **This week** | rest of the librarians | Once the pilot returns and copy is adjusted |
| **Sep 14+** | all 20 staffers | Copy tested on real recipients; domain has six weeks of sending history |

The delay makes the staffer emails **better**, not merely later. That's the reason to accept it rather than a consolation for it.

## Also corrects an error of mine

The same doc asserted Vercel Web Analytics was **not enabled**, because the analytics API returned `404 Web Analytics not found`. That was reading a tool error as a fact about the project.

`/_vercel/insights/script.js` serves **200**, which Vercel only does for provisioned projects — and `@vercel/analytics/react` injects its tag client-side, so its absence from server HTML proves nothing either. Corrected to: verify in the dashboard, not through the API.

The section keeps the one caveat that *is* true — this audience sits on institutional networks that block third-party scripts, so the pageview count is a **floor**, not a measurement.

Also drops the superseded "check the recess calendar" note now that real dates replace it.

Docs only.

author: eijebong
body:
Generic worker likes to chown and chmod its config on start which is all fine and dandy until it's a file that is bind mounted in its container and it chowns the config to a user that isn't you. Then it breaks git by always creating a diff (since the mode of the file changes) and git breaks because it sees the change but can't read the file anymore.

```
error: open("docker/generic-worker-config.json"): Permission denied
fatal: cannot hash docker/generic-worker-config.json
```

This has annoyed me one too many times. Turns out that generic-worker-static was already doing something similar for worker-runner's config since #8520 (specifically
06c28e08df4bf1f087a64dbb2ce2f425270db1bc even if it doesn't mention it at all). I just copy/pasted the solution with
`s/worker-runner/generic-worker` since it's correct in this case too.

author: kasnder
body:
Addresses the battery and performance issues found while reviewing the accessibility service, plus the smaller findings from the same pass. Five commits, each independently reviewable.

## 1. Stop event delivery when there is nothing to block

**The highest-drain configuration was the default one, and it did no useful work.**

`configureAccessibilityService()` maps an empty target set to `packageNames = null`, which `AccessibilityServiceInfo` treats as *all packages*. Rules are opt-in — `isRuleEnabled` defaults to `false`, `isPackageDisabled` defaults to `true` — so this was the state of every fresh install after the user granted accessibility access and before they toggled anything.

In that state every content-change and scroll event from every app on the device woke the process, and each one scheduled a delayed clear that called `getRootInActiveWindow()` (a synchronous binder round-trip that materialises a window snapshot) to tear down overlays that did not exist.

- `eventTypes` is set to `0` when no rules are enabled, so the system stops dispatching to this process entirely. Toggling a rule re-arms the service through the existing static-instance `updateRules()` path, which does not depend on event delivery.
- The same treatment is applied while the screen is off, replacing the `screenOn` check that discarded events only after they had already been delivered.
- The delayed clear is skipped when no overlays, sentinels, or pause notification are outstanding.

Also fixes a bug found along the way: the clear path never cancelled the pause notification, so *"pause blocking for <app>"* lingered after the user had left that app — and the same-package guard in `showPauseNotification()` meant returning to the app could not refresh it.

## 2. Throttle and consolidate accessibility tree traversal

**Walk the tree once per pass instead of once per rule.** `processRootNode()` called `applyRule()` for every matching rule, and rules with neither a path nor a view id fell through to a full recursive walk. The bundled set ships six Instagram rules, one of which (`desc=reels tray container`) is desc-only, so an Instagram pass walked the whole tree from scratch on top of the per-rule work. Rules are now split by how they resolve — path and view id rules go straight to `matchPaths()` / `findAccessibilityNodeInfosByViewId()`, and only match-by-inspection rules are evaluated together in one shared walk. Every `getChild()` can cross back into the inspected app's process, so the traversal dominates the cost of a pass.

**Hold a floor between passes.** `scheduleProcessEvent()` coalesced onto a Choreographer frame callback, which bounds passes to the display refresh rate — not a meaningful limit for a full traversal, and in practice ~10–40 passes/sec while scrolling a feed. A 100ms floor is applied on top, still trailing-edge so the final state of a burst is always processed.

> The 100ms constant is deliberately conservative. Overlays track element bounds, so raising it trades scroll-tracking smoothness against CPU — too high and blocked content visibly leaks through before the overlay catches up. Worth tuning on a real device.

**Defer releasing the all-packages filter.** Attaching the first overlay switches package filtering to "all packages" and detaching the last switches it back, so blocked elements scrolling in and out of the viewport made `setServiceInfo()` thrash — and each call makes the system recompute event routing for every installed app. The release is now debounced by two seconds; re-acquiring or any explicit reconfigure cancels it.

## 3. Remove the dead layout dumper

`LayoutDumper` was gated behind `ENABLED = false`, so it was constructed and `start()`ed on every service connect only to return immediately. If the flag were ever flipped it would serialise the entire accessibility tree into a string and write it to logcat every two seconds — an expensive recurring traversal, and a privacy hazard, since the dump includes the text and content descriptions of everything on screen.

## 4. Trim per-reload and per-switch overhead

- **Cache the pause notification's app icon.** `getAppIcon()` did a PackageManager lookup, a drawable load and a full draw into a fresh `ARGB_8888` bitmap on the dispatch thread every time the user entered a target app. Now cached, including negative results.
- **Parse the bundled rules file in one call** instead of re-entering the parser with a single-element array per line. This also restores the parser's `//` comment-line feature for bundled rules, which per-line parsing discarded before it could apply. No behaviour change today — every rule in both flavours' files carries its own inline `comment=` and neither uses `//` lines.
- **Guard the parser's per-line debug logging** behind `isLoggable()`, so the string concatenation is not paid on every reload regardless of log level.
- Reuse the service's existing `ServiceConfig` instead of allocating one per picker rule change, and hoist `getChildCount()` out of the remaining loop conditions.

## 5. Key rule preferences on rule identity, not the raw rule string

Saved enable/pause state was keyed on `FilterRule.hashCode()`, i.e. `ruleString.hashCode()` — a hash of the entire raw line, **including `comment=`, `category=` and `color=`**. Editing any of those changes the key, so fixing a typo in a bundled rule's comment silently reset that rule for every existing user.

`FilterRule.identity()` now builds a string from the matching fields only (package, view id, content descriptions, class name, text, path), with descriptions sorted so the result does not depend on set iteration order. Preferences key on the first 64 bits of its SHA-256.

Existing installs are **migrated once** from `getRules()`, where the full rule set is known: legacy values are copied unless a value already exists under the new key, then legacy keys are removed and a prefs version is recorded. Without this an upgrade would silently reset every rule the user had enabled or paused.

## Testing

`./gradlew test` passes — 135 tests, 0 failures. Commit 5 adds 8 tests covering identity semantics (presentation edits preserve state, matching edits do not, desc order is irrelevant, distinct packages stay distinct) and migration (state carries over, legacy keys are cleared, newer state is not overwritten, it does not run twice).

There is no test coverage for the service itself, so commits 1–2 are behaviour-preserving by inspection rather than by test — same nodes tested against the same rules with the same visibility gating. The traversal restructuring and the overlay-tracking cadence both want verification on a real device against Instagram, WhatsApp and LinkedIn.

## Deliberately not changed

`notificationTimeout` stays at `100`. Raising it to 250–300ms was on the original list, but it interacts badly with commit 2: the traversal floor already caps the expensive work, and `notificationTimeout` only gates cheap event delivery to an already-running foreground process. Raising it to 250ms would make it the binding constraint on overlay tracking — slower than the 100ms floor deliberately chosen to stop blocked content leaking through during a scroll. It buys little now and costs responsiveness.

author: andrebrait
body:
Fixes #76

## What

`CommandLineProgressBar` draws into a fixed block of rows, and every draw path in the class returns the cursor to the top of that block. The thread-less failure line added in #37 was a bare `writer.printf(...)`: it moved the cursor down a row and never came back, so every later thread line rendered one row further off — once per failure — and it wrote outside the lock the other draw paths hold, so it could interleave mid-sequence with a worker's ANSI output.

The line now takes one row for itself (that is what the user reads) and then re-opens the block, inside the same `synchronized` as the rest. Before `init()` it still prints plainly: nothing is reserved at that point, which is exactly where the existing listing messages write.

## Red → green proof

Test file frozen byte-identical across both runs — `git hash-object cli/src/test/java/io/github/datromtool/cli/progressbar/CommandLineProgressBarCursorTest.java` = `b29527408bf881556cd8bf6b2a469e8dbf2d6447` at red time and at green time.

RED, executed against untouched production code (`git stash push -- cli/src/main`, run, `git stash pop`):

```
$ mvn -B -pl cli -am test -Dtest=CommandLineProgressBarCursorTest
[ERROR] Tests run: 1, Failures: 1, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
[ERROR]   CommandLineProgressBarCursorTest.aThreadLessFailureLeavesTheCursorWhereItFoundIt:82
  the bar must re-open its 3-row block after the line, so later thread lines still land on their own rows
```

GREEN, same test, zero edits:

```
[INFO] Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 -- in CommandLineProgressBarCursorTest
[INFO] Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 -- in CommandLineProgressBarSanitizationTest
[INFO] Tests run: 13, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 -- in ScanCommandTest
```

The test renders through a real jline terminal and reads the ANSI stream back: it counts newlines and cursor-line moves to assert the failure takes exactly its own row, then asserts the block is re-opened. It asserts the message is present first, so neither check can pass on an empty capture.

A note on how that assertion got its shape: the first version demanded *zero* net movement, which the fix could never satisfy — the message legitimately consumes a row. That was a wrong premise in the test, corrected before the red run recorded above; the invariant that actually matters is that the block is re-opened underneath it.

## Gates

```
$ sh scripts/agent/run-gates.sh --diff origin/master
GATE PASS: mvn -B -q verify
GATES: PASS
```

Found during an independent adversarial review of the merged #37 fix.

author: seeker71
body:
The manager buys food most mornings and the record lived nowhere a second person could read. This is the smallest surface that changes that: **one number typed on a phone in the market**, and an entry that already knows the date, the place, and what it was for.

Surface: `/grocery`, served on **app.hati.earth**.

## The amount is the whole interaction

Typed in thousands — the *ribu* habit already used at a warung. The hub's own ledger confirms it: its real amounts are `385`, `477.3`, `351`, `125`, `443`, `197`, `869`, `162`.

| typed | recorded |
|---|---|
| `123.5` | Rp 123.500 |
| `477.3` | Rp 477.300 |
| `0.25` | Rp 250 |
| `12.05` | Rp 12.050 |

Computed by **exact integer arithmetic on the Form kernel** ([`endpoint_grocery_amount.fk`](api/app/form_recipes/endpoint_grocery_amount.fk)) — the typed string is split into digits and multiplied, so no float touches the money path. There is deliberately **no Python mirror**: `serve_via_kernel` fails hard when the kernel is absent, so Python never quietly resumes ownership. Resilience lives at the edge (the offline queue), not as a second implementation that could drift.

**Four-way proven.** Go, Rust, TypeScript and the c-bootstrapped `fkwu` return the same integer on all nine cases — `fourth arm: 9 case(s) four-way, 0 divergent`, no unsupported op. Receipt: [`commit_evidence_2026-07-29_grocery_amount_four_way.json`](docs/system_audit/commit_evidence_2026-07-29_grocery_amount_four_way.json).

## The description arrives before it is typed

Shops are `household_place` cells with `kind="shop"` and a `default_description`, so the grounds' existing GPS pinning and kernel-side proximity (`endpoint_place_distance.fk`) carry them — **no second location system**. Within ~150m the shop's stored sentence becomes the description; beyond that `nearest` returns nothing rather than a market 4km away, and eleven bilingual category icons plus a custom field carry it instead.

Precedence: a typed note wins → the shop's description → the icon's label.

**Why this matters:** in the hub's ledger as we found it, every purchase row had `What` **empty** — the amount recorded, the meaning lost. That column is the reason this app exists.

## One ledger, both directions

The sheet is restructured to an append-only log so nothing ever has to move:

```
      A           B          C                          E            F
 1    When        Amount     What                       Remaining    =-SUM($B$2:$B)
 2    23/07/2026  385000     pasar pagi — sayur & ikan  Spent        =SUMIF($B$2:$B,">0")
 3    26/07/2026  -4000000   top up                     Topped up    =-SUMIF($B$2:$B,"<0")
```

`Amount` is signed (buy positive, top-up negative — the convention the old settlement rows already used, so every existing number keeps its meaning). `Remaining` is a formula in a **fixed cell**, reading positive when there's float left. `Paid` is gone. A one-time `restructure()` migration converts the sheet in place; simulated against the live export first — 10 rows preserved, Spent Rp 3,009,300, Topped up Rp 5,781,300, Remaining Rp 2,772,000.

Money in (`POST /grocery/topup`) and money out (`POST /grocery/spend`) are one cell type with a `kind`, so "what's left to spend" is a single signed sum. The app leads with that number.

Nothing is locked in: the graph is the source of truth, the sheet is a mirror fed by a webhook the hub owns, `GET /api/grocery/export.csv` carries the fuller ten-column record, and unsent entries queue in `localStorage`.

## Fixes found by using it as a non-technical person would

- **A rejection was displayed as a save.** `send()` returned "don't requeue" as success, so a refused amount cleared the form and looked recorded while nothing landed. Saved / rejected / offline are now three distinct outcomes.
- **Nothing confirmed a save** — the number just vanished. Now "✓ Tercatat Rp 385.000" with an undo.
- **A wrong number was permanent.** `DELETE /grocery/spend/{id}` — yours to undo, a resident's to fix for anyone; it says when the sheet already has the row rather than editing the hub's document behind their back.
- **`Permissions-Policy` carried `geolocation=()`**, blocking the API for our own pages — silently breaking the hub's *existing* place-pinning too. Now `geolocation=(self)`; the browser still prompts, camera and mic stay closed.
- Tap targets under 44px: **5 → 0** on mobile, measured on the built page.

## Also repairs the base branch's own CI

`main` has failed Thread Gates daily since 2026-07-21 with six federation tests dying on `OSError: [Errno 8] Exec format error: form/form-cli`. Root cause: `native_federation_graph_service._binary()` took `form/form-cli` on sight, while its sibling `native_runtime_observation` already read the host-native carrier receipt — and the pinned kernel ships that file as **Mach-O arm64**, unrunnable on a Linux runner. Now both read the receipt.

A/B under CI's exact conditions: **6 failed without the fix, 13 passed with it.** In CI this took validate-thread-process from **8 failures to 1**.

## Verification

- Full suite: `2034 passed`. `windows-floor` and GitGuardian green.
- Both viewports from a real production build: mobile 390px (no horizontal scroll), desktop 1440px (content 1152px). GPS auto-fill confirmed live.
- Idea recorded via `POST /api/ideas` (`93e25cee-af3a-416f-9244-9c5685aff36e`).

## Known remaining

- **One red test:** `test_runtime_policy_pin_matches_the_reusable_workflow_call`. `PINNED_OBSERVER_WORKFLOW_SHA` is `64b62db3`, which **does not exist in this repository**; the workflow correctly pins `f2457c87`. `#3971` moved the workflow and left the constant behind. A verified one-line fix exists but is held back as a trust-pin change awaiting explicit sign-off. This test already fails on `main`, so merging does not introduce it.
- **DNS:** `app.hati.earth` needs one proxied record pointing where `suci.hati.earth` already does. Traefik labels are in this diff.
- **The sheet webhook** must be deployed against the hub's spreadsheet and its `/exec` URL placed in the keystore. The sheet **id** already ships in `api/config/api.json`.
- The standard receipt's platform rows (mac / windows / android metal) are **pending**; four-way in CI is a rung below them.

Replaced the two raw `400` status comparisons in the shared Sentry integration helpers with `HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST`. This follows the repository convention for HTTP status codes without changing retry behavior, diagnostic hints, or user-facing messages.

## Code Understanding and AI Usage

**Did you use AI assistance (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.) to write any part of this code?**
- [ ] No, I wrote all the code myself

**If you used AI assistance:**

- [x] I have tested edge cases and understand how the code handles them

**Explain your implementation approach:**

`httpx` exposes response status codes as integers. `HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST` is an `IntEnum` with the same value as `400`, so these comparisons remain equivalent.

The first comparison adds useful guidance when Sentry rejects a query. The second retries alternative query segments after the same response. I kept both control-flow paths and all messages unchanged. A separate constant was unnecessary because the standard-library enum is already the project convention.

The existing scoped tests cover the HTTP 400 diagnostic and retry paths, so no test changes were needed for this behavior-preserving, one-file refactor.

author: raprogramm
body:
# Pull Request

## Description

Closes #1868

## What lands

| Path | Action | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Configs/.config/nushell/autoload/hyde.nu` | sync | HyDE's environment, prompt setup and aliases |
| `Configs/.config/nushell/config.nu` | preserve | the user's own configuration, untouched on update |
| `Scripts/dots/nushell.toml` | new metafile | dependencies and deployment |
| `Scripts/dots-groups/shell.toml` | one line | Nushell joins zsh and fish in the shell chooser |

## Why the autoload directory

Nushell reads every file in `$nu.user-autoload-dirs`, which resolves to
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/nushell/autoload`, before it reads `config.nu`. Deploying
there is the direct equivalent of fish's `conf.d`: HyDE's environment applies
without the user's `config.nu` having to reference it, and updating HyDE never
touches a file the user edits.

## What `hyde.nu` sets

The same ground `conf.d/hyde.fish` covers: the XDG base directories and user
directories, `LESSHISTFILE`, `PARALLEL_HOME`, `~/.local/bin` on `PATH`,
starship with HyDE's config and cache locations, and the shell aliases.

Every assignment goes through `default`, so a value the session or the user
already exported is never overwritten.

One deliberate difference from the fish file: `HYPRLAND_CONFIG` is resolved
rather than hardcoded. Hyprland selects its config provider from the
extension, so the Lua entry point is preferred and the hyprlang file is the
fallback:

```nu
[
    ($env.XDG_DATA_HOME | path join "hypr" "hyde.lua")
    "/usr/local/share/hypr/hyde.lua"
    "/usr/share/hypr/hyde.lua"
    ($env.XDG_DATA_HOME | path join "hypr" "hyprland.conf")
]
| where {|candidate| $candidate | path exists }
| get -o 0
```

`conf.d/hyde.fish` still points unconditionally at `hyprland.conf`, which is
the pre-Lua path. That is left alone here so this pull request stays about
Nushell.

Starship needs one accommodation. Nushell cannot source generated code at
runtime, so the init script is written into the vendor autoload directory the
first time and picked up from then on, instead of being regenerated on every
startup.

## Verification

Deployed into a clean `HOME` and started as an interactive shell, with every
relevant variable unset beforehand:

```
HYPRLAND_CONFIG=<HOME>/.local/share/hypr/hyprland.conf
XDG_DATA_HOME=<HOME>/.local/share
STARSHIP_CONFIG=<HOME>/.config/starship/starship.toml
ll=eza -lha --icons=auto --sort=name --group-directories-first
PATH[0]=<HOME>/.local/bin
```

`vendor/autoload/starship.nu` is generated as expected. On a machine where
`hyde.lua` exists, the same run resolves `HYPRLAND_CONFIG` to it instead of
the fallback, and an already-exported value is left untouched.

Checked against Nushell 0.114.1. The new metafile passes the structural check
from #1871.

## Known limitation

Nushell reads the user autoload directory in the REPL, not for `nu -c` or
`nu script.nu`. Interactive sessions, which is what a shell configuration is
for, are covered; a script run under Nushell inherits whatever the session
already exported, which for a HyDE session is set by uwsm.

## Type of change

- [ ] **Bug fix** (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] **New feature** (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] **Breaking change** (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] **Documentation update** (non-breaking change; modified files are limited to the documentations)
- [ ] **Technical debt** (a code change that does not fix a bug or add a feature but makes something clearer for devs)
- [ ] **Other** (provide details below)

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/HyDE-Project/HyDE/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) document.
- [x] My code follows the code style of this project.
- [x] My commit message follows the [commit guidelines](https://github.com/HyDE-Project/HyDE/blob/master/COMMIT_MESSAGE_GUIDELINES.md).
- [x] My change requires a change to the documentation.
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly.
- [x] I have added a changelog entry.
- [x] I have added necessary comments/documentation to my code.
- [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.
- [x] I have tested my code locally and it works as expected.
- [x] All new and existing tests passed.

## Additional context

`pre-commit run` passes on the files this branch touches. The repository has
244 files with pre-existing end-of-file and trailing-whitespace findings; they
are left alone rather than folded in here.

* **New Features**

  * Included Nushell aliases for quick navigation, HyDE helper commands, Git, and launching code.
  * Optionally bootstraps Starship for Nushell with default cache/config settings.

body:
> **Depends on #21** (creator identity + `precompute-creators.ts`). #21 is still open; its migration
> **has been applied**, so `creator_rankings` exists and this endpoint works today. But until #21
> merges, nothing repopulates the table nightly — merge #21 first.
>
> No new manual SQL for this PR.

Adds the Top Affiliates leaderboard: `api/top-creators.ts` + `client/src/pages/creators.tsx`, reading the nightly aggregate in `creator_rankings`. **Zero ScrapeCreators credits** — Supabase reads only.

---

## API — `api/top-creators.ts`

Mirrors `api/top-products.ts`: identical `resolveTier`, free-tier coercion applied **before** the cache lookup so `?niche=&days=&page=&limit=` cannot widen the response, and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=300`.

| | niche | days | rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| free / anon | forced `all` | forced `30` | top **5** |
| paid | any | 7 or 30 | full list, paginated |

**No live-compute fallback, deliberately.** The aggregation loads ~316k video rows and takes minutes; computing it inside a request would hang the endpoint. A missing cache row returns **503** `{error:"leaderboard not computed yet"}` (`max-age=60`), which the page renders as a friendly wait state.

### One deviation from top-products, and why

The response carries **both** `total` and `creatorCount`. The precompute stores only the top 400, while `creator_count` records how many were actually ranked (**10,497** for `all:30`). Reporting only the payload length understates the dataset; reporting only `creator_count` would make the upsell promise 10k rows Pro cannot serve. So `total` (400) drives pagination and upsell copy — "Unlock 395 more ranked affiliates" — while `creatorCount` renders as "10,497 creators ranked".

## Page — `/dashboard/creators`, sidebar "Top Affiliates" (Trophy icon)

Registered under `/dashboard/*` to match every other authenticated page. Reuses the products.tsx patterns: niche select with `(Pro)` locking, window toggle, the post-#19 single-upsell-block, mono numerics, no emojis.

Three judgment calls worth surfacing:

- **GMV of 0 renders as "—", never "$0".** Zero here means "promoted only unranked products", not "sold nothing" — $0 would be a false claim about a real creator.
- **Numeric-key creators show `display_name` only**, no handle line, rather than inventing an `@id:7526...` label.
- **Confidence is an amber dot + %**, with a `title` explaining it is the share of modeled GMV from measured sales deltas.

Row click expands an inline panel with top products (thumbnail via `/api/thumb`, title, that creator's video count).

Also adds the dev-server proxy in `server/routes.ts` — same pattern as top-products/top-videos, so local Express and prod Vercel share one implementation and cannot drift.

---

## Curl matrix

Run against the handler with a real Supabase session per tier (temporary users, deleted afterwards — **0 remain**).

```
############ (1) ANON — no auth ############
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: private, max-age=300
rows=5  total=400  creatorCount=10497  page=1  limit=5

############ (2) ANON bypass ?niche=gym-fitness&days=7&limit=100&page=3 ############
Cache-Control: private, max-age=300
rows=5 total=400 page=1 limit=5 -> coerced=True

############ (3) PAID — default all/30 ############
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: private, max-age=300
rows=50 total=400 creatorCount=10497 page=1 limit=50

############ (4) PAID — shoes-footwear 7d page=3 limit=25 ############
rows=15 total=65 creatorCount=65 page=3 limit=25

############ (5) 503 — cache row missing ############
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Cache-Control: private, max-age=60
{"error":"leaderboard not computed yet","niche":"nonexistent-niche","days":30}

############ (6) 400 — invalid days ############
HTTP 400  {"error":"Invalid days"}
```

`npm run check` passes.

---

## Screenshots

### Free — 5 rows + single upsell (1440px)
![free desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shayurc/tikbase/feat/creators-leaderboard/docs/screenshots/1b/free-desktop.png)

### Paid — full list, pagination (1440px)
![paid desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shayurc/tikbase/feat/creators-leaderboard/docs/screenshots/1b/paid-desktop.png)

### Expanded row — inline top-products panel

author: itamarzand88
body:
## Summary

The azurerm provider constraint we generate had no upper bound, so Terraform resolved
whatever was newest. Version 5 renamed arguments we emit, and the module we generate
stopped passing `terraform validate`.

What happens when someone installs an Azure deployment:

1. We generate a module declaring `azurerm >= 3.100`.
2. `terraform init` resolves that to the newest matching version, now a 5.x release.
3. **`terraform validate` rejects our storage table**, because `storage_account_name`
   became `storage_account_id` in that major.

Existing deployments are unaffected: they resolved their provider once and kept it in
`.terraform.lock.hcl`. A fresh install has no lock file and resolves the new major.

This bounds the constraint to `>= 3.100, < 5.0` so we decide the supported range instead
of a release deciding it for us.

## What was broken

Every branch's `Rust crates` job went red at the same time, with no commit to blame. The
Azure generator tests render the real module and run `terraform validate`, so they failed
the moment the new provider shipped:

```
Error: Missing required argument
  on metadata.tf line 1, in resource "azurerm_storage_table" "metadata":
  The argument "storage_account_id" is required, but no definition was found.

Error: Unsupported argument
  on metadata.tf line 3:
    storage_account_name = azurerm_storage_account.default_storage_account.name
```

An unbounded major constraint claims we work with versions that do not exist yet, which
can never be true.

## What I did

Bounded the constraint, and left a note saying the ceiling is temporary so it is not read
later as a considered maximum. Porting the emitters to the new major is real work with a
support decision attached (anyone still on 3.x or 4.x breaks if we emit 5-only syntax),
so it belongs in its own change.

## Files touched

- `alien-terraform/src/generator.rs` - the constraint, plus why the bound exists
- 18 generator snapshots - the version string, nothing else

## How I tested

`cargo nextest run -p alien-terraform` - 158/158 pass. Before this change, four Azure
tests failed on `terraform validate`; they render the module and validate it for real, so
they are the same check a customer's `terraform init && terraform validate` performs.

Reviewed the snapshot diff line by line: 18 files, one line each, only the version string.

One caveat worth stating: a deployment that already applied successfully on the new major
would now see a constraint conflict and have to downgrade on its next `init`. That is only
reachable for a stack using none of the renamed resources, since anything with a storage
table could not have applied.

author: henriquekraemer
body:
Adds a `snapshot_socket_timeout` connection option (in seconds) for the idle timeout on snapshot connection sockets, defaulting to the current fixed 30 seconds. Same pattern as the `replication_socket_timeout` option proposed in #715, applied to the snapshot connection instead.

```yaml
replication:
  connections:
    - type: postgresql
      # ...
      snapshot_socket_timeout: 90
```

## Background

The snapshot socket timeout is an idle timeout: it fires when the snapshot loop stops consuming the source stream for 30 seconds. The main way that happens is storage backpressure, since a storage flush blocks the chunk loop. We hit this reliably while re-replicating a deployment where the new sync rules instance snapshots while the previous instance keeps streaming on the same storage: on wide tables, a flush under that combined load can take longer than 30s, and the idle timeout kills the source connection mid-snapshot. It shows up either as a socket timeout inside the chunk query or as `postgres query failed` on the next chunk, when the timeout fired between queries and destroyed the connection.

With resumable snapshots the table resumes from the last key, so no work is lost, but each kill costs the retry delay plus re-reading the current chunk. Snapshot concurrency (#731) makes the window easier to hit, but the exposure exists in the sequential path as well, since flushes have always run between chunk reads.

The default stays at 30 seconds, so behavior is unchanged unless the option is set.

## Tests

Added config normalization tests (seconds to milliseconds, unset by default, invalid values ignored), mirroring the tests in #715.

author: deckhouse-boatswain
body:
## Description

Adds Dex patch `017-fix-upstream-refresh-token-rotation.patch` to fix refresh failures with upstream providers that rotate refresh tokens, such as GitLab.

Dex stored one upstream credential in both the shared offline session and the issued refresh token. When another client used and rotated the shared credential, the private copy became invalid, so refresh failed permanently with `500 invalid_request`.

The patch makes each credential owned by one storage object, writes rotated credentials back only to that owner, and keeps the offline session as fallback for old tokens. No schema change, migration, config change, or forced re-login is required.

Main changes:

- use token-owned credential first, shared credential as fallback;
- prevent stale overwrites of newer shared credentials;
- recover from shared-credential races with bounded retries;
- call the upstream connector at most once per request;
- persist rotated credentials even if the request later fails;
- stop clearing credentials during reuse interval;
- improve errors, avoid credential logs, and fix nil panic.

## Why do we need it, and what problem does it solve?

GitLab users are logged out every `idTokenTTL` and must re-authenticate in `kubectl`, `d8 k`, and web apps behind DexAuthenticator. Raising `idTokenTTL` only delays the issue.

Regression tests reproduce the production failure with two OAuth2 clients and a rotating upstream refresh token. The patch adds 12 tests; all fail without it.

## Why do we need it in the patch release (if we do)?

Needed because current-release users have no real workaround.

Backport variants for 1.75 and 1.76 are prepared and verified against v1.75.14 and v1.76.6: patch applies, image builds, tests pass.

## Checklist

- [x] The code is covered by unit tests.
- [ ] e2e tests passed.
- [ ] Documentation updated according to the changes.
- [ ] Changes were tested in the Kubernetes cluster manually.

## Changelog entries

```changes
section: user-authn
type: fix
summary: Fix Dex token refresh with upstream providers that rotate refresh tokens (GitLab), which logged users out every `idTokenTTL`.
impact_level: default
```
