## 課題と解決策

CVE-2026-66066（KindaRails2Shell）への根本対応として、APIのRailsを修正版の7.2.3.2へ更新しました。
Rails 7.2の実行要件とRuby側のセキュリティ修正を踏まえ、Rubyも3.3.12へ更新しています。

GMではActive Storageによる添付ファイル保存を使用しておらず、画像はImgurまたはFirebaseに保存しています。一方、Active Storage・Action Text・Action Mailboxのエンジンがロードされ、標準アップロードルートが公開されていたため、未使用エンジンと関連設定も削除しました。

## 変更内容

- Rails 6.1.7.8 → 7.2.3.2
- Ruby 3.0.7 → 3.3.12
- Puma 4系 → 7.2.1
- `.ruby-version`・RuboCop・GitHub ActionsのRuby設定を3.3へ同期
- Rails 7.2 / Ruby 3.3互換のため、mysql2・Devise・Spring等の依存関係を更新
- Rails 7向けにenumを位置引数形式へ更新
- API-only構成でDevise Token Authがセッションへ書き込まないよう設定
- Rack 3互換のためAuthorizationヘッダー名を明示
- Ruby 3.3ベースイメージで廃止されたapt-key/Yarnリポジトリ設定を削除（API内にYarn利用なし）
- 未使用のActive Storage、Action Text、Action Mailboxをアプリケーションのロード対象から除外
- Active Storageの環境別サービス設定と`storage.yml`を削除
- OpenAPIからActive Storage／Action Mailboxの標準ルートとスキーマを削除

## 影響

- APIコンテナの再ビルドが必要です。
- `config.load_defaults` は既存互換設定を維持し、アプリ挙動の一括変更は行っていません。
- DBマイグレーションはありません。
- GMの業務APIに変更はありません。未使用だったRails標準のActive Storage／Action Mailboxエンドポイントのみ削除します。

## 検証結果

- `docker compose build api`: 成功
- API起動: Rails 7.2.3.2 / Ruby 3.3.12 / Puma 7.2.1
- `GET /fes_years`: HTTP 200、DBデータをJSONで取得
- `POST /rails/active_storage/direct_uploads`: HTTP 404
- Active Storage／Action Text／Action Mailboxの各Engine: 未ロード
- `rails routes`のActive Storageルート: 0件
- `rails zeitwerk:check`: 成功
- RuboCop全体: 369 files / 0 offenses
- OpenAPI再生成: 成功、無効化したエンジンへの参照0件
- 認証関連対象テスト: 10 runs / 44 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors
- fixtureを無効化しているテスト群: 150 runs中142 runs成功。残る8件は、現行ルートが存在する一方でRoutingErrorを期待するテスト、およびテストセットアップのgroup lookup 404によるもの
- 全Railsテスト: 317 runs / 499 assertions。`assign_rental_items.yml`が現行schemaに存在しない旧カラム（`rental_order_id` / `rentable_item_id`）を参照するため、124 failures / 95 errors
- `bundler-audit`: 今回対象のRails脆弱性を含むその他の指摘は解消。Devise 4.9.4のMedium 2件のみ残存するが、対象機能のConfirmable / TimeoutableはUserモデルで未使用（devise_token_auth 1.2.6のDevise 5対応待ち）

## 導入手順

```sh
docker compose build api
docker compose up -d api
```

author: earlyprototype
body:
## Why this PR exists

**This is a review-only PR. Do not merge it.** Every file in it is already
present, byte-identical, on `claude/issue-6-akvuxp` (PR #10).

PR #10 carries the full EXP_010c-4 census: 277 measured windows × 25 prompts,
plus 554 generated data artifacts (one results JSON and one terminal tensor per
arm). At 570 files against a 100-file limit, automated review skips it.

So this branch re-stages **only the six non-artifact files** written since the
last successful review (`ce692f8`), against that same commit. The diff here is
six files instead of 560, which is small enough to actually get reviewed. The
findings are applied to `claude/issue-6-akvuxp`, not merged from here.

> **Correction (2026-07-29).** An earlier version of this description said a
> repo-level `.coderabbit.yaml` could not help "because org-level UI
> configuration takes precedence over the repo file." That was the wrong
> mechanism. CodeRabbit reads the config **from the base branch**: this PR
> reports `Configuration used: Path: .coderabbit.yaml` because its base is
> `claude/issue-6-akvuxp`, which carries the file, while PR #10 reports
> `Configuration used: Organization UI` because its base is the default
> branch, which does not have the file yet. No org-level change is required —
> once this work merges to the default branch, the filters apply to
> subsequent PRs on their own.

Note that targeting a non-default base is also why auto-review never fires
here ("auto reviews are disabled on base/target branches other than the
default branch"); each round needs an explicit `@coderabbitai review`.

## Review status

Round 1 returned four findings, all accepted and fixed in
[`498e7ca`](https://github.com/earlyprototype/ATR_research/commit/498e7ca9027b783e3839017b6f4e2775e2c061c6)
on `claude/issue-6-akvuxp`, mirrored here as `d2cea87`. All four threads are
resolved and confirmed addressed; round 2 raised nothing new.

**No measured value changed.** After the fixes, `build_final_map.py` still
reproduces 300/300 cells, 47 whole-word / 162 mixed / 91 punctuation-funnel,
the 21-cell target set, 8 non-convergence cells, `D` at (0→23) only, and H12
SUPPORTED 15/50. The defects were in the instrument and its documentation,
not in the measurements; census artifacts were not regenerated.

| # | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Partial-census guard was opt-in behind a flag, so a partial artifact set could emit a final map and H12 verdict indistinguishable from the real one | Refusal is now the default; `--allow-partial` is an explicit override that suppresses the H12 verdict and stamps the map `PROVISIONAL` |
| 2 | `BASE` was an absolute `/home/user/...` path | Derived from `__file__` |
| 3 | Runbook listed all 21 targets against `terminals_census/`, but only 19 are census arms | Exact per-target manifest; `8→21` is arm `O8` in `terminals_scan.pt`, `10→21` is arm `A4` in `terminals_full.pt`. Also fixed a stale EXP_011m pointer to `output/terminals.pt`, which does not exist |
| 4 | Review filters matched `**/output/...` repo-wide | Scoped to the `exp_010c_windows` tree |

## What's in the diff

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `build_final_map.py` | Pure analysis. Assembles all 300 cells across the full/scan/infill/census tiers, applies the `EXP_010c4_SPEC.md` §3 arm-class rule, evaluates H12 under the §6 pre-analysis amendment, emits the non-convergence and `D` inventories and the ASCII map. Refuses a partial census by default. |
| `RESULTS_EXP010C.md` | 2026-07-29 census section: the 300-cell map, arm classes, the 21-cell target set, 8 non-convergence cells, `D` at exactly one cell (0→23), H12 SUPPORTED 15/50. Plus the via-tail characterisation subsection and a dated post-review-corrections section for this round. |
| `SESSION_2026-07-29_CENSUS.md` | Reasoning trail. All interpretation fenced as blockquotes per the register rules; includes a prediction hostage for EXP_011m. |
| `RUNBOOK_JLENS_MEDIUM.md` | New §3a census hand-forward: the 21-cell target set with the exact artifact manifest, the contrast sets, the single-cell `D` finding, the **corrected** readout-reliability prior, the agreement/target-class dissociation, and the hook-point control as highest-value remaining ATR control. |
| `terminal_characterisation_census.json` | Per-arm characterisation the map and results section are computed from. Generated, but included because the two documents above cannot be checked without it. |
| `.coderabbit.yaml` | Path filters excluding generated run artifacts, scoped to the EXP_010c tree. |

## What reviewers should look at

Three claims in the write-up are corrections of earlier statements in this same
branch, and are the highest-value things to check:

1. **The readout-reliability prior was falsified by the census.** The sampled
   tiers suggested direct/via-tail agreement was high only at extraction
   layer 21. The full census does not support that: agreement rises roughly
   monotonically with depth (≈0/25 at j ≤ 4, ~5/25 at j ≈ 13, 18.9/25 at
   j=22), and j=21 averages only **6.6/25** across its eleven census arms. The
   old prior rested on two cells. Both `RESULTS_EXP010C.md` and the runbook
   §3a were corrected, not overwritten.
2. **The 010c-3 hand-forward is superseded, not deleted.** The earlier
   "exactly (8→21) and (10→21)" target claim is marked superseded by the
   census's 21 cells, and the superseding is visible in the record.
3. **H12's vacuous-truth hole.** The §6 amendment restricts H12 to cells with
   ≥1 already-measured neighbour; `build_final_map.py` implements that
   restriction. Worth confirming the code matches the amendment's wording.

Also worth a look: the target set is **not** a contiguous band and includes
single-layer windows (10→10, 13→13, 20→20, 21→21), and the whole-word
prompt-dependent class is **not** the same set as the high-agreement class —
so two-instrument agreement cannot validate the target cells, which is why the
write-up calls EXP_013m load-bearing rather than confirmatory.

## Provenance

- No new measurement. Every number derives from the committed per-arm shards on
  `claude/issue-6-akvuxp`; `build_final_map.py` is deterministic over them.
- Census protocol unchanged from the pre-registered `EXP_010c4_SPEC.md`: gated
  convergence (threshold 0.999, patience 3, check_every 10, check_start 100,
  max_iter 1000, gate_lag 1), seed 42, the registered 25-prompt subset.
- Frozen inputs untouched.

author: imhiamou
body: ## Summary Transforms the project into a **multi-game platform** without changing how Hidden Hunt plays. The existing hide-and-seek card game is now **Game Mode 1**; **Word Chain** is added as **Game Mode 2**. ## Architecture ### Server (`server/`) - **`lobby.js`** — shared lobby: `createLobby`, `joinLobby`, disconnect. No duplicated lobby logic in game modules. - **`registry.js`** — game mode registry. Adding a future game = create `server/games//` and register it here. - **`dictionary.js`** — English dictionary validation via `an-array-of-english-words`. - **`games/hidden-hunt/index.js`** — entire existing Hidden Hunt server logic (cards, abilities, placement, rematch), unchanged in behaviour. - **`games/word-chain/index.js`** — separate Word Chain module (dictionary validation, chain rules, turn alternation). - **`server.js`** — thin entry point wiring lobby + all registered games. ### Frontend (`games/`) - **`games/hidden-hunt/client.js`** — existing Hidden Hunt UI/logic extracted unchanged. - **`games/word-chain/client.js`** — Word Chain UI (chain display, word input, turn indicator). - **`index.js`** — shared lobby + router: picks the correct game module after both players join. ## Lobby changes When **creating** a lobby the host chooses: - **Lobby Code** (4–8 chars, as before) - **Game Mode**: ○ Hidden Hunt / ○ Word Chain - **Character** (shown only for Hidden Hunt — Knight/Mage/Hunter/Rogue) `gameMode` is stored on the lobby object. **Joining** works exactly as before. After both players join: - `hidden-hunt` → existing placement → card game flow - `word-chain` → Word Chain screen opens immediately ## Word Chain rules (server-authoritative) - Player A opens with any valid English word. - Each next word must start with the last letter of the previous word. - Words must exist in the dictionary and not have been used before. - Invalid moves are rejected with a message; the turn does not pass. - Turns alternate automatically after each valid word. ## Testing 9-check integration suite passes locally: - Hidden Hunt lobby create/join with `gameMode` - Word Chain lobby create/join + `wordChainStarted` - Valid words (CAT → TABLE), duplicate rejection, dictionary rejection Merging deploys both frontend (GitHub Pages) and backend (Render from `main`).

author: buzzromain
body:
## What this checks

This app never writes to NVM/flash (`git grep -n "nvm_write\|nvm_erase" -- src/` finds nothing), so every secret buffer -- including the `mnemonic` global watched here -- lives exclusively in RAM. The only way a secret could survive closing and reopening the app is if BOLOS does not actually reset that RAM when (re)loading the process -- **a platform guarantee, not something this app's own code controls.**

This adds a sixth Speculos check (`tests/speculos/verify_app_reopen_clears_mnemonic.py`) that verifies that guarantee empirically. Unlike the existing five checks in this directory (which all verify this app's own `memzero()`/`explicit_bzero()` cleanup code), this one is explicitly *not* hunting for an application bug -- there is no application-level fix expected here if it passes.

## Scenario

1. A first Speculos container types and confirms a full 12-word test mnemonic on "Check BIP39".
2. The real `mnemonic` buffer (`src/nbgl/bip39_mnemonic.c`) is read at the return of `bip39_mnemonic_check()` -- the point furthest into the flow where it's still guaranteed to hold the full typed phrase (that function deliberately does not clear it on a valid-checksum path, since it may still be needed for SSKR generation) -- confirming the secret was genuinely present.
3. That container is torn down entirely (`docker stop`/`rm`).
4. A second, completely independent container boots from the same `app.elf` (no shared Docker volumes/state with the first).
5. Before any simulated user interaction, the same global is read again in this fresh process -- its `R9`-relative runtime address re-resolved from scratch, never assumed identical to the first session -- at the entry of `ui_idle_init()`/`display_home_page()`, the very first UI code a fresh process runs at boot.

**Why `docker stop`/`rm` instead of tapping the app's own "Quit app" action** (confirmed reachable, it's a footer link on the home screen): reaching it from the just-confirmed state requires navigating back to the dashboard first, and `display_home_page()` unconditionally clears the buffer via this app's own defense-in-depth code (`reset_globals()`) before it ever draws that screen -- before the platform guarantee under test would ever get exercised. That would make a `PASS` ambiguous (clean because of BOLOS, or clean because of unrelated application code?). Tearing the container down directly keeps the buffer populated with real content up to the moment the process actually disappears.

## Result -- PASS

Run against a real `flex` build:

```
Container 1 -- mnemonic buffer at bip39_mnemonic_check() return (nonzero=88/324):
  666c79206d756c6520657863657373207265736f7572636520747265617420706c756e6765...
  (decodes as "fly mule excess resource treat plunge nose soda reflect adult ramp planet")

Container 2 -- mnemonic buffer at ui_idle_init() entry, before any interaction (R9=0x50000000, nonzero=0/324):
  0000000000000000...0000  (entirely zero)

PASS: no trace of the first session's typed mnemonic is present in the second,
freshly-booted process's buffer -- BOLOS resets this RAM on app reload.
```

## Scope

No production code changes -- see the reasoning above for why none are expected on a `PASS`. `tests/speculos/README.md` updated with a new Check 6 entry (table of contents, files table, duration table, and a dedicated section) following the same structure as the existing five checks.

If this had come back `FAIL`, the plan was to stop and discuss rather than treat it as a routine one-line fix -- documented as such in the script and the README, since a real failure here would point at either a test-infrastructure artifact or something significant about BOLOS's RAM handling under Speculos, not an application bug.

author: devdudeio
body:
Two parties, two keys, two independent signatures, one transaction:

```
92fc291cca681972b763cb9cc029bd62cd59b6131887e4e77f6b0c30e77fe4c6
height 1167825 on VRSCTEST, via api.verustest.net
```

The maker moved 1 VRSCTEST into an offer output and signed it away under
`SIGHASH_SINGLE|ANYONECANPAY` against an output paying them 1.2. The taker — holding a
key the maker has never seen — appended their own input, their receipt and their change,
signed under `SIGHASH_ALL`, and broadcast.

| | |
|---|---|
| maker gave | 1.0 (from the CC offer output) |
| maker received | 1.2 |
| taker paid | 1.2 + 0.0002 fee |
| taker received | 1.0 + 1.2998 change |

3.5 in, 3.4998 out, 0.0002 fee. Nothing escrowed, no third party.

## Two real bugs surfaced doing it — which is the point of doing it

**`funding::spendable` handed every UTXO to the native builders, including reserve
outputs.** A wallet holding a single token therefore **could not make an ordinary
payment**: the builder refused the token output as funding, and rightly — its value is in
the payload, not the satoshis, so spending it as ordinary funding destroys whatever it
carries.

This bit immediately: the maker held 0.99 shylock from the conversion work and the very
first `send` failed. Now separated into `Funding::other` and handed *back* rather than
dropped, since a token transfer needs exactly those.

**`take_offer` would have half-funded a token-wanted offer.** A reserve output has zero
native value, so the demand read as nothing, nothing was funded, and the token side would
not have conserved — rejected on chain after all the work. Now refused explicitly, with
the reason.

That second one is a scope limit, stated plainly: `take_offer` funds native demands only.
Paying a token needs reserve inputs and token change, which this path doesn't build.

## `fund_offer`

The step before `make_offer` that had no builder — an ordinary transaction whose first
output pays `offer_funding_script`. The module docs referenced it before it existed.

## Verification

All six gates green: `fmt --check`, `clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`,
`test --workspace --all-features` (**419 passed, 0 failed**), `doc -D warnings`,
`check -p verus-sdk --no-default-features`, `deny check`.

The live swap test is gated behind `VERUS_LIVE_SWAP` and needs two funded keys, so it
doesn't run in CI — the on-chain result above is reported rather than implied.

author: keiranholloway
body:
Part of the **Prompts Live in the Database** feature (#909). This is the Core half — the `biffo-plugin-idea-scout` half and the `biffo-platform` distribution follow separately.

Closes #910
Closes #911

## Why

Editing Idea Scout's synthesis prompt saved successfully and **changed nothing that runs** (`biffo-plugin-idea-scout#64`): the prompt was frozen into an orchestration workflow's `action_config` at seed time. `#61` shipped a warning making that honest; this makes it false.

Both fixes proposed on #64 turned out to be unavailable, for a deliberate reason rather than a gap — `GET /internal/plugins/me/config/{role}` resolves the plugin from the *caller's own identity*, so the orchestrator reading idea-scout's config is exactly the cross-plugin read that route refuses. The design that works is the third one: **Core resolves at agent-run creation**, where it already owns `plugin_chat_agents`.

## M1 — Core resolves prompts at run creation (#910)

- `POST /internal/agent-runs` resolves `instructions`/`model` from the chat-agent registry by `agent_name` when the snapshot omits them, and writes the resolved values into `definition_snapshot` — so the snapshot is what actually ran (ADR-0014 §10).
- **Precedence, stated in the docstring and tested both ways:** config wins if present. Every existing workflow keeps working unchanged; omitting the key is the opt-in.
- `instructions` is now optional on the `agent` and `agent_fan_in` actions. Blast radius was checked, not assumed: idea-scout's fan-in is the only seeded workflow in the estate using an agent action.
- A missing prompt with no registry row fails loudly with 422 rather than creating a run with an empty one.

**Beyond the issue as written:** the orchestrator hardcoded `"model": "moonshotai/kimi-k3"` into `AGENT_CONFIG_DEFAULTS`, so a model key was *always* present by the time Core saw it and registry model resolution could never fire — an admin editing an agent's model would still have been editing an inert field. The default now lives in exactly one place, `settings.agent_default_model`, applied only after the registry is consulted. Precedence: snapshot → registry → default.

## M2 — Version the registry, record the version on each run (#911)

- `plugin_chat_agent_history`, modelled on the existing `ddl_import_history` precedent. Every admin edit writes the **previous** values with author and timestamp. An unchanged PUT writes nothing, so the timeline stays answerable.
- `GET /admin/plugins/{plugin}/chat-agents/{key}/history`, newest first, tenant-scoped.
- `AgentRun` records `prompt_version_id` (which registry row) **and** `prompt_version` (which generation of it). The generation is what makes "this run was worse" answerable — the row id alone is invariant across edits, so it names the agent, not the version.
- Portal: the prompt version shows on the agent-run detail, and nothing at all when there isn't one.

## M3 (Core half) — a plugin can guarantee its own rows (#912)

- `POST /internal/plugins/me/config/seed` — insert-if-absent, resolved from the caller's own identity like the routes beside it.
- **It never overwrites an existing row.** This runs on every plugin cold start; overwriting would silently revert an admin's edited prompt to the built-in constant on every deploy and undo the whole feature. That is the first test in the file.
- Seeding writes no history rows — a seed-created row is the row's origin, not a change to it.

The plugin-side half of #912 (self-seeding at startup, removing the built-in fallback, dropping the frozen prompt from `seed_fan_in_workflow.py`, deleting #61's warning) lands in `biffo-plugin-idea-scout`.

## Migration

`0014_plugin_chat_agent_history` — creates the history table and adds both `agent_runs` columns, with a working `downgrade()`. Chained on `0013`, one head.

## Verification

Local gates, each on its own exit code: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `pyright`, `bandit`, `pytest` (1546 passed, 6 skipped), `pnpm lint`, `typecheck`, `test` — all 0, run against the **assembled** batch rather than each milestone alone.

**Not verified here, and deliberately so:** that editing the synthesis prompt on dev changes what a real scout run produces. That needs the plugin half plus `biffo-platform#124`'s deploy, and it is the criterion the feature exists for — it is not claimed until someone has watched it in a browser.

author: vdbbjorn
body:
Follow-up to [#57](https://github.com/codest-be/albertoo/pull/57), branched from `main` so it can merge independently — it touches the control loop, not the admin surface.

## The query

`PostgresTenantProcessorLock.GetKnownTenantsAsync` ran:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id FROM alberto_events ORDER BY tenant_id
```

The entire event log, scanned every time, to produce a list whose length is the number of tenants.

Migration 012 created `alberto_tenants` to retire exactly this. Its own header says so — *"so GetKnownTenantsAsync can query the catalog instead of doing a full-table SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id"*. The migration landed; the C# side never followed. So this is finishing a change that was already half-made, not a new idea.

```sql
SELECT tenant_id FROM alberto_tenants ORDER BY tenant_id
```

## Why the catalog is safe to read here

- **No gap on existing stores.** 012 backfills with `MIN(created_at)`/`MAX(created_at)` grouped over the whole log, so a store that migrated at any point already knows every tenant it has ever seen. The catalog does not start empty.
- **No lag window.** The trigger is `AFTER INSERT ... FOR EACH STATEMENT` — once per append, not once per row — and it fires inside the appender's own transaction. A tenant becomes discoverable the instant its first event is durable, the same moment the scan would have found it.
- **Sharding unaffected.** `alberto_tenants` sits beside `alberto_events` in each database, so a sharded module's answer stays per-shard.

## The one behavioural difference

**The catalog has no delete path.** A tenant whose events have been purged keeps its row, where `SELECT DISTINCT` would have dropped it. Upfront distribution then acquires a lease for a tenant with no work — one lease row and one empty pass — rather than re-scanning the entire log on every startup to avoid it.

That is a real change, so it is pinned by a test rather than left in a comment.

## Tests

This method had **no coverage at all** before this PR — and no in-repo callers either, though it is on the public `ITenantProcessorLock` interface, so it is library surface a consumer can reach. Three tests added, all appending through the real tenancy-enabled event store so the trigger runs for real:

- ordering is by tenant ID, appended out of alphabetical order to make the assertion mean something
- a tenant is visible as soon as its first append commits
- a tenant whose events were purged is still returned — the difference above

The fixture is a private database: the method returns the whole catalog with nothing to scope it by, so on a shared one it would also return every tenant any other test in the assembly happened to append.

I checked the purge test discriminates: reverted to the old query, it fails; restored, it passes. The other two pass under both implementations by design — they document guarantees the two queries share.

`dotnet test` — **1470 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped**.

## Summary
- `rx->timing_adj` gates `adjust_timing()` in `rade_rx_v2.c` (the coarse +/-40 sample CP-centering correction), but it was never set anywhere in the C port (`rade_rx_v2_init`, `rade_api.c`, `rade_rx_wav.c`) — it stayed at its zero-initialized value, so `adjust_timing()` was dead code.
- The receiver would lock onto whatever sub-symbol sample-phase timing offset the CP autocorrelation peak happened to land on at acquisition and keep it uncorrected for the rest of the session.
- Found via a sweep test that prepends 1-40ms of silence before a TX burst and measures loss vs. baseline: loss showed a periodic bump (period exactly 160 samples / 20ms = `RADE_V2_SYM_LEN`), peaking at +15% above baseline — enough to fail a +/-10% verification gate.
- The Python reference (`rx2.py` in drowe67/radae, `dr-radev2` branch) enables this almost immediately by default via `--timing_adj_at 0` (`receiver.timing_adj = 1` once `s > 0`). This change mirrors that by enabling it unconditionally in `rade_rx_v2_init()`.

## Test plan
- [x] Rebuilt `rade_rx_wav`/`rade_tx_wav` and reran the 1-40ms offset sweep against `wav/all.wav`: peak loss dropped from 0.094 (+14.6%) to 0.091 (+11%), and violations of the +/-10% baseline dropped from ~14/40 offsets to 2/40.

body:
## Summary

Adds mutual fund CAS (Consolidated Account Statement) import: upload a password-protected CAS PDF (from CAMS, KFintech, or MFCentral), preview all parsed holdings in a bulk-edit table, select/edit/deselect, and confirm to create/update accounts. One parser handles all three sources since their layouts are effectively identical.

## Changes

- **Backend**: new `statements/parsers/cas.py` (line-based extraction: folio + market value + scheme text on one line, units/NAV/registrar+ISIN/cost value on the next), a 50-AMC alias table for grouping, `POST /statements/cas/parse` (bulk preview, no DB writes) and `POST /statements/cas/confirm` (creates or updates accounts in one transaction).
- **Account matching for re-uploads**: added `AccountRepository.get_by_name()` and `meta` support on `update()` so re-importing a later CAS updates existing holdings by folio+scheme instead of duplicating them.
- **Frontend**: `UploadCASFlow.tsx` (table-based multi-row preview) behind a new `ImportStatementFlow.tsx` chooser ("Bank Statement" vs "Mutual Fund CAS"), replacing the old single-flow "Import Statement" entry point. Added a `wide` size option to the shared `Modal` component for the holdings table.
- **Tests**: parser unit tests, API tests (including the create-vs-update re-upload path), and a Playwright e2e spec — all against synthetic fixtures generated to mirror the real CAMS layout structure (no real financial data committed).

## Notable

- The original parser (from the initial implementation) assumed a layout with explicit "AMC:" and "Folio No:" labels. **Validated against a real CAMS statement** (read locally, never committed) and found this was wrong — real CAMS "Consolidated Account Summary" exports have no such labels; folio/market-value/scheme are glued together per PDF column layout, and AMC name is only inferable from the scheme text itself. Rewrote the parser accordingly and rebuilt all fixtures as synthetic data mirroring the corrected structure. Verified 47/47 holdings parsed correctly with zero warnings against the real file.
- Found (not fixed here, separate pre-existing bug): `/api/allocation` doesn't currency-convert like `/api/accounts` and `/api/networth-history` do, so it silently shows empty when display currency doesn't match a holding's native currency.

## Test plan
- [x] Backend unit + API tests pass (parser + statements API)
- [x] Playwright e2e (happy path, re-upload/update, wrong password, non-PDF)
- [x] Manually verified end-to-end against a real CAMS statement — all 47 holdings imported correctly, grouped by AMC, matching real rupee values

## Summary
- `AssetEventUtil.getCubes()` had a shortcut path: when the binding-tree request scoped the lookup to a single cube `source`, it resolved that one cube via `getXCube()`/`getCubeNode()` and returned immediately - even if the lookup came back empty.

- Fixed by falling back to the full datasource loop whenever the single-cube lookup doesn't resolve a node, using local `cubePrefix`/`cubeSource` variables so the fallback loop still sees the original `prefix`/`source` values.

author: kenhuri69
body:
Réponse à « fermer toutes les branches fusionnées sur `main` et lister celles ayant des commits à remonter ». Plan vivant : `.claude/plans/merged-branches-cleanup.md`.

**Périmètre** : documentation seule. **Zéro diff code/données** (aucun fichier sous `packages/`, `data/` ou `assets/`) ⇒ pas de bump `CURRENT_SAVE_VERSION`, golden inchangé, garde-fous inchangés. Pas de smoke test (guidelines §7, dernier point : changement purement documentaire).

## La première mesure était fausse

Le clone de session est **shallow** (`.git/shallow` ; 127 commits visibles sur `main` pour 525 PR). `git branch -r --merged origin/main` ne rendait donc que **12** branches. Après `git fetch --unshallow` (1029 commits), la classification devient fiable.

Deuxième piège : le dépôt mélange merges classiques et **squash merges**. Une branche squash-mergée n'est pas ancêtre de `main` alors que son contenu y est. J'ai donc croisé trois critères — ancestry, `head.sha` des 525 PR (agrégées via l'API), et présence effective des lignes ajoutées dans l'arbre de `main`.

## Résultat sur 209 branches distantes

| Catégorie | Nb |
| --- | --- |
| Ancêtre de `main` | 176 |
| Squash-mergée (tip == head d'une PR mergée) | 25 |
| Contenu déjà dans `main`, sans PR | 1 |
| **Total remontées** | **202** |
| **Commits non remontés** | **7** |

## Les 7 branches à garder

- **PR ouverte, à merger normalement** : `premier-plan-finaliser-cesdux` (#525), `session-842v9w` (#513).
- **Travail réel jamais remonté, décision requise** : `r2-ecran-ville-outil` (3 commits `wip`, aucune PR), `r3-hud-aventure-se-range` (4 commits `wip`, aucune PR), `map-design-issues-jhjdy6` (#289 fermée sans merge — N-ARCS.2, arc de Vhalen).
- **Superseded** : `h-named-roster` (refaite par `-v2`, PR #255 mergée), `code-doc-coherence-remediation` (lots A→E redécoupés en PR atomiques déjà mergées).

⚠️ `main` contient bien des commits « lot R2 » et « lot R3 », mais ils viennent de `premier-plan-finaliser-cesdux` (#522/#523) et touchent `assets/layouts/town-*.json`, **pas** `TownScreen.tsx`/`town.css`. Deux implémentations distinctes du même lot : 8 % (R2) et 11 % (R3) seulement des lignes de ces branches existent dans `main`. Les supprimer perdrait ce code.

## Ce que je n'ai pas pu faire

La suppression des 202 branches est **refusée à la session**, par les deux voies, en 403 :

- `git push origin --delete` via le relais git de session ⇒ `RPC failed; HTTP 403`, sans échec côté proxy d'egress (`recentRelayFailures: []`).
- `DELETE /repos/…/git/refs/heads/…` ⇒ `Write access to this GitHub API path is not permitted through this proxy.`

Conformément à la consigne « ne pas réessayer un refus de politique », je le signale au lieu de contourner. La liste exacte est versionnée dans `.claude/plans/merged-branches-cleanup.branches.txt` et se joue en une commande depuis un poste habilité :

```sh
xargs -n 20 git push origin --delete \
  < .claude/plans/merged-branches-cleanup.branches.txt
```

author: sattyamjjain
body:
Two items, two commits.

## 1 · The public leaderboard was stale and unsigned

`generated_at: 2026-07-04`, `commit: a5fdd13`, **`signature: null`** — while the product's claim is *"a dated, signed record, not a screenshot"*. Both halves were false in the one place a buyer checks.

**Regenerated, and nothing was fabricated.** The board is built by *aggregating committed `report.json` files*, not by re-running a policy — so no GPU was needed and none was faked. Rows and examples are **byte-identical** to the previous board; only the provenance envelope moved.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `commit` | `a5fdd13` | `9e39ef2` |
| `generated_at` | 2026-07-04 | today |
| `signature` | **null** | ed25519, keyid `5b9a65790d93d0bc` |
| `inputs_digest` | `7b493125…` | `280401608e…` (matches the report as it exists today) |

> **Correction to the brief:** it said 22 releases behind. The real figure is **8 released tags** — `a5fdd13` first shipped in `v0.18.0`. The guard reports the accurate number.

**Signing reused the existing path, not a second scheme.** `sign_leaderboard` already wrapped `attest.sign_bytes` with its own DSSE payload type. The gap was operational — nobody had run it with a persistent key.

**Schema v2 → v3 fixes an honesty problem re-stamping creates.** A rebuild moves `generated_at` to today while every row still carries a measurement made with tool `0.1.0`. `measured_with` records the versions the *numbers* came from; `is_restamp()` answers it directly. This board: `measured_with: ["0.1.0"]`, `is_restamp() == True`.

**Verify it yourself** (no network trust in this PR):
```bash
provael leaderboard verify --in leaderboard/results/leaderboard.json \
  --pubkey leaderboard/results/leaderboard.pub
# -> leaderboard OK  keyid 5b9a65790d93d0bc
```
Tamper-tested: flipping one success count returns `INVALID` and exits 1.

**Three CI guards** so it cannot rot: signed; signature verifies **against the published key** (a signature under an unpublished key is worse than none — a buyer following our docs would get `INVALID`); build commit ≤ **3 released tags** behind. Three because re-stamping is a GPU-free one-command operation, while failing every release would be noise. Both mutation-tested.

**The `/leaderboard` disclosure block is untouched** — four rows is still not a survey, two of three adversarial families still measured 0%.

## 2 · Checkpoint supply-chain integrity in the gate

`SECURITY.md` documents **CVE-2026-25874** — LeRobot unauthenticated pickle-deserialization RCE (CVSS 9.8), `lerobot` through `0.5.1`, in the async-inference `PolicyServer` which `pickle.loads` untrusted payloads over an unauthenticated gRPC endpoint. **Provael never starts that PolicyServer**, so that path isn't reachable through Provael — but loading *any* third-party pickle executes it. The tool named the risk publicly; the Action didn't check for it.

Runs **before any policy is instantiated** — the check is worthless after the load. Two controls, **both fail-closed**, each with an explicit opt-out that is *recorded in the evidence*, never silent:

- **Pinned SHA-256** over the weight files. **No pin is a failure**, not a pass — "we did not check" and "we checked and it matched" must not produce the same verdict. Digest is order- and layout-independent, so a pin re-checks anywhere.
- **Pickle refused** without opt-in. Where safetensors are also present the checkpoint is loadable safely, so `mixed` passes with a finding saying which to load.

Full fail-closed matrix, all verified:

| case | verdict |
|---|---|
| correct pin, safetensors | pass |
| **wrong pin** | **fail** |
| **no pin (default)** | **fail** |
| no pin + explicit opt-out | pass |
| **pickle, no opt-in** | **fail** |
| pickle + explicit opt-in | pass |
| **never fetched** | **fail** |

### EAI mapping — EAI03, not EAI07

**EAI03 — Model & pipeline poisoning, backdoors & supply chain.** The mapping is in the title. Deliberately **not** EAI07: that entry declares CPS/firmware/teleop out of scope *for attacks*, and filing a control there would imply this closes part of that scope. It does not. The PolicyServer RCE has an EAI07 flavour; what the gate inspects is the checkpoint artifact.

### ⚠️ Honesty boundary — enforced, not just asserted

This is a **supply-chain control**. It emits a **verdict, never a rate**, and does **not** reduce attack success — a checkpoint passing every check can still be driven off-task at exactly the rate the ASR reports.

- In SARIF it is nested under `checkpointIntegrity`, **never flattened beside `adversarialAsr`**
- The record carries that sentence in a `note` field, so it survives being pasted into a slide
- A test asserts the evidence contains **no rate-shaped key at all** (`asr` / `successes` / `attempts` / `ci95`)

## Test plan

`uv sync --locked` · `ruff` clean · `mypy src` clean (87 files) · **650 passed, 13 skipped** · `mkdocs build --strict` clean · `uv build && twine check` both PASSED · registry + manifest + assurance + version-consistency goldens all green.

Release-blocker check: `release.yml`'s `fetch-depth: 0` (bf7bef52, which unblocked 0.26.0) is **still present** — confirmed before tagging.

## ⚠️ Two things that need your action

**1. The signing private key is on my disk, not in the repo.** `.gitignore` had *no* key rules at all despite a workflow already consuming `secrets.PROVAEL_SIGNING_KEY`; now `*.pem`/`*.key` are ignored with an explicit negation for the published `.pub`. The private key is at `provael-leaderboard-signing.pem` (chmod 600, gitignored, never printed). **Move it into `secrets.PROVAEL_SIGNING_KEY` and delete the local copy** — without it nobody can re-sign, and the freshness guard will start failing in 3 releases.

**2. Signing this board BREAKS a bullet on www.provael.com.** `/leaderboard`'s honesty block hard-codes *"The payload is unsigned."* as static text while only the value is dynamic, so it will render:

> **The payload is unsigned.** `signature` is `present` … **no cryptographic attestation of origin**

The website fetches this board at **build time from `main`**, so it self-contradicts on the next deploy with nobody touching it — and now *understates* the product. Needs a website PR; flagged for the provael.com prompt along with the `/continuous-assurance` update for what the gate now checks.

author: vitenti
body:
## Summary
- **Root fix**: `NcGalaxyShapeFactorFixedQuad` gets an opt-in `use-pop-correction` that fixes a real ~18% worst-case error for alpha<2 Beta intrinsic-ellipticity populations, caused by the pointwise `P_pop(r)/(2*pi*r)` divergence near a domain node's `chi_I=0` crossing. A quintic-smoothstep window (exact partition of unity, cancellation-safe) tapers the cached grid to zero in a small region and replaces it with a cheap native-`chi_I`-polar sub-quadrature that cancels the `1/r` via the polar measure instead of resolving it. `use-marginal-spline` inherits the fix automatically since both paths share the same evaluation function.
- **Rotation-covariance fix**: FixedQuad's "contained" branches placed their angular quadrature on an absolute grid instead of one rotated with `eps_obs`, breaking the exact `P(eps*e^{ia}|g*e^{ia})=P(eps|g)` identity (up to 96% off before the fix).
- **Cache-miss fix**: rotate the reduced shear into the galaxy frame instead of rotating the observed ellipticity, so `epsilon_obs` is a genuine per-galaxy constant and FixedQuad's per-galaxy domain/spline cache actually gets reused across walkers (previously invalidated every call whenever ra/dec were free parameters).
- **Interface cleanup**: collapsed `NcGalaxyShapePop`'s `eval_p(x)`/`eval_p_rho2(rho2)` vfuncs into a single r-native `eval_p(r)=P_pop(r)` contract, removing a dead vfunc and per-subclass Jacobian duplication.
- **New CLI tools**: `inspect galaxy-shape-integrand` (heatmap the shear-marginalization integrand for one galaxy, multi-panel with linked pan/zoom and a shared colorbar) and `catalog check-m2lnl` (recompute -2lnL for catalog rows against current code, for validating old catalogs after a likelihood-affecting change).
- Fixed FixedQuad's marginal-spline cache to build a fixed-knot fallback (instead of disabling caching) when a population is unsafe for the adaptive autoknots build.

## Test plan
- [x] Full `tests/python/nc/lss/galaxy/` suite: 448/448 passing
- [x] `tests/c/nc_galaxy_shape_pop_series`, `tests/c/nc_galaxy_shape_intrinsic_mode`: passing
- [x] New regression tests added for pop-correction (real hard-case accuracy, rotation covariance, no regression on smooth populations, gobject property round-trip), rotation covariance, and marginal-spline fixed-knot caching
- [x] Verified against real production catalog (`exp_007_v5`) and against an independent scipy oracle

author: tedeuxx
body:
Closes the **plugin half** of [tedeuxx/tadeumendonca-io#202](https://github.com/tedeuxx/tadeumendonca-io/issues/202). Replaces #80, which is closed — same slice, rebuilt on a fresh branch because its commit subject used `process:`, a type that appears nowhere in this repo's history, and correcting it would have meant a force-push.

## Why this was still open

`-io`#233 replaced that repo's boundary-path **enumeration** with a fail-closed **rule**. But the gate that actually fires does not read that repo's guide — it reads this plugin, and `agents/critical-reviewer.md` still said:

> content is boundary **by path**, not by directory

So the consuming repo had adopted the rule while the reviewer was still pattern-matching a path list. That gap is the whole reason `-io`#202 survived #233.

## What changes

The trigger tests **what a diff changes**, not where it lives:

> If a diff changes **words or images any reader will see — human or machine** — on the product, in a crawler's card, or on any external surface the work publishes to, the review is incomplete until `brand-guardian` returns a verdict. The file they live in is irrelevant: prose, a data field, a meta tag, alt text, an OG image, `robots.txt`, a literal inside a component, a constant in a build script a generator emits into a post. A repo guide may enumerate today's content paths; that list is an **aid, never the definition**.

"Human or machine" is load-bearing rather than flourish, and it is a correction `brand-guardian` made to my first draft: the OG/unfurl class — copy a scraper pins and a person then reads on someone else's timeline — is exactly what this rule exists for, and *"a person will see"* reads as excluding it. `-io`'s own rule already said "a reader **or a crawler**"; mine was the looser of the two while claiming to be the superset.

## Why a rule and not a list

An enumeration **fails open** — anything unlisted reads as safe class and merges with no copy review at all. Twice now, both caught by accident rather than by the gate:

- **`-io`#233** — the portfolio-copy module sat outside the list, so edits to *published* copy classified as safe class.
- **`-io`#202** — a generator constant held a hashtag set **bound for** a post scaffold the owner voices and publishes under his own name, in a path classified as build tooling. `brand-guardian` never ran, and the set the generator first emitted had been **invented by the agent**, against that repo's explicit *"do not write positioning copy from memory."*

**A near-miss, not a breach** — and getting that straight was `brand-guardian`'s blocking finding on the first draft. I had told the same incident three different ways across three files: two said the set was "posted under the owner's own name", one said it was caught before publication. Those are incompatible, two clauses apart. The record says it was corrected before use, and only because someone reading an unrelated issue's comments happened to notice the owner had already stated his own set. All three files now tell that one account.

## Why not the marker convention #202 preferred

Rejected **as the sole gate**, not outright — the ADR now concedes where the marker is genuinely better and I had argued past it. A check can assert a *listed* path still exists, catching a rename; it cannot catch **omission**, which is the failure that happens. But a marker's real advantage is **locality**: it is applied at the site of authorship, by the person writing the copy, at the moment they write it, while a path list is edited in a distant file by someone who must remember it exists. Same failure reason, materially different miss rate. So: viable as a complement, rejected only as the thing the gate rests on.

The amendment also now names that this rule is `-io`#202's own **option 3**, which that issue judged *"probably too fuzzy to be a gate"* — adopting the option the issue doubted is a claim, and it should be visible rather than quietly made.

## Cost, stated

A rule is applied by judgement and will over-trigger. That is the direction the error should point.

It **cannot be tested** — no assertion decides whether a string is reader-facing. But the first draft said that made it unobservable, which `critical-reviewer` corrected: `critical-reviewer` already owes a mandatory disclosure on every MR (*report the verdict, or say it did not run*), so under-application leaves a trace and is auditable after the fact. That disclosure is the only instrument this rule has, which makes it load-bearing rather than a courtesy.

## Applying the rule to itself

`brand-guardian` **ran on this PR**, deliberately — installing a fail-closed trigger and not firing it on the first diff that arguably meets it would have set exactly the wrong precedent.

Its verdict was **ADJUST**, and the adjustments are in. Its scoping is worth recording, because it draws a line this repo did not have: the trigger fires on this repo's `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/**` **because `CLAUDE.md` declares the repo a public knowledge-transfer artifact and CV differentiator** — not because process prose is generally reader-facing. In a plugin repo making no positioning claim about itself, an ADR amendment about a review gate would be safe class. The standing cost of keeping that mission claim as broad as it is: every substantive doc change here triggers a copy review.

Confidentiality checked and clean — nothing from the gitignored `.brand/` layer is quoted, paraphrased or reconstructible, and no client or employer is named. The one quoted phrase traces to `-io`'s own public `CLAUDE.md`.

## Files

- `agents/critical-reviewer.md` — the trigger, the fail-open reasoning, the no-check-can-enforce reasoning.
- `agents/brand-guardian.md` — its frontmatter `description`, which is what agent selection reads.
- `CLAUDE.md` — the roster paragraph carried the same stale wording.
- `docs/proposals/agentic-dev-loop.md` — the persona's live description; missed by my first sweep, found by the reviewer.
- `docs/adr/0002-…` + `docs/adr/README.md` — **amendment #4**, plus an inline supersession pointer in amendment #1's Decision text so a reader landing there is not left with the old rule.

## Gates

Docs/agents-only diff. `hooks-test` is path-filtered to `hooks/**` and **does not match** — stating that rather than letting a non-running check read as a passing one. `claude-review` reports `skipping` by its own `base.ref != 'main'` condition, which can never hold in a trunk repo. No code, no dependency, no hook behaviour touched.

## Filed, not fixed here

- **#81** — `CLAUDE.md`'s Mission section states a target role that does not match the positioning source. Found by `brand-guardian` the moment this PR put these docs in scope. Boundary, and the correct wording comes from the owner's private source.
- **#82** — the roster count contradicts itself (18 vs 19) and one persona is named `e2e-testing` where the file is `qa-e2e`.

## After merge

`.brand/surfaces.md` still describes the by-path framing this supersedes. It is gitignored so it cannot travel in a PR, and it is the thing that gets forgotten — flagged here so it doesn't.

## Class

**Boundary** — it changes what the content gate inspects, which is the review mechanism itself, and it amends an ADR decision. `critical-reviewer` agreed and will not merge it; the go/no-go is the owner's.

author: ggarzia-msft
body:
This pull request adds robust CSV parsing and escaping utilities to the shared string library, updates secret spec parsing for Docker compatibility, and introduces comprehensive unit tests to ensure correctness and round-trip fidelity. The main goal is to match Docker's `buildx` handling of CSV values (via Go's `encoding/csv`), ensuring correct parsing of quoted fields, embedded commas, and malformed input.

**CSV parsing and escaping utilities:**

* Added a template function `SplitCsvFields` to parse a single CSV record according to RFC 4180 and Go's `encoding/csv`, handling quoted fields, embedded commas, escaped quotes, and malformed input detection.
* Added `CsvEscapeField` to escape individual fields for CSV output, quoting fields as needed and doubling embedded quotes, and `JoinCsvFields` to join fields into a CSV record, ensuring round-trip parseability.
* Included `<optional>` to support the use of `std::optional` in parsing functions.

**Integration with secret spec parsing:**

* Updated `ParseSecretSpec` to use `SplitCsvFields`, ensuring Docker-compatible parsing of `--secret` specs, including proper handling of quoted fields and malformed input rejection.

**Testing:**

* Added a new test file `WSLCCsvSharedUnitTests.cpp` with unit tests covering all aspects of the CSV parsing and escaping logic, including round-trip tests and malformed input handling, for both wide and narrow string types.

body:
Pulls the format-conformance component of the declarative programme's check phase forward (orchestrator directives `DIR-PU-DA-declarative-surface` Phase 6, `DIR-PU-DA-baseltest-parity` item 5) so future format amendments get their test surface from the published corpus instead of hand-mirrored unit tests. Reference adoption: baseltest's `test_format_conformance.py`.

## The gate

- **`fetchPublishedFormats`** build task: the corpus bundle from the latest mavai-R release on every build (mirrors punit-report's schema fetch; `-PformatsDir` sources a local checkout).
- **`FormatConformanceTest`** drives the format layer over every corpus case — contract parse + the load-time construction walk (views resolve, selection expressions compile, criteria validate eagerly), and full services-file resolution under exactly the corpus's `requires:` registrations. Environment fail-fasts (endpoint/model defaults) get placeholders: the corpus binds format outcomes, not environment.
- **Binding obligations asserted per case**: outcome, and refusal *category* via a 73-entry map from category to punit's own refusal wording (wording is informational per the manifest's contract; the fragment check is what makes a wrong-reason refusal fail).
- **The obligation diff**: the run diffs its assertions against the manifest's full obligation — selective assertion fails the build, and the diff itself is mutation-tested. Manifest↔tree and category-registry checks included.
- **Known-unmet ledger, asserted inverted**: obligations punit does not yet meet pass only while unmet — the day one is met, the build fails until the entry is removed. Today: the eleven named-path-anchors (`roots:`) cases of mavai-R v0.10.5 (family amendment 2026-07-29; the punit twin directive will retire them).

## First catch (production fix included)

An optimization `initial:` overlay restating the baseline configuration **loaded silently**; the services format mandates refusal (iteration 0 is the baseline by default). Now refused in `ServicesResolver` beside the twin duplicate-point rule.

## Notes

- `testRuntimeOnly(project(":punit-lm"))` puts the family's `language-model` type on the gate's classpath — punit-lm's main source depends on punit-decl's, so the task graph stays acyclic.
- Blast radius: 4 files, +536.
- Full build green against the live v0.10.5 corpus.

author: shoumikhin
body:
## Why this is needed

Today, using the ExecuTorch runtime from a C++ program means building
ExecuTorch from source: clone the repo, sync submodules, and run a CMake
build before you can compile and link your own runner. The pip wheel only
ships the Python runtime module (`_portable_lib`) plus a small set of
headers meant for authoring custom operators. There is no way to just
`pip install executorch` and link a standalone C++ application against the
runtime.

This is friction for anyone whose deployment path is C++ (the common case
for on-device inference) and who already has the wheel installed for
export. The runtime is compiled during the wheel build and then discarded.

This change ships the runtime as a linkable shared library, its public
headers, and a CMake package config inside the Linux wheel, so a C++
program can link the ExecuTorch runtime with no source checkout and no
separate build.

## What is inside

Added to the Linux wheel (nothing removed; other platforms unchanged):

- `executorch/lib/libexecutorch.so` (SONAME-versioned, with the standard
  `libexecutorch.so -> .so.1 -> .so.<version>` chain): the consolidated
  shared runtime. It bundles the runtime core plus the common runtime
  extensions (module, tensor, data_loader, flat_tensor, named_data_map).
- `executorch/include/executorch/extension/...`: the public headers for the
  Module, Tensor, DataLoader, FlatTensor (.ptd reader), NamedDataMap, and
  header-only MallocMemoryAllocator APIs. Runtime/Program/backend headers
  were already shipped and are reused.
- `executorch/share/cmake/executorch-config.cmake`: a CMake package config
  that exposes an `executorch::runtime` imported target (plus convenience
  aliases `executorch::core`, `executorch::extension_*`).
- `executorch/utils/cmake_prefix_path`: a small helper (mirrors
  `torch.utils.cmake_prefix_path`) so CMake can find the config in one line.

## Why a shared library (not static archives)

The runtime is shipped shared on purpose. ExecuTorch keeps a single
process-global backend/kernel registry. Shipping the runtime as one shared
`libexecutorch.so` lets a separately distributed backend or delegate shared
library register into that one registry: the backend `.so` is built without
its own copy of the runtime (its `register_backend` reference is undefined
and resolves against `libexecutorch.so` at load), and its static-init
registration runs when the `.so` is loaded (via whole-archive for a C++ app,
or an explicit import/dlopen for Python, which is how ExecuTorch already
ships the QNN backend today). Static archives would give each consumer its
own private registry, which cannot support loading multiple independently
distributed backends into one runtime.

The set is intentionally libtorch-free and excludes the general CPU
operator/kernel libraries, because a delegate supplies its own compute. It
is also Linux only: the `.so` naming and SONAME symlink chain are Unix
specific, so the Windows and macOS wheels are byte-identical to before.

## How to use it

```bash
pip install executorch
```

```cmake
find_package(executorch CONFIG REQUIRED)

add_executable(my_runner main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(my_runner PRIVATE executorch::runtime)
```

```bash
cmake -S . -B build \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$(python -c 'import executorch.utils as u; print(u.cmake_prefix_path)')"
cmake --build build
```

Existing consumers that use `find_package(executorch)` to link the Python
`_portable_lib` for custom-op extensions keep working unchanged. The new
C++ SDK availability is reported separately via `EXECUTORCH_SDK_FOUND`, so
the legacy `EXECUTORCH_FOUND` / `EXECUTORCH_LIBRARIES` contract is
preserved.

## Test plan

Verified on Linux x86_64:

- Built the wheel with `python setup.py bdist_wheel` and confirmed it
  contains `libexecutorch.so` with its SONAME symlink chain, the CMake
  config, the `utils` helper, and the new extension headers, and that
  headers with no shipped implementation are excluded.
- Installed the wheel into a clean virtual environment and built a small
  standalone C++ runner against it with `find_package(executorch)` and
  `executorch.utils.cmake_prefix_path`. The runner compiled, linked, ran,
  and initialized the runtime.
- Built a separate "coreless" backend shared library (no bundled runtime,
  `register_backend` left undefined) and confirmed that loading it against
  the installed `libexecutorch.so` registers the backend into the runtime's
  registry (`get_backend_class` goes from not-found to found). This is the
  mechanism that lets independently distributed backends coalesce into one
  runtime.
- Confirmed the runner and the runtime link no libtorch/libc10 (via `ldd`).
- Confirmed the Windows and macOS wheel code paths add nothing new, so those
  wheels are unaffected.
- Lint and format pass (flake8, ufmt, cmake-format).

Known limitation: the wheel-build step stores the SONAME symlinks as plain
file copies rather than symlinks. Linking and loading still work because the
SONAME target is present as a real file; a follow-up can preserve them as
true symlinks to save space.

## CI

Adds a PR job (test-cpp-sdk-wheel-linux in pull.yml, calling
.ci/scripts/test_cpp_sdk_wheel.sh) that builds the wheel, installs it into a
clean venv, and uses find_package(executorch) to build a C++ consumer linking
executorch::runtime, then loads a coreless backend shared library and asserts
it registers into libexecutorch.so. This gives the feature direct coverage:
before, no PR job built the full wheel or linked the C++ SDK.

body:
Why:
Reference-server inspection (simulator infra/mcp_server.py, permitted read) shows each peer's FastMCP tools are pure mailboxes: they enqueue the opponent's message and always return {"ok": true}. Validating synchronously and mapping ProtocolError to a ToolError breaks interop — a peer that retries on any transport exception aborts the exchange, and a tampered audit would surface as a transport error instead of being recorded as the sender's technical loss. So the server acks transport and validation is decoupled.

Changes:
- adapters/fastmcp_server.py: PeerInboxes (four thread-safe queues); build_server exposes negotiate/receive_turn/submit_audit/receive_control as enqueue-and-ack tools that never raise; drain() feeds each queued message through the M5-01 InboundPeer, returning Delivery(tool, accepted, reason) — a rejection is a game-level outcome, not a transport error.
- adapters/__init__.py: package for transport adapters; only place fastmcp enters. The transport-neutral core (peer/, sdk/) still imports no fastmcp (guarded test).
- ADR-002 amended: receive tools are pure transport acks; schema/transition/audit failures are game outcomes, surfaced on drain, not transport errors.
- pyproject: add fastmcp>=3.4.5,<4 (SR-005: each peer is a FastMCP server); uv.lock updated.

author: filo6699
body:
## Summary

- H004: add a TCP listener with one sequential command loop per connection and context-driven graceful shutdown.
- Parse strict `region://token@host:port/` endpoints, including bracketed IPv6.
- Add required server CLI flags for listen address, data directory, authentication token, and geometry.
- Coordinate in-process chunk readers/writers and serialize protocol read-modify-write operations.
- Cover URI edge cases, real loopback TCP, shutdown, and concurrent storage access.

## Explicitly out of scope

- TLS and the `regions://` scheme.
- WAL, checkpoints, durability modes, caches, worker pools, binary transfer commands, metrics, and default port behavior.
- Formal versioned protocol, storage, and concurrency specifications.

## Wire/on-disk/CLI impact

- Wire: existing text commands are now served over TCP; command syntax and response encoding are unchanged.
- URI: accepts only `region://token@host:port/`; no default port is inferred.
- CLI: adds `-listen`, `-data-dir`, `-token`, `-chunk-edge`, `-large-chunk-edge`, `-block-bits`, and `-version`. Runtime flags have no implicit production defaults.
- On-disk: `fs_split_v1` bytes and path layout are unchanged.

## Validation

All local checks passed:

```text
test -z "$(gofmt -l <repository Go files>)"
go mod tidy
git diff --exit-code -- go.mod go.sum
go vet ./...
go test ./...
go build ./...
golangci-lint run
go test -race ./...
go test -count=1 ./...
go test -run TestServeLoopback -count=20 ./internal/server
go test -run TestStoreConcurrentReadsAndWrites -count=20 ./internal/storage/fs_split
scripts/git/verify-history.sh
```

## Benchmark evidence

Not applicable; this change does not claim a performance improvement.

## Migration/rollback

No storage migration is required. Rollback requires stopping the TCP process and reverting these commits; existing `fs_split_v1` data remains compatible.

## Release note

Add the first authenticated TCP server runtime, strict region URI parsing, configurable server CLI, and safe in-process concurrent chunk access.

body:
**Linear:** [FIX-978](https://linear.app/fixpoint-labs/issue/FIX-978) · **Spec doc:** `docs/specs/FIX-978.md` · **Epic:** [FIX-980 — Honest task substrate](https://linear.app/fixpoint-labs/issue/FIX-980) ([epic PR #983](https://github.com/fixpoint-labs/flow-state-dev/pull/983))

Docs-only. No changeset (BP-022). This PR is never merged — it is closed unmerged when implementation starts.

---

## For reviewers — what this document is

This is a **direction document**, not an implementation. Reviewing it well means
answering one question: **is this the right approach?**

**In scope to challenge:**

- The problem framing — are we solving the right thing?
- The approach — will it work, does it fit the architecture and `docs/philosophy.md`?
- Any numbered **Decision** in §6 — that's the sign-off surface.
- Missing constraints, edge cases, or dependencies that would **invalidate** the design.
- Scope — a deliverable that shouldn't ship, or one that's missing.

**Out of scope — deliberately unsettled here, and owned by the implementing agent:**

- Names, signatures, file paths, and module layout.
- Local structure: which helper, how a function is decomposed, error-message wording.
- Micro-optimizations and style preferences.
- Test names and internal test structure (the *behaviours* to test are in §10; the tests
  themselves are not).
- Anything Part II left open on purpose — it is directional by design, and a gap at
  that altitude is intended, not an omission.

Feedback in the second list is welcome and gets **recorded verbatim in §13** for the
implementer to weigh against real code. It will not be argued with, and it will not be
folded into the design prose — that would pretend the spec can settle something it
can't. Please don't re-raise it: one mention is enough for it to land in §13.

> **One reviewer-specific note for this spec.** Its central constraint is *negative*:
> **an expired lease is not evidence of abandonment** (epic Decision 3). The default
> lease is 30s, nothing renews it, and a model call routinely exceeds it — so a healthy
> worker's lease is expired most of the time. Any suggestion of the form "just call
> `reclaim()` / just skip expired leases" has been weighed and rejected in §3 with the
> reasoning; it trades a hang for silent duplicate execution. If you want to challenge
> that, challenge the reasoning in §3 rather than re-proposing the mechanism.

---

## Part I — The Case

### 1. Problem — why it matters, why now

**In plain language.** A task board hands each unit of work to a worker, and marks that
work "in progress" while the worker runs. If the process dies at exactly the wrong
moment — a crash, a restart, a deploy — the work stays marked "in progress" forever,
because the thing that would clean it up is never called. The next time anything tries
to run that board, it waits for a worker that no longer exists. It waits for about
fourteen hours. Then it gives up and reports the wrong reason: it says the work is
*blocked on a dependency*, which is not what happened at all.

Two separate failures, and the second is the worse one. The wait is expensive. The
report is *dishonest* — a caller who reads it and acts on it acts on a false cause.

**Why now.** This is live today, not a future hazard. Any board built on a collection
that outlives a single turn reaches it — the code-first durable path
(`defineTaskCollection` + `taskBoard`) — and the framework ships that path as a
supported way to build a board. There is no workaround a caller can adopt without
taking a worse risk: the one recovery verb that exists, `reclaim()`, resets *any*
expired claim, and a healthy worker's claim expires as a matter of routine (see §3),
so calling it blindly re-runs live work and duplicates its side effects. The user is
currently choosing between a fourteen-hour hang and silent duplicate execution.

This is the fifth instance of the epic's shape: **the substrate's report diverges from
what happened and the caller cannot detect the divergence.** Here the divergence is
that the board reports `blocked` when it is actually stranded, and takes most of a day
to say so.

### 2. Solution in plain terms

The board already has an exit for "I cannot make progress" — the `complete-or-blocked`
mode exists to stop a drain that has nothing left it can run. That exit asks the wrong
question. It asks *"does the collection contain zero in-progress rows?"* when what it
means is *"is any worker of mine actually working?"* Those two questions have the same
answer right up until a row is held by something that isn't a live worker of this
drain — which is precisely the stranded case, and precisely when the board needs the
exit most.

**So: make the board measure the thing it was standing in for.** A drain knows which
tasks its own workers claimed, because every claim in a drain goes through one block.
Record them. Then the exit condition becomes: *no claim of mine is outstanding, and
nothing here is claimable.* When that is true the drain cannot progress, whether the
in-progress rows belong to a dead prior execution or a live concurrent one — so it
stops, promptly, and **names the real cause**: a claim is held outside this run.

What it deliberately does **not** do is decide whether that other claim's owner is
alive. It does not need to, because it never writes to the row. It reports and exits;
the row is left exactly as it was found. That is what makes this safe under the epic's
Decision 3 — the constraint is that expiry is not evidence of abandonment, and this
design never infers abandonment at all.

**The philosophy this leans on.**

- **Tenet 5 (fix at the owning layer, at the convergence point).** The hang is
  reproducible from the delegation surface, from `planAndExecute`, from a hand-built
  board — every one of them through `taskBoard`. `taskBoard` is where they converge, so
  the fix goes there and cures all of them, rather than each caller learning to call
  `reclaim()` defensively. The same tenet picks the seam *inside* the board: every claim
  passes through one claim block, so the ledger has exactly one writer.
- **Tenet 1 (coherence over local cleverness).** `count(in_progress) === 0` is not a
  weaker version of "no worker is active" — it is a different predicate that happened
  to agree. Replacing the proxy with the property removes an incoherence rather than
  adding a special case on top of it.
- **Tenet 3 (earn every addition).** The temptation here is to build the whole recovery
  mechanism: a claim-ownership field, lease renewal, an automatic sweeper. All three are
  already scoped as FIX-939 milestone 2 and none of them is needed to stop lying to the
  caller. This spec ships the honesty and leaves the recovery where it was already
  planned.

### 3. Tradeoffs & alternatives

**The simpler approach, and why it loses.** Call `collection.reclaim()` before each
drain. It is three lines, it exists today, and it makes the reported symptom go away. It
is also wrong, and this is the load-bearing fact of the whole issue:

- `DEFAULT_LEASE_DURATION_MS` is 30 seconds
  (`packages/orchestration/src/tasks/collection/internal.ts`).
- **Nothing renews a lease.** `leaseUntil` is stamped once by `applyClaimToTask` at claim
  time and thereafter only ever *cleared* on a terminal transition — never extended. A
  grep for `renew` / `heartbeat` / `extendLease` across `packages/orchestration/src/`
  returns nothing.
- A generator's model call routinely runs longer than 30 seconds.

Therefore **an expired lease is the normal state of a healthy long-running worker.**
A pre-drain `reclaim()` resets that worker's task to `pending`, a second worker claims
it, and the model call plus its side effects run twice — with the first worker's
eventual write-back declined by FIX-951's containment guard, silently. That trades a
loud fourteen-hour hang for silent duplicate execution, which is strictly worse. The
same objection kills the variant "teach the wake predicate to ignore expir

The implementation focuses on semantic HTML structure, client-centric content, and a layout foundation ready for responsive CSS styling. --- ## 🎯 What Was Implemented The services section has been expanded from a placeholder into a complete, professional content block featuring **5 distinct AML/CFT service offerings** presented in a card-based grid structure. 🛠️ Technical Approach ### HTML Structure The services section (`section#services`) follows this semantic hierarchy: ``` section#services ├── h2 "Our Services" ├── p (introductory paragraph) └── div.services-grid ├── article.service-card │ ├── i.fa-solid.fa-shield-halved (icon) │ ├── h3 "Compliance Program Development" │ └── p (description) ├── article.service-card │ ├── i.fa-solid.fa-chart-line │ ├── h3 "AML/CFT Risk Assessments" │ └── p (description) ├── article.service-card │ ├── i.fa-solid.fa-file-contract │ ├── h3 "Regulatory Reporting & Filing" │ └── p (description) ├── article.service-card │ ├── i.fa-solid.fa-chalkboard-user │ ├── h3 "Staff Training & Awareness" │ └── p (description) └── article.service-card ├── i.fa-solid.fa-handshake ├── h3 "Advisory & Remediation Services" └── p (description) ``` ### Design Decisions - **`

` headings, and `

All changes are contained within `index.html`. --- ## 🧪 Testing Instructions Since this is an HTML-only change with no build process, testing is straightforward: ### Manual Verification Steps 1. **Clone/checkout this branch** locally ```bash git checkout feature/services-section-content ``` 2. **Open `index.html`** directly in a browser (no server required): ```bash open index.html # macOS start index.html # Windows xdg-open index.html # Linux ``` 3. **Verify the following:** - [ ] Page loads without console errors - [ ] Font Awesome icons render correctly for all 5 service cards (requires internet connection for CDN) - [ ] All 5 service cards are visible on the page - [ ] Each card displays: icon → H3 heading → descriptive paragraph - [ ] The `H2` section heading ("Our Services") is present - [ ] Introductory paragraph appears below the H2 - [ ] Inspect the DOM — confirm `div.services-grid` wraps all `article.service-card` elements 4. **Validate HTML structure** (optional but recommended): - Paste the contents of `index.html` into the [W3C Markup Validator](https://validator.w3.org/#validate_by_input) - Confirm no errors related to the services section 5. **Test icon fallback** (offline scenario): - Disable network access and reload the page - Icons will not render, but text content (headings and descriptions) should remain fully readable — confirming graceful degradation --- ## 🚀 Deployment Notes - **No deployment pipeline** is configured for this project at this stage - This is a **static HTML file** — deployment consists of uploading/pushing `index.html` to the target hosting environment (e.g., GitHub Pages, Netlify, or a web server) - The Font Awesome CDN dependency requires **internet access** for end users to see icons; author: diberry
body:
## Summary

Step 4 `ToolFamilyPostAssemblyValidator` compared **documented** parameter names against **raw source CLI** option names. But the Annotations step renames identifier parameters to natural-language display names (CLI `--resource` → documented `Resource name`). With no reverse mapping, the validator wrongly reported:

- `parameter(s) documented but not present in source CLI JSON: 'resource-name'`
- `required source parameter(s) missing from article: 'resource'`

This was a hard Step 4 failure blocking generation for the 8 tools across 5 namespaces (advisor, applens, get, monitor, redis) that expose `--resource`.

## Fix

- Add `SourceVerificationHelpers.LoadNaturalLanguageReverseMap(mcpToolsRoot)` — loads `mcp-tools/data/nl-parameter-identifiers.json` and builds a `display-slug → CLI-name` reverse map (graceful empty dict if the file is missing/malformed).
- In `GetSourceVerificationIssues`, reverse-map each documented display slug to its canonical CLI name **before** both the extra-parameter and missing-required-parameter comparisons.
- Fully **service-agnostic** and data-driven — no hardcoded parameter or service names.

## Behavior preserved

- Genuinely-extra documented parameters are still flagged.
- Genuinely-missing required source parameters are still flagged.

## Tests (TDD)

- Converted the bug-encoding `ValidateAsync_Fails_WhenDocumentedParameterIsNotInSourceJson` into `ValidateAsync_Passes_WhenDocumentedParameterIsNaturalLanguageRename` (Key Vault `--resource` documented as `resource-name` → passes).
- Added `ValidateAsync_Fails_WhenDocumentedParameterIsGenuinelyNotInSourceJson` (Monitor, documents `region` → still fails).
- Added `ValidateAsync_Passes_WhenRequiredSourceParameterDocumentedAsNaturalLanguageRename` (Cosmos, required `--account` documented as `account-name` → passes).
- Seeded `nl-parameter-identifiers.json` in the test harness `McpToolsRoot`.
- Varied services across cases (Key Vault, Monitor, Cosmos) per the universal-design principle.

11/11 `ToolFamilySourceVerificationTests` pass; Release build is warning-free.

## Docs

- CHANGELOG `[Unreleased] > Fixed` updated (AD-026).

⚠️ Do not merge — pending team review.

author: andrewwhitecdw
body:
### Problem
fix: timestamp print ignores file/flush kwargs

### Fix
Replace:
```
    def print_with_timestamp(*args, **kwargs):
        now = datetime.datetime.now()
        formatted_date_time = now.strftime(time_format)

        builtin_print(f'[{formatted_date_time}] ', end='')  # print with time stamp
        builtin_print(*args, **kwargs)
```

with:
```
    def print_with_timestamp(*args, **kwargs):
        now = datetime.datetime.now()
        formatted_date_time = now.strftime(time_format)

        common_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in kwargs.items() if k in ('file', 'flush')}
        builtin_print(f'[{formatted_date_time}] ', end='', **common_kwargs)  # print with time stamp
        builtin_print(*args, **kwargs)
```

author: dandpb
body:
🚨 **Severity:** HIGH
💡 **Vulnerability:** Unhandled XSS susceptibility and application crash risk in `learner.ts`. Supposedly numeric fields (`aidi.current`, `aidi.thresholdAmber`, `aidi.thresholdRed`, `snapshot.curr`) were rendering using `.toFixed(2)` without any type validation or HTML escaping.
🎯 **Impact:** If an attacker or a corrupted state managed to inject string payloads into these fields, the application would either completely crash during rendering (because strings do not have `.toFixed()`), or if somehow bypassed, execute arbitrary injected scripts (XSS).
🔧 **Fix:** Added a `formatNumeric` inline helper that checks `typeof value === "number"`. If true, it formats securely; otherwise, it sanitizes the payload through `escapeHtml(value)`. Also updated regression tests using `as any` casting to verify payloads are caught.
✅ **Verification:** Run `pnpm test` in `engines/codexDojo` and ensure tests pass, specifically `escapeCoverage.test.ts` where payloads are now actively injected and confirmed safely rendered as strings.
