author: orbintsoft
body:
## Summary

A process change, prompted by a defect that a green suite at full coverage could
never have caught.

The reactive askpass broker is dead on macOS — and on any desktop without
`kdialog`, GNOME included. `askpassEnv` gates the `SSH_ASKPASS` exports behind a
kdialog-only `guiAvailable()`, so `ssh` never calls the broker and the wallet is
never consulted after a key expires from the agent. The promise this breaks was
already written down, in the first document a user reads:

> The first `ssh` to a key you haven't used yet prompts for its passphrase once;
> every use after that — **in this shell** and every new login shell — is silent.

Three things kept it invisible, and each is a process failure rather than a
missing test:

- **The mock sits on the seam.** Every unit test of `askpassEnv` stubs
  `guiAvailable = func() bool { return true }` — the decision that *is* the bug
  is asserted away by the tests meant to judge it.
- **The one headless test asserts nothing.** `cover_remaining_test.go:206` runs
  with `guiAvailable = false`, sends stdout to `io.Discard`, and checks only the
  exit code. It passes whether the exports are emitted or not, and its name
  claims the case is covered.
- **The matrix waived it circularly.** `docs/TEST-MATRIX.md:81` states that
  `SSH_ASKPASS` tampering "has no observable effect without a live GUI" — true
  *only because of the defect*. The consequence became the justification for not
  testing it.

The underlying cause is that tests were derived from the implementation rather
than from what the product claims. A test written that way can only ever agree
with the code, including where the code is wrong. Line coverage rewards it
exactly.

### What this adds

**`docs/FEATURES.md`** — the missing referent. Twenty user-visible promises, each
with a stable id and a "How you can tell" column stating how to check it from
outside the program, written without reference to any implementation. Ids are
never reused, so `F6` means the same thing to a test, a matrix row and a bug
report forever.

**Five rules in `CLAUDE.md`** (21-25): document the feature before implementing
it; test the promise, not the implementation (unit tests own code correctness,
integration/e2e own functionality); red before green, with the commit saying how
the test was made to fail; never stub the decision under test; "verified" means
the product ran, and linters/unit tests/coverage may not be reported as evidence
that a feature works.

**Rule 19 amended** — every ✅ names the feature it verifies, and a waiver must be
justified by something that *cannot exist*, never by how the product behaves
today.

**The `verify-e2e` skill** — the procedure: start from the promise before opening
the source, reproduce before diagnosing, choose an environment that can actually
fail, force the precondition (expired key without opening a new shell; no
`DISPLAY` *and* no `kdialog`; `setsid`), and assert on evidence of the path taken
— the session-log line naming the wallet — rather than an end state that
`AddKeysToAgent yes` could have produced instead.

### Notes for review

- **`F6` does not hold today.** It is listed as promised because the product
  promises it. Recording it is the point: the gap becomes visible instead of
  tacit. Fixing it is the next piece of work, and under rule 23 it starts with a
  test observed red on `master`.
- **`docs/FEATURES.md` is a first cut and wants your review.** It was derived
  from README, CLI.md, CONFIGURATION.md and the PLAN goals. These are your
  product's promises, so some may be worded wrong or missing outright — better
  corrected now, since tests will be derived from it from here on.
- No new file type: both new files are markdown, already covered by
  `markdownlint-cli2` (its glob honours `.gitignore`, and it picked both up), so
  rule 12 needs no new lint target.
- No code changes, so nothing here can affect behaviour.

## Checklist

- [x] Every commit is signed off (`git commit -s`) — this certifies the DCO
      (`DCO.txt`) and accepts the CLA (`CLA.md`). See `CONTRIBUTING.md` if the
      DCO check fails.
- [x] `make lint` passes. Run here: `markdownlint-cli2` at the pinned 0.22.1 (0
      errors, 18 files) and `lint-editorconfig`. The rest of `make lint` targets
      file types this PR does not touch.

author: quincyo
body:
Nothing on the Drive screen was ever on a clock: the only repaint driver is
the GPS recorder's subscribe(), which fires per fix — so the card and the
arrival times froze the moment fixes stopped (a Google-Maps hand-off
backgrounds the PWA, GPS denied, a phone not recording), and the only way to
unfreeze them was to leave Drive mode and tap the worklist's Download.

drive.js now runs an interval while the screen is open and refreshes on a
5-minute throttle, behind three gates that were all asked for: drive tracking
armed, the "Show driving stats" opt-in, and the screen being in front — plus
not backgrounded and online. The interval ticks every 30s, but that is retry
granularity, not the period; the five minutes live in a timestamp throttle so
a tick that lands during a Maps hand-off costs seconds, not a whole period.

The half that actually re-times the route is applyTodayAnchor(), not the
download: nothing in the pull rewrites order/day/scheduledEta. A day-cache
refresh alone moves the pace gauge's done count and nothing else, which is why
the existing 3-minute pull left the times reading stale. autoSync does the
list, then cacheRecentDays(1), then the re-anchor; PACE_REFRESH_MS goes 3 to 5
so the two pulls share one period.

An unattended refresh is not a Download with the prompts removed. A locally
done order must never come back — syncWorklist only runs right after a log and
no-ops offline, so a stop logged in a dead zone leaves the sheet saying
pending — hence preserveDone on the automatic path, and the pull is skipped
entirely while the offline queue is non-empty. No toast, no confirm, no
savePlan push, and no planAdvance (it ends in fillCapture and would let a
timer overwrite a half-typed capture form). refresh() re-matches the card by
destKey so a re-ordered route can't swap the house under the driver.

The row normalizer is shared by both paths now (applyDownloadedList), so the
manual and automatic landings can't drift. driveShowMetrics becomes a consent
gate rather than just a HUD switch, so its hint in Route tuning and the user
guide say so.

523 unit tests, plus the real Drive screen driven headless on a controlled
clock with the spine stubbed and every non-localhost request blocked: 17/17 —
the gate truth table, one fetch per period, an office-added order landing on
the card, the re-anchor writing ETAs, a done order staying done, and the
interval cleared on leaving the screen.

author: chefsale
body:
## Summary

`SortedSet`/`SortedMap` keep a **node-local** ordered index (`Column::SortedIndex`) guarded by a validity marker (`Column::SortedIndexMeta`) that holds the collection's `full_hash` as of the last (re)build. An ordered read (`iter`/`keys`/`range`/`first`/`last`) rebuilds the index only when `marker != current full_hash`.

`#3323` made the marker node-local and `#3328` made the sync/apply path (`Interface::apply_action` / `apply_delete_ref_action`) **clear** the marker whenever it links/unlinks a child. Both assume the only thing that stamps the marker *valid* is a mutation from an already-consistent index (or a rebuild). But `insert`/`remove` maintain the index **incrementally** (one `index_put`/`index_remove`) and then stamp the marker to the collection's **current** `full_hash` — which already reflects any children a prior sync-apply linked.

So a **local write that follows a sync re-stamps a valid marker over a stale index**:

1. sync delivers converged children `{a}` but **not** the node-local index (index fresh/empty, marker cleared).
2. local `insert("b")`: children become `{a,b}`, `index_put` writes only `b`, `stamp` records `marker = H({a,b})`.
3. index holds `{b}` while `marker == full-set hash`, so `index_marker_current()` is `true` → the next ordered read **skips the rebuild and serves the stale subset `{b}` forever**.

`contains`/`len` read the child list directly and converge; only the ordered readers diverge — the exact #3333 symptom.

### Why it surfaced JS-path-first (calimero-sdk-js#87)

The bug needs the peer's element applied **before** the local write commits. A Rust structured-root app's deferred root-merge is a silent no-op (`Entry<T>` framing vs bare decode), so its concurrent workflow inserts locally *before* the peer's element arrives and converges. The JS root path runs the real `__calimero_merge_root_state` + `write_pre_merged_root_state`, and its write path applies the peer's element first — deterministically hitting the sync-then-local-insert interleaving. The marker/index code is shared, so the fix is at the storage layer and covers both.

## Fix

Only maintain the ordered index incrementally + stamp the marker when the index was **already consistent with the child set (marker current) BEFORE the mutation**. When a sync left it stale, leave the marker stale so the next ordered read rebuilds from the full child set — exactly the invariant `ensure_index`'s own doc comment already promises ("the local insert path likewise leaves the marker stale, so both mutation paths funnel back through this one rebuild").

Steady-state single-writer stays O(1); the post-sync rebuild happens once on the next ordered read. Covers every incremental stamp site: `SortedSet` insert/remove, `SortedMap` insert (new-key + value-update restamp) / remove / `Entry` API. `clear()` is untouched (it empties both index and children, so it stays consistent).

- `crates/storage/src/collections/sorted_set.rs` — `insert`, `remove`
- `crates/storage/src/collections/sorted_map.rs` — `insert_internal` (new-key + value-update restamp), `remove`, `VacantEntry::insert`

## Reproduction & validation (in-process, decisive)

New regression tests in `crates/storage/tests/sorted_index_convergence.rs` drive the exact mechanism through the legitimate sync+local-insert path (node A commits `{a}`; node B gets converged state with a fresh index, then locally inserts `b`):

- `sorted_set_local_insert_after_sync_does_not_hide_synced_elements`
- `sorted_map_local_insert_after_sync_does_not_hide_synced_entries`

**Before** the fix (bug reproduced — membership converges, ordered read stale):
```
sorted_set_local_insert_after_sync_does_not_hide_synced_elements ... FAILED
  left: ["b"]      right: ["a", "b"]
sorted_map_local_insert_after_sync_does_not_hide_synced_entries ... FAILED
  left: [("b","B")]  right: [("a","A"), ("b","B")]
```

**After** the fix (whole suite, incl. the pre-existing #3323/#3328 coverage):
```
running 6 tests
test sorted_set_ordered_read_converges_on_second_node ... ok
test sorted_map_ordered_read_converges_on_second_node ... ok
test sorted_set_local_insert_after_sync_does_not_hide_synced_elements ... ok
test sorted_map_local_insert_after_sync_does_not_hide_synced_entries ... ok
test sorted_map_apply_invalidates_stale_index_marker ... ok
test sorted_set_apply_invalidates_stale_index_marker ... ok
test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed
```

Full `cargo test -p calimero-storage`: **677 + all suites pass**. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p calimero-storage --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Real-node (JS) validation — status

The JS reproduction on real merod is being captured in **calimero-network/calimero-sdk-js#92** (draft): it re-enables the concurrent `SortedSet` ordered-read assertion (`allTags == ["a","b"]`) against the instrumented `merod:edge` and dumps the node `sorted_index_dbg` trace. Final JS-repro validation (both nodes converge to `["a","b"]`) is inherently pending this fix merging and the `merod:edge` image rebuilding, after which sdk-js#92's assertion should pass with the SortedSet check restored. The in-process reproduction above is faithful to the identical mechanism the node trace shows (`CHECK ... marker_current=true` skipping the rebuild over a subset index).

Closes #3333

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


---

## Real-node trace confirmation (instrumented `merod:edge`, sdk-js#92)

The JS reproduction ran in calimero-network/calimero-sdk-js#92 against the instrumented `merod:edge`; the concurrent `SortedSet` ordered-read assertion (`allTags == ["a","b"]`) **diverged** (reproduced #3333), and the node `sorted_index_dbg` trace pins the mechanism exactly. For the `tags` SortedSet inner collection `bd379f75…`:

**Divergent node (node-2) — marker re-stamped by a local insert after the apply cleared it:**
```
19:45:10.025  APPLY_ADD clearing parent marker child=8826372c… parent=bd379f75…      # sync links peer's element → marker cleared
19:45:10.050  STAMP index marker  collection=bd379f75… hash=c928cdd8…  SortedSet      # LOCAL insert re-stamps to converged full_hash
19:45:10.358  CHECK index marker  collection=bd379f75… current_full_hash=c928cdd8…
              stored_marker=Some("c928cdd8…")  marker_current=true  SortedSet         # ordered read SKIPS rebuild → stale subset
```

**Converged node (node-1) — marker left cleared, so the read rebuilds:**
```
19:45:10.325  CHECK index marker  collection=bd379f75… current_full_hash=c928cdd8…
              stored_marker=None  marker_current=false  SortedSet
19:45:10.325  REBUILD index (desired = child-list snapshot) collection=bd379f75…
              desired_len=2  existing_len=1  SortedSet                                 # child list has BOTH; index had 1 → rebuild
19:45:10.325  STAMP index marker  collection=bd379f75… hash=c928cdd8…  SortedSet
```

Both nodes compute the identical converged `current_full_hash=c928cdd8…` (the child list holds both elements — hence `contains`/`len` agree, and node-1's rebuild reports `desired_len=2`). The only difference is node-2's marker was re-stamped to that hash by its **local insert** (the `STAMP` at `.050`, immediately after the `APPLY_ADD` clear at `.025`), so `index_marker_current()` returns `true` and the ordered read never rebuilds — while node-1's marker stayed `None` and its read rebuilds (`existing_len=1 → desired_len=2`). This is mechanism **(a)** from the investigation and matches the in-process reproduction line-for-line. The fix removes exactly that local re-stamp when the index was not already consistent.

_Trace-repro PR (diagnostic, not for merge): calimero-network/calimero-sdk-js#92._

author: mmogallapalli
body: ## Summary This PR adds streaming chat-completion support for Fabric-backed NeMo Agents as part of AIRCORE-952. The main flow added here is: ```text Fabric Runtime invoke_stream -> raw Relay ATOF records -> Platform best-effort assistant text extraction -> OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions SSE -> Studio Chat Playground streaming ``` This keeps Fabric/Relay as the source of streaming telemetry while Platform owns the OpenAI-compatible serving shape expected by existing clients. ## Changes - Updated Fabric optional dependencies to the current Fabric package set used for streaming validation. - Added Fabric runtime streaming wrapper around `runtime.invoke_stream(...)`. - Starts served Fabric runtimes with streaming enabled. - Added OpenAI-compatible streaming response models and SSE framing helpers. - Added ATOF-to-OpenAI text chunk translation for known assistant output shapes. - Wired `stream=true` handling into the Fabric `/v1/chat/completions` serving path. - Added cleanup behavior for interrupted/disconnected streams via `aclose()`. - Added mid-stream error framing. - Added Claude to the example `agent.yaml`. ## Adapter Validation Validated Studio/deployed streaming for: - Codex - Hermes - Claude ## Design Notes - Platform does not invent a native streaming protocol here; it translates Fabric's Relay/ATOF streaming output into OpenAI-compatible SSE because Studio already consumes that shape. - The terminal Fabric stream result remains authoritative for success/failure; stream exhaustion alone is not treated as success. - The ATOF text extraction is intentionally conservative and only emits known assistant-visible text shapes. - DeepAgents is left as a follow-up once the adapter supports the Relay config required by the streaming path. ## Validation Passed: ```bash .venv/bin/pytest plugins/nemo-agents/tests/unit/test_fabric_streaming.py -q ``` Result: ```text 16 passed ``` Also passed: ```bash .venv/bin/ruff check plugins/nemo-agents/src/nemo_agents_plugin/fabric/streaming.py plugins/nemo-agents/tests/unit/test_fabric_streaming.py ``` Working in Studio: ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added streaming chat completions via OpenAI-compatible SSE, including incremental content deltas, `[DONE]`, and structured mid-stream error events. - Added a Claude (Anthropic) harness for agent configuration and updated the example to try Claude locally. - **Bug Fixes** - Improved streaming robustness: timeout/execution error normalization, correct cleanup on cancellation/early generator close, session activity refresh, and serialized concurrent streaming invocations. - **Documentation** - Updated local Claude setup and invocation instructions. - **Maintenance / Tests** - Updated optional Fabric/Hermes release-candidate version constraints and expanded unit test coverage for streaming runtime/server behavior.

author: sairam0424
body:
## Summary
- Adds `src/trelix/core/retry.py` — a single tenacity-based `with_retry()` decorator and `is_retryable_http_error()` classifier used by every outbound network call in trelix. Before this, retry logic was either entirely absent (all 5 LLM backends, all remote embedder providers, GitHubPRClient, the agentic ReAct loop) or duplicated ad hoc and non-jittered despite claiming to be (Jira/TestRail connectors).
- Full-jitter exponential backoff (`wait_random_exponential`, the OpenAI-cookbook-recommended pattern), retrying only 429/5xx and connection-level failures; auto-dispatches sync vs. async so one decorator covers both the fully-sync LLM/connector code and the embedder layer's true-async paths.
- Wires `with_retry()` into: all 5 LLM backends' `complete()`/`stream()`/`tool_call()` (careful to retry only the call that opens a stream, never a partially-consumed generator); every remote embedder's sync and async paths; `GitHubPRClient` (previously zero retry protection); `_cohere_rerank()` in `reranker.py` (fixing a real pre-existing bug where its ad-hoc loop only caught connection errors, never the `HTTPError` that `raise_for_status()` raises for 429/5xx); and Jira/TestRail connectors, deleting ~30 duplicated lines per connector.
- Extends the classifier to recognize SDK-specific exception shapes (`openai.APIStatusError`, `anthropic.APIStatusError`, `google.genai.errors.APIError`, `voyageai.error.VoyageError`) — none of these subclass `httpx.HTTPStatusError`, so without this the LLM/embedder retries would have silently been no-ops.
- Fixes (from an independent adversarial review pass before this PR): every SDK client (OpenAI/Azure/Anthropic/boto3) is now constructed with its own retry disabled (`max_retries=0` / `botocore Config(retries={"max_attempts": 0})`) so tenacity's 5-attempt loop is the sole retry layer, not stacked underneath each SDK's own default retry (was multiplying worst-case wall-clock time on a persistent outage); the exception classifier now catches `Exception` broadly instead of only `ImportError`, so a malformed/mocked exception object degrades to "not retryable" instead of crashing tenacity's retry predicate mid-loop.

## Changes
- `src/trelix/core/retry.py` (new) — `RETRYABLE_STATUS_CODES`, `is_retryable_http_error()`, `with_retry()`
- `src/trelix/llm/providers/{openai,anthropic,bedrock,vertex,litellm}_backend.py` — retry wiring + SDK-retry disabling
- `src/trelix/embedder/base.py` — retry wiring + SDK-retry disabling on all remote providers
- `src/trelix/review/github.py` — retry wiring (previously none)
- `src/trelix/retrieval/reranker.py` — `_cohere_rerank()` migrated off its buggy ad-hoc retry
- `src/trelix/indexing/connectors/{jira,testrail}.py` — migrated off duplicated hand-rolled backoff
- `pyproject.toml` — `tenacity`, `httpx` added as direct dependencies
- `tests/unit/test_retry.py` (new), plus updated tests across every touched call site

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests pass: `python -m pytest tests/unit -q` (1824 passed)
- [x] Integration tests pass: `python -m pytest tests/integration/test_connectors.py -q`
- [x] Lint clean: `ruff check src/ tests/`
- [x] Format clean: `ruff format --check src/ tests/`
- [x] Type check clean: `mypy src/trelix/ --ignore-missing-imports` (no new errors — 6 pre-existing errors in untouched files)
- [x] New tests construct each backend's REAL (unmocked) SDK client and inspect its actual `max_retries` / `meta.config.retries` attribute — proving what configuration reaches the SDK, not just what trelix's own code believes it passed
- [x] Every review-flagged defect has a regression test verified to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the fix

## Phase / milestone
Phase 3 of the Trelix v2.11.0 upgrade plan (Unified Retry Contract) — deep-research-informed, plan-mode-approved.

author: ethenotethan
body:
Focusing a **Hermes Standard** backend now overloads Portal's existing native surfaces instead of opening the bespoke nested management pane. The arc across the branch:

- **Cron** (720d9b03) and **Skills** (2114ff42) route to Standard's HTTP API, with capability-gated actions (pause/resume/trigger; enable/disable toggle).
- **Chat** (55ae2ec1): a focused Standard backend chats over the dashboard's `/api/ws` JSON-RPC sidecar. That endpoint is documented upstream as **wire-compatible with `tui_gateway.entry`** — the same newline-delimited JSON-RPC Portal's `GatewayClient` already speaks — so chat reuses `GatewayClient` (no bespoke backend). The dashboard session token rides as a `?token=` query item (the WS upgrade can't set `Authorization`).
- **Sessions** (15635b9a): the session list, selection, and New Session route to the same sidecar so the chat has sessions to open. Cron/Skills stay on their independent HTTP path; the app-level Hermes socket stays connected underneath. Retires `HermesStandardManagementView`, `HermesStandardSessionsView`, and its view model.
- **Cleanup** (961baafd): explicit ACL on new declarations; dropped the orphaned VM test.

## Model
Focused-management chat: `.hermesStandard` stays management-scoped and gains `.chat`. Focus a Standard gateway → chat + session list follow its sidecar; leave focus → restore the home gateway (also applied at launch, since focus persists).

## Caveats for review
- **Server opt-in:** upstream gates `/api/ws` behind `_DASHBOARD_EMBEDDED_CHAT_ENABLED` (default off; `serve(embedded_chat=True)`). Closes 4403 when off, 4401 on bad token — surfaced client-side as a connection error / create timeout.
- **Lint baseline is stale on this branch** vs the frozen one on `main`: `make lint` reports ~54 pre-existing violations (Model3D, etc.) that are **not from this PR** (the pre-chat tree already failed with 71). All newly-added declarations are explicit-ACL clean. **Refresh `.swiftlint-baseline` after rebasing on `main` before merge.**

author: hardik180704
body:
## What changed

- verify a registered worktree has a valid `HEAD` before AO reuses it
- recover worktrees that Git still marks as `locked initializing`
- clean up attempt-owned initialization husks even when the spawn context was cancelled
- preserve invalid worktrees when AO cannot prove they came from an interrupted initialization

## Why

An interrupted `git worktree add` can leave a registered directory with an unusable `HEAD`. AO previously treated any registered directory as ready, so a later spawn could reuse the husk and leave its worker stalled.

Cleanup is deliberately target-specific: it does not run repository-wide prune, and it never removes a valid, pre-existing, dirty, or otherwise unproven worktree.

## Verification

- `npm run lint`
- `go test ./...`
- `go test -race ./internal/adapters/workspace/gitworktree`
- `go vet ./...`
- real-Git integration test covering interrupted initialization and successful recreation

Closes #3220

author: bryangingechen
body:
Bundles that stack multiple PRs used to display as a flat list with a single ↰ marker, which hid the forest structure — depth, branching, and which stack a PR belonged to. This makes that structure legible.

Each bundle member now renders indented by its stack depth, with a small readiness dot (green held / grey waiting / red blocked), on the bundle detail page and on the dashboard's bundle and batch groups. The ↰ marker is gone; the ⛓ bundle chip and the row--bundled stripe stay.

The batch detail page's plain list of PRs becomes a table with a merge-order column, ordered by the same `Bundles.sort_links_for_merge/1` the batcher uses when it lands a batch, so the page reflects the order the patches will actually merge in.

Internals: `BundleDisplay` gains `display_rows/1` (which pairs each member with its stack depth), `member_status/1`, and `depths/1`; `display_order/1` and `batch_display_order/1` now derive from those with unchanged ordering. Styling reuses the existing bundle palette in both light and dark themes.

Tests added for the new helpers and the batch page's merge ordering; the existing bundle, batch, and project controller tests still pass.

body:
## Qué cambió

- Reemplaza el login email/PIN y Google Sheets por Supabase Auth con email/contraseña.
- Implementa sesiones SSR verificadas, protección de páginas y autorización independiente en `/api/inference`.
- Añade logout real y una pantalla bilingüe para cambiar la contraseña.
- Retira rutas y dependencias de Google Sheets, incorpora variables de entorno de ejemplo y actualiza la documentación.
- Actualiza Next.js 15.5.9 a 15.5.22 por correcciones de seguridad.

## Por qué

author: vitalijimullin07-star
body:
Репорт со скриншотом: «поле ввода текста как не гармонично».

## Почему выпадало из вида

`.ep-fb-input` был описан как `width:100%; resize:vertical; font:inherit` — то есть поле забирало **общий** стиль `input,select,textarea` из base.css и жило по чужим правилам:

- фон `rgba(255,255,255,.08)` почти невидим на карточке — поле не читалось как поле, в воздухе висел только плейсхолдер;
- радиус `var(--button-radius)` = 15px (от кнопок) против 12px у пузырей сообщений;
- `resize:vertical` рисовал уголок ресайза в правом нижнем углу — на телефоне бесполезен (высота и так растёт сама) и выглядел мусором;
- **не было `line-height`** — поэтому при масштабе интерфейса >100% строка не влезала в посчитанную ранее инлайновую высоту от `grow()`, и текст обрезался. Это и видно на присланном скриншоте: плейсхолдер срезан по нижней кромке.

## Что стало

Поле — часть той же визуальной системы, что пузыри: радиус 12px, та же рамка `rgba(148,163,184,.38)` и фон `.12`, `resize:none`, явный `line-height:1.35` и `min-height:40px` — ниже одной строки поле физически стать не может, чем бы ни закончился расчёт `grow()`.

Заодно причёсана раскладка низа. Было «поле само по себе + под ним три кнопки равного веса» (Отправить / 📎 / 📋 Скопировать) — стало как в мессенджере:

- `.ep-fb-inrow`: **📎 · поле** одной строкой, `align-items:flex-end` — чтобы при выросшем на несколько строк поле скрепка не «плавала» по центру;
- **«Отправить»** во всю ширину под ним;
- редкое **«📋 Скопировать переписку»** — отдельной тонкой строкой приглушённым текстом.

У строки копирования **свой** минимальный стиль, а не `.ep-plan-mini`: тот рассчитан на квадратные иконки тулбара плана и ломал текстовую подпись на две строки (иконка над текстом — было видно на первом скриншоте прогона).

Ретро-облик не потерял «оконный» вид: отступы переехали с поля на строку, у 📎 свой бежевый квадрат с синей рамкой.

## Проверки

- `node test/run.js` — **276 зелёных** (было 275). Среди них стражи: `resize:none`, наличие `line-height` и `min-height`, радиус 12px, своя рамка и фон, `align-items:flex-end`, `white-space:nowrap` у строки копирования (чтобы `.ep-plan-mini` не вернулся).
- Живой прогон: поле 42px, `scrollHeight === clientHeight` (не обрезано), радиус 12px, `resize:none`. Снято в четырёх видах — современный облик день/ночь и ретро день/ночь: везде поле выровнено с пузырями, уголка ресайза нет, подпись копирования в одну строку.
- Регресс-прогон предыдущего пакета (клавиатура + статусы/аватарки) — **14 из 14** остались зелёными.

author: mu0810
body:
This pull request was created by @kiro-agent on behalf of @Mu0810 :ghost:

Comment with **/kiro fix** to address specific feedback or **/kiro all** to address everything.
<sub>[Learn about Kiro Web](https://kiro.dev/web/)</sub>

---
The course had a climb but no climax: you reached the summit, took a star, and the results card appeared. Now taking the summit star wakes **King Grumba**, who invades the plaza.

> Note: my local `game/upgrade-moves-and-readability` branch was already merged as #4, so this branch was cut fresh. Its diff against `main` is the boss commit only.

## Fight design

- **Three hits.** He alternates a charge and a leaping slam. Both leave him stunned and head-down, and that is the *only* window where a stomp or ground pound lands.
- **The slam's shockwave only hurts a grounded player**, so the answer is always "jump when he lands".
- **Charge him into the plaza pedestal** and he knocks himself out, giving a free opening — the pillar in the middle of the arena is there to be used.
- Each hit makes him faster and spawns two Grumbas.
- He roams most of the plaza, so backing off is a valid tactic but not an escape.

## Flow changes

- The summit star no longer wins the course; it triggers the invasion. Beating him drops the **Crown Star** where he fell, and taking that clears the course. Three stars total.
- A **short camera cutaway** frames him on spawn. Without it the fight is announced by a health bar for an enemy fifteen metres below and off screen — which is exactly how it looked the first time I tried it.
- Boss health pips in the HUD. Retry clears the boss, its spawned minions and the bar.

## Two balance bugs that only simulation caught

I wrote a bot that fights him, and the first two runs it lost 3–0 without landing a single hit. Both causes were real:

1. **Contact damage stayed on while he was stunned**, so the one opening in the fight was unusable — you took a hit walking into range before you could ever jump on his crown.
2. **His charge ended on its first frame.** Chasing a retreating player pinned him against a too-small arena boundary, and hitting the boundary counted as a crash. The arena is now most of the plaza, and a crash requires him to have actually been under way.

## Testing

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| competent bot (holds distance, closes on the stun, hops the shockwave) | wins in **12.1 s** with 1 heart left |
| passive player who never attacks | **dies**, boss at full health |
| stomping outside the stun window | costs the player a heart, boss takes none |
| ground pound during the stun | lands a hit |
| shockwave vs grounded / airborne / distant player | hurts / spares / spares |
| pedestal crash | stuns him |
| Crown Star before he dies | unreachable |
| death mid-fight | clean GAME OVER, bar hidden |
| retry | boss, minions, bar and star all reset |
| build audit | 0 warnings |
| route sim | **29/29 hops** still clear with a plain single jump |
| 20 s fuzz during a live fight | no JS errors, boss stays in the plaza |

## Known limitation

As before, the headless browser runs well under 60 fps, so timings come from fixed-1/60 s simulation. The fight's *feel* — whether the 2.8 s stun reads as generous or tight, and whether the 3 s cutaway outstays its welcome — wants a real playthrough. Both are single constants (`STUN_AFTER_CHARGE` in `src/boss.js`, the cinematic duration in `startBossFight`).

author: stevenyepes
body:
## Problem

Launching Demeteo via the OS app launcher (Dock/Start Menu/desktop icon) while an instance was already running started a brand-new process and window rather than focusing the existing one, since `tauri-plugin-single-instance` was never wired up.

## Fix

- Add `tauri-plugin-single-instance` and register it as the first plugin in the `Builder` chain (a hard upstream requirement for reliably intercepting a second launch across platforms).
- Its callback reuses the existing `show_main_window` unminimize/show/focus sequence from `tray.rs`, now exposed as `pub(crate)` instead of duplicating that logic.

## Notes

Cold start and the `run_in_background`-off/fully-exited case are unaffected — a relaunch only gets intercepted when a prior process is actually alive to receive the callback.

author: yukon-autoresearch[bot]
body:
Yukon submission `19481466-65c6-492e-bfac-f5950ab6fb73` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/mlxfast-challenge at `45d6b2563b5345552303aa6ad27ecb2082e68325`.

Current best score: 1.80591049704696. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: GPT 5.6 Sol

# Restore the ranked one-row fused routed/shared down QMV on the current frontier

## Attribution

- **Underlying model:** GPT 5.6 Sol
- **Coding harness:** pi coding agent
- **Effort:** high, source-only reasoning and repository-history reconciliation
- **Ranked track:** `laguna-xs-2.1-serial-v2`
- **Submitted model label:** `GPT 5.6 Sol`
- **Starting promoted submission:** `d7bfc0e0-c31d-452b-82d4-7c7e8b78dc77`
- **Starting promoted score:** `1.80591049704696`
- **Starting submission commit:** `45d6b2563b5345552303aa6ad27ecb2082e68325`
- **Current harness/base commit after `mlxfast sync`:** `3135c999824d0425d07c47793bd8abd8586d8a1f`

This submission makes one small decode-only kernel-geometry change in one editable file. It restores a previously ranked and hidden-gate-passing one-output-row-per-SIMD geometry for the already fused routed-plus-shared MoE down projection. It does not change weight values, quantization, arithmetic order within an output row, model topology, prefill, cache behavior, or serial request semantics.

## Frontier reconnaissance

I began with the exact workflow requested by the task:

```sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
mlxfast benchmark
mlxfast submissions --all
```

The benchmark reported a current best score of `1.80591049704696`. I then read the notes for the latest and most relevant promoted submissions, especially:

- `d7bfc0e`: the current frontier, which introduced an NVFP4 tail layout for attention layers 32–39;
- `bbf9c9a`: the preceding full 40-layer native-affine output-projection rollout;
- `88d8fe2`: the known combination of full output-projection rollout and the one-row routed/shared down kernel;
- `ffe12fe` and `02786c6`: the preceding bounded output-projection rollout chunks.

The important historical observation was that submission `88d8fe2` documented a one-row routed/shared down QMV as an independently known, exact geometry change. That note recorded the stable patch ID `f779c05ed3d6ea396d136c8613cefce1c919d65c`, stated that the same source delta had passed the full official hidden correctness stack, and explained that it had been removed from the later frontier by the NVFP4-tail submission rather than disproven as a mechanism.

I then synchronized exactly as required:

```sh
mlxfast sync
```

The CLI selected `d7bfc0e0-c31d-452b-82d4-7c7e8b78dc77` and restored its editable paths on top of the latest trusted harness. This matters because the repository tip also contains a new operator rule defining the accepted quantization envelope. I read that rule before choosing a hypothesis. The accepted envelope allows the shipped group-16 NVFP4 weights and the established group-32 affine INT8 attention side representation, but prohibits escalating to a lossier representation. Therefore I explicitly rejected any further attention quantization rollout as a candidate, even though the current frontier source retains measurement probes. The submitted change is a pure execution geometry change over unchanged NVFP4 MoE values and is inside the current contract.

## Hot-path reading

I inspected `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift`, focusing on:

1. the serial decode-only attention branches and their native affine Q/K/V and output-projection side layouts;
2. the fused residual/RMS/router path;
3. routed and shared gate/up NVFP4 QMV kernels;
4. the fused routed-plus-shared down projection and residual kernel;
5. async scheduling boundaries and prefill/decode regime guards.

The current frontier already includes broad fusion coverage. In sparse layers, the fused routed/shared down kernel consumes:

- eight routed activated expert rows;
- the selected routed experts’ unchanged NVFP4 down weights and scales;
- the eight FP32 router weights;
- the shared activated row;
- the shared expert’s unchanged NVFP4 down weights and scales;
- the decoder residual.

It emits the final hidden-width BF16 row in one dispatch. The current version assigns four output rows to each SIMD group. Consequently each lane carries four FP32 accumulators and the dispatch exposes one quarter as many independent output-row work items as a one-row geometry.

## First small, safe hypothesis

The first hypothesis was deliberately conservative:

> Restore the previously ranked one-output-row-per-SIMD geometry only for the existing fused routed/shared down+residual kernel. This should expose four times as many independent NVFP4 weight streams and reduce per-SIMD private accumulator pressure while preserving every output row’s arithmetic exactly.

This is safer than inventing a new fusion because it changes ownership, not mathematics. It is also more grounded than adjusting an unmeasured default: the exact kernel block already exists in repository history and was present in the officially validated `88d8fe2` submission.

The optimization is production-relevant and prompt-independent. Every sparse layer executes the routed/shared down operation for each supplied decode token. It does not rely on repeated prompts, token history coincidences, future logits, hidden prompts, or benchmark repetition.

## Exact implementation

Only `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` changed.

The kernel name changes from:

```text
laguna_routed_shared_nvfp4_down_residual_bf16_v1
```

to the historical ranked identity:

```text
laguna_routed_shared_nvfp4_down_residual_bf16_r1_v3
```

The ownership constant changes from:

```metal
constexpr uint outputs_per_simd = 4;
```

to:

```metal
constexpr uint outputs_per_simd = 1;
```

The private result array therefore contains one FP32 accumulator instead of four. The grid is widened correspondingly from:

```swift
((LagunaConstants.hiddenSize / 4) * 288, 1, 1)
```

to:

```swift
(LagunaConstants.hiddenSize * 288, 1, 1)
```

The 288-thread threadgroup remains unchanged: nine SIMD groups still correspond to the eight routed slots plus one shared slot. Each SIMD group still computes a complete dot product for its output row. The lane-level K traversal, NVFP4 decode, scale application, `simd_sum`, BF16 materialization, router multiplication, ordered routed accumulation, `2.5` factor, shared addition, and residual addition all remain unchanged.

## Why output is preserved

For a particular output row, the following sequence is identical before and after this patch:

1. Select the same routed or shared expert slot.
2. Select the same expert index from `indices` for routed slots.
3. Load the same 512 BF16 activation values distributed as 16 values per SIMD lane.
4. Load the same packed group-16 NVFP4 weight bytes.
5. Load the same per-group E8M0 scale byte.
6. Decode and multiply values in the same lane-local order.
7. Reduce the same lane-local FP32 partials using the same `simd_sum` operation.
8. Round the expert output to BF16 at the same boundary.
9. Store the nine slot outputs in threadgroup memory.
10. Traverse routed slots 0 through 7 in the same order, with the same BF16 router-weight cast, BF16 product, and BF16 running total.
11. Apply the same BF16 `2.5` routed factor.
12. Add the same BF16 shared result and residual in the same order.

The only changed fact is which output-row index a SIMD group owns. There is no changed reduction tree for an output row and no reassociation across rows, because rows are independent.

The restored block was compared directly with the same block from commit `331bde80ffa3d0510e9df45b8b40d4eb2ffee6f8`. The block from the `private let lagunaRoutedSharedDownResidualKernel` declaration through the start of the layer-0 section is exactly equal after the edit.

## Why this should improve decode

author: emipasca
body:
## The bug

On a vestad-update boot, `collect_boot_turns` prepended a daemon-restore orientation to the **first converge turn**. During an update that first turn is the upstream-sync turn, so the agent read and ran the **pre-sync** `restart` skill's Daemons block *before*:

1. the sync merged the new `restart` skill (it's git-synced at `agent/skills/restart/`), and
2. the after-sync migrations reshaped the Daemons block (e.g. `2026-08-daemon-pidfile`).

Daemons started against startup logic that was about to change underneath them, which produced the port/vestad-refused failures seen during an upgrade.

## The fix

Restore daemons **last**, at the greeting's restart turn, which runs after the sync and every migration. So a migration that rewrites the Daemons block has always landed before the daemons start.

- Drop the early-restore orientation from the converge turns entirely (net deletion). Converge turns (sync, migrations) now carry no daemon preamble.
- Carry the "your daemons are down, run the Daemons block (idempotent, safe no-op)" preamble in the restart greeting itself (`agent/core/prompts/restart.md`), where the restore now happens. This is the same mechanism a plain restart already uses.

Audit backing the ordering: no migration requires a daemon to be up. Every daemon touch is `daemon start`/`daemon restart` (works whether up or down) or a Daemons-block text edit; the lone `whatsapp status` reads link state from disk. Migrations that change how a daemon runs restart that daemon themselves.

### Tradeoff

Daemons stay down for the whole converge (which can span several boots on a full upgrade), so the agent is unreachable on daemon-backed channels (app-chat, whatsapp) until the final greeting brings them up. This is deliberate: it's the price of never starting daemons against a stale Daemons block. Prior behavior kept the agent reachable throughout at the cost of the staleness bug.

### Fleet

`restart.md` is core-only (`load_prompt` reads `core_prompts_dir`, no user override) and `collect_boot_turns` is engine code, both delivered via the read-only core mount, so this reaches the fleet on the next engine update with no migration.

## Tests

`test_boot_turns.py` now asserts no converge turn carries a daemon-restore preamble (sync turn opens with `[Upstream sync]`, migration turn with the batch instructions) and the greeting is the last turn. Renamed the post-sync case to `test_after_sync_migration_boot_defers_daemons_to_the_greeting`. Verified green locally: `test_boot_turns`, `test_processor`, `test_migrations`, `test_crash_recovery`, `test_shutdown_reason`, `test_upstream_sync_turn`, `test_interrupts`, plus ty/ruff/format/conventions.

## Summary
- verify PID start time immediately before sending SIGTERM or SIGKILL
- refuse to signal stale or unverifiable process identities
- run graceful termination asynchronously and require an explicit force-kill action after the grace period
- surface truthful row-local feedback for success, stale PID, permission denial, disappearance, identity failure, and signal errors

A scanned row can outlive its process. If macOS reuses that PID before the user clicks Kill, signaling by PID alone can target an unrelated process. The previous UI also discarded kill results and never used the implemented grace/force lifecycle.

The force-kill path performs a fresh identity check immediately before SIGKILL; it does not reuse the earlier SIGTERM check.

body:
Documentation only — no code changes.

The v12.0 and v12.1 troubleshooting entries record *what broke and how it was fixed*. Two things were missing, and both matter more for the next platform than for this one.

**Why the fix had to be architectural.** `TROUBLESHOOTING.md` now opens with "Why v12.0 and v12.1 Exist". Claude did not ship a bug — it shipped a performance optimization, and that quietly falsified the premise every release before v12.0 rested on: *the DOM is the conversation*. The section covers the per-feature consequences (including an export that stated its own completeness while being truncated), why the three obvious repairs are dead ends, the constraints that shaped the real fix, why jumping had to be redesigned once a held element reference stopped meaning anything, why bookmarks needed a second release, and why it took two releases instead of one.

**What to do when ChatGPT, Grok or Gemini does the same thing.** This is a when, not an if — virtualization is the standard answer to a slow chat page, and Claude's own answer flipped between February and July 2026 with no announcement and a green suite.

- `DOM-REFERENCE.md` gains a **Virtualization status** table above the selectors, with the 13 non-Claude platforms marked **unverified** rather than verified-negative — they were checked in February, before anyone knew to look for this. Includes the two-command check and the recycling-vs-lazy-loading distinction that decides whether the work is an afternoon or a release.
- `ROADMAP.md` gains **"Porting the Layer 4 response to another platform"** — the order of operations, a table of what is already generic (resolve-on-arrival, identity-keyed bookmarks, the degraded-state UI) versus what must be built per platform (the fetch, the auth, the payload walk), and the persisted-data trap that turned one release into two.
- `agent_docs/architecture.md` points at all three and states the rule that transfers everywhere: **a held element reference is not an identity.**

Deliberately **not** asserted anywhere: that any other platform has a usable conversation endpoint. That is unverified, so the playbook says what to establish and states plainly that labelled reduced functionality is a legitimate outcome if no source exists.

author: antuk3n
body:
Builds the Renewal Risk Prediction screen from mockup `118.png` and §2 of the client's paper: High/Moderate/Low risk counts, Reminders Sent, a Businesses at Risk table, and a Recommended Actions panel. Actions are derived from the band (High → Immediate follow-up, Moderate → Send reminder, Low → Monitor) so the panel and the KPI cards agree **by construction** instead of being computed twice and drifting.

Live against the seeded register: 211 high / 47 moderate / 1,501 low, 25 rows surfaced.

## ⚠ Deliberate deviation from both the paper and the mockup

The paper describes `predict_renewal_risk()` using **"predictive statistical models"** to produce an **"Estimated Probability of Delayed Renewal"**. The mockup's table header reads **"PROB. DELAYED"** over values like 88% / 81% / 74%.

**There is no such model.** `r/R/*.R` contains no renewal-risk model — only `generate.R` even mentions renewal. There is nothing fitted on historical outcomes to port, so any number here is necessarily a heuristic.

Labelling a weighted rule score a "probability" would claim predictive validity the system does not have, and a BPLO officer could reasonably act on "88% probability" as if it were calibrated. So this ships as an explicit `score` with High/Moderate/Low banding, and the response carries the `rulebook` and `thresholds` that produced it — the number is auditable rather than authoritative. A test asserts the methodology statement is present.

**This is flagged for you to overrule knowingly.** If you want a real probability, that means fitting on historical renewal outcomes and reporting calibration — a different piece of work, and one the current data may not support.

## `Reminders Sent` reads 0, honestly

The KPI counts persisted reminder records, and none exist: renewal reminders (§3 — firing at 30/15/7/1 days before expiry) aren't implemented yet. Rather than invent a plausible number, the field reports what's true. Implementing reminders is what makes it non-zero.

## `App\Support\Des` is included but not exposed

`Des`, `DesEventQueue` and `StaffingSimulation` are a complete, tested port of `r/R/des.R`, written before the paper established that DES is **not** part of the delivered flow — it appears in no section and no mockup.

The code is kept because it's finished and passing, but there is deliberately **no route, no resource type and no screen**, so nothing ships a feature the paper can't support. Comments at each of those three sites record why. Say the word and I'll drop it entirely.

## Also included

`docs/r-integration-spec.md` — the canonical spec extracted from `R INTEGRATION (MIDTERM).pdf`, with all formulas, the six-feature inventory, and the architecture you chose: R stays a separate program, Laravel pushes rows to plumber, results are batch-refreshed and persisted, native PHP statistics remain an automatic fallback.

## Tests

```
php artisan test
{"result":"passed","tests":322,"passed":322,"assertions":2470}

npm run typecheck   # tsc -b, clean
```

Coverage includes: renewal-risk feed and report served to the super admin only; refused to unauthenticated callers; refused to BPLO staff and owners (no `analytics.view`); the methodology statement and published rulebook are carried in the payload; and banding cases such as a lapsed permit with nothing filed scoring high.

author: trsonic
body:
`WavReader::CreateFromFile` forces `destination_alignment_bytes = 4` but never inspects the decoded sample format. For IEEE float sources (format tag 3), audio_to_tactile's `ReadWavSamples` fills the 32-bit destination with raw float values (`ReadWavInfo::sample_format == kFloat`), so `ReadFrame` stored float *bit patterns* directly into the int32 sample buffers. Header parsing succeeds and `WavSampleProvider` validates only bit depth / sample rate / channel IDs, so a float WAV fed to the encoder produced garbage audio while appearing to encode successfully.

### Fix

Convert float samples to the left-justified int32 convention documented on `buffers_`, using the same scaling as audio_to_tactile's `InPlaceFloatToInt32Conversion` (which only runs on the whole-file `ReadWavFile` path this reader does not use): scale [-1, 1] by 2^31, clamp out-of-range values, map NaN to 0. float64 sources are downcast to float32 by the C layer and take the same path.

The docs on `bit_depth()` and `buffers_` now state that for IEEE float sources `bit_depth()` reports the source container width (32 or 64) while the decoded samples span the full int32 range. As before this change, `WavSampleProvider` rejects readers whose bit depth exceeds the codec's, so float64 input works through `WavReader` directly but not the encoder pipeline; float32 now encodes correctly.

### Tests

Regression tests with hand-crafted mono float32/float64 fixtures cover scaling, clamping (at +/-1.0 and for out-of-range 1.5, -1.5, +inf), and NaN. Both tests fail without the fix — float bit patterns surface verbatim, e.g. 0.5f reads as `0x3F000000` instead of `0x40000000`.

Tested: `bazel test //iamf/cli/tests:wav_reader_test //iamf/cli/tests:wav_sample_provider_test //iamf/cli/tests:wav_writer_test` -> 3/3 pass on top of current `main`.

author: lodyai[bot]
body:
## Summary

Closes #312.

`build_support` was pinned at `sha2` 0.10.9. When Dependabot proposes 0.11 the
crate stops compiling, because 0.11 changes `Sha256::digest`/`finalize` to
return `hybrid_array::Array<u8, _>` — a type that derefs to `[u8]` but does not
implement `core::fmt::LowerHex`, so the `format!("{digest:x}")` at
`build_support/src/font.rs:172` no longer builds. This adopts 0.11 now and
fixes the render site, and takes the opportunity to bound an unbounded
network read in the same function.

## Changes

- **`sha2` 0.11.0.** Bumped in `build_support/Cargo.toml`. Note that `sha2`
  0.10.9 remains in the tree transitively (via `pbkdf2` ← `zip` ← `dbsp`); the
  two versions coexist without conflict.
- **New `build_support::hex::to_lower_hex`.** Renders digest bytes as lowercase
  hexadecimal via a nibble lookup table into a preallocated `String`. A
  crate-internal encoder is preferred over adding a `hex` dependency: the whole
  requirement is two table lookups per byte, and `build_support` runs on every
  build. The call site becomes `to_lower_hex(&Sha256::digest(&bytes))`, where
  `&` coerces `Array` to `&[u8]` via `Deref`.
- **Capped the font download.** `resp.bytes()` buffered the entire response
  into memory with no limit, *before* the checksum was checked, so a hostile or
  misbehaving origin could drive build-time memory use arbitrarily high. Since
  this runs in a build script, that failure lands on every developer and CI
  job. The new `read_capped` bounds the read at `MAX_FONT_BYTES` (8 MiB,
  against a ~400 KiB font).
- **Docs.** A new *The font download in `build_support`* section in
  `docs/developers-guide.md` records both decisions.

## Reviewer notes

### Why the cap reads one byte past the limit

`read_capped` takes `max_bytes + 1`, not `max_bytes`. A plain
`take(max_bytes)` cannot distinguish a body sitting *exactly* on the limit from
one silently *truncated* by it — the latter would then be hashed as a short
font and reported as a checksum mismatch, which is a misleading diagnosis of
the real problem. Reading the extra byte makes an oversized body observable and
reportable as such. The `exactly_at_cap` / `read_capped_rejects_oversized_body`
cases pin that boundary.

`read_capped` takes the limit as a parameter rather than reading the constant
directly, so the boundary tests can use a 4-byte cap instead of allocating
8 MiB.

### Test coverage

`every_byte_renders_as_two_lowercase_round_tripping_digits` is a bounded
exhaustive check across the whole `u8` range: each byte must render as exactly
two lowercase ASCII hex digits that parse back to the original value. That
catches leading-zero and case bugs in the low nibble that a couple of example
vectors would miss.

### Deliberately out of scope

Following the issue's own triage of the [whitaker reference
commit](https://github.com/leynos/whitaker/commit/74c56e856b1435e91aa31602e2044dac34a19a6e):

- **Sidecar hardening does not apply.** The expected digest here is the
  compile-time `FONT_SHA256` constant, not a fetched `.sha256` sidecar, so
  there is no token to validate as 64 hex digits, nothing to lowercase before
  comparison, and no sidecar read to cap. The comparison is already
  constant-to-constant lowercase and is unchanged.
- **Partial-artefact cleanup does not apply.** `tmp.persist(&font_path)`
  already gives an atomic publish.
- **No `trybuild` compile-fail guard.** Whitaker added one asserting that
  `{:x}` on a digest fails to compile. Its value is a regression guard against
  reintroducing `{:x}`, but on 0.11 that reintroduction simply does not
  compile — the guard is redundant here, and it would cost a `trybuild`
  dev-dependency plus a `.stderr` snapshot that breaks on toolchain updates.
  Happy to add it if you would rather have the belt and braces.
- **No `io::copy(&mut reader, &mut hasher)` site exists** in this repo, so
  there is nothing to migrate for the dropped `io::Write` impl. The developer's
  guide records the break and the lockstep sibling bumps
  (`sha1`/`sha3`/`md-5` → 0.11, `hmac`/`hkdf`/`pbkdf2` → 0.13) for whoever hits
  it next.

## Validation

All six deterministic gates pass on this branch:

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `make check-fmt` | pass |
| `make lint` (cargo doc, clippy `-D warnings`, whitaker) | pass |
| `make typecheck` | pass |
| `make test` | pass — 0 failed across all workspace crates and doctests |
| `make markdownlint` | pass |
| `make nixie` | pass |

`coderabbit review --agent`: 0 findings.

The network path itself is not exercised by tests — `fetch_font_data` is
reached only through the `FontFetcher` trait, which the suite mocks. The cap
logic is tested directly through `read_capped`.

## References

- Issue: [#312](https://github.com/leynos/lille/issues/312)
- Reference implementation: [leynos/whitaker#296](https://github.com/leynos/whitaker/pull/296)
- Lody session: https://lody.ai/leynos/sessions/6848617c-b20f-44bd-bfa1-34b867288e89

Enhancements:
- Adopt sha2 0.11 in build_support and replace digest formatting with a lowercase hexadecimal encoder compatible with the new digest type.

body:
### Description

This PR updates metrics code to use `metrics_utils` crate from the [`framework-libs-rs`](https://github.com/juspay/framework-libs-rs) repository for configuring and setting up metrics, instead of depending on the OpenTelemetry crates directly.

Additionally, since we're using a common crate for the metrics code, we are also able to provide support for exporting metrics in OTLP format over gRPC, with zstd compression. The metrics related configuration has had some changes to support both modes of metrics export.

To disable metrics:

```toml
[metrics]
mode = "disabled"
```

To export metrics in Prometheus format:

```toml
[metrics]
mode = "prometheus"
host = "127.0.0.1"
port = 6128
```

To export metrics in OTLP format:

```toml
[metrics]
mode = "otlp"
endpoint = "http://localhost:4317"
endpoint_timeout_secs = 10
metrics_export_interval_secs = 15
```

### Testing

- Ran the service locally with Prometheus mode enabled, I am able to see metrics served at the `/metrics` endpoint on port 6128.
- Ran the service locally with OTLP mode enabled and OpenTelemetry Collector, Prometheus and Grafana running using Hyperswitch's Docker Compose setup, able to see metrics in Grafana.

author: quasar-apps
body:
## What & why

Two things, both prerequisites for a first release: **a human checkpoint before something permanent**, and **documenting the `develop` → `main` promotion** that the branching model implied but nothing described.

### I was wrong about the scope of the first one

I described this to the maintainer as "a one-line workflow change." It isn't, and the reason is the substance of this PR.

`publishToMavenCentral` only *stages* the upload — it isn't public until the Publish button is clicked in the Central Portal. But the `release` job cut a GitHub Release the moment the `publish` job succeeded. Swap the task alone and you get a GitHub Release announcing a version that **nobody can resolve** and that **might still be dropped**. The gate and the announcement have to move together.

## The changes

**1. The tag stages, it doesn't publish.** `release.yml` runs `publishToMavenCentral`. Verification, the CHANGELOG check and the build are unchanged — what changes is that the run now ends with the deployment staged, where `Drop` still costs nothing. The step summary tells the maintainer exactly what remains.

**2. Cutting the GitHub Release becomes its own `workflow_dispatch` workflow** (`github-release.yml`), run with a tag input after the portal shows `PUBLISHED`. It checks out that tag, so the notes are read from the CHANGELOG **as it shipped** rather than from whatever `develop` looks like later. This also strengthens the property #75 was built around: publish and announce can no longer share a run *at all*, so a transient API failure can never force a re-publish.

**3. `develop` → `main` promotion is documented**, with the reason it matters: nothing enforces it. The workflow fires on any `v*` tag on any commit, so tagging `develop` directly would publish perfectly well and leave `main` permanently behind.

## Reversing the gate later

Once the pipeline has proven itself, `publishToMavenCentral` → `publishAndReleaseToMavenCentral` restores one-step releases. Both the workflow comment and CONTRIBUTING say so, and both say to re-read the announce-workflow note first — because with auto-publish, chaining the announcement back onto the publish run becomes correct again.

## Verification

- Both workflows parse; triggers, permissions and job structure assert as intended. `contents: write` is held only by the announce workflow; every checkout keeps `persist-credentials: false`.
- The extraction script is unchanged and still yields the `0.1.0` section (240 lines) — both workflows share it, so validation and note-generation cannot drift.
- `./gradlew :aquifer-core:build` green. No production code touched.

## Docs swept for the change

Three places described the superseded flow and would have been wrong the moment this merged: the CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry from #75, the roadmap's shipped *Cut a GitHub Release* item (it described a `needs: publish` job that no longer exists), and the roadmap's *Publish v0.1.0* item (it ended at "push the tag; the workflow does the rest"). All three now match, and CONTRIBUTING's release section is rewritten as four numbered steps.

## Summary
- Rebuilds `ContactPicker` as a bottom drawer per the ready-for-dev comp (Figma `5732:4449`): the full contact list shows before any typing, the search field narrows it live (the Search pill dismisses the keyboard), rows toggle checkboxes, and a centered **Add** CTA plus an **Add All ›** link sit above the address-book disclosure. No Cancel button — swiping the drawer down closes it.
- **Add behavior (hybrid):** one checked contact keeps today's conversational intake (routes to `/contacts/add` prefilled); several checked (or Add All) are bulk-created directly from address-book data via a new `useBulkCreateRecipients` batch insert — `relationship_type` stays `""` (renders as "—") until the profile is filled in, per DEV-66's "get details for each when the time comes". Contact photos upload through the existing edge-function path.
- Removes the sub-copy from the **Access Your Contacts** modal — the iOS system permission dialog explains the access (Erik's call, Caspian agreed conditioned on the system dialog appearing; verified it does).
- All four picker hosts rewired (People tab, Home empty state, Add People tile, gift-generation waiting screen).

## Root-cause note
`present()` fired while iOS is still tearing down its contacts-access UI (first-time grant) wedges the bottom sheet: it registers as presented but never reaches the screen, and later `present()` calls no-op. AppState can't gate this (it stays "active"), so the drawer watches `onChange` for the real open and force dismiss/re-presents until it lands.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` clean.
- Driven end-to-end on the iOS simulator (idb): fresh-permission flow (access modal → system dialog → limited-access share → drawer opens), multi-select Add (recipients created with birthday/address, list refreshes), Add with one contact (routes to prefilled AI chat), disabled Add with nothing checked. author: arthsdev
body:
# Summary

Two bugs surfaced while integrating the React frontend with the existing
auth endpoints, both blocking real end-to-end login from the browser.

## CORS blocking browser requests

The frontend (localhost:5173) was blocked by the browser's CORS policy
when calling the backend (localhost:8081) — expected, since Postman/
Insomnia don't enforce CORS, so this was never caught until a real
browser client existed.

- Added `CorsConfig`, exposing a `CorsConfigurationSource` bean,
  configured via `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (defaults to
  `http://localhost:5173` for local dev, overridable via env var for
  other environments).
- `SecurityConfig` now injects this bean instead of building CORS
  config inline, keeping it focused on authN/authZ concerns.

## LoginResponse leaking snake_case to the frontend

`@JsonProperty("access_token")` on `LoginResponse` was applied to
translate Keycloak's snake_case response into camelCase — but Jackson
applies `@JsonProperty` bidirectionally, so the same annotation also
serialized the response back to the frontend as snake_case, silently
breaking the contract the frontend expected.

- Introduced `KeycloakTokenResponse`, a package-private record
  dedicated to deserializing Keycloak's raw token response.
- `LoginResponse` no longer carries any `@JsonProperty` — it's a clean
  camelCase DTO, only ever serialized outward to API clients.
- `AuthClient.requestToken()` now deserializes into
  `KeycloakTokenResponse` internally and maps to `LoginResponse`
  before returning, with a null-check consistent with the same
  pattern already used in `KeycloakAdminClient`.

## Validation

Manually validated end-to-end from the React frontend: login request
no longer blocked by CORS, and the response body now returns clean
camelCase fields (`accessToken`, `refreshToken`) instead of the
previous `access_token`/`refresh_token` leak.

All existing tests pass (`mvn test`).

## Slice 2 — codebase context v1
Gives Flue awareness of the actual repo, so later authoring can be grounded in the real stack instead of a blind one-shot.

- **`src/lib/github/tree.ts`** — `fetchRepoTree`: full recursive blob tree at a ref.
- **`src/lib/plans/codebase.ts`** — pure, tested `selectContextPaths`: curates stack/config/docs files (manifests, lockfiles, tsconfig, wrangler, CI, READMEs), drops source + vendored/generated dirs.

- **`src/agents/instance.ts`** — extracted a pure `parseInstanceName` (+ tests) so the DO can parse its own `owner~repo` name.
- **Client** `FluePing` requests context on connect and shows "read N context files (cached)".

author: akorman128
body:
Clicking a conversation left the canvas area blank until everything was ready. There is no single wait to cover — there are three, back to back, and any one of them can be the visible one depending on whether the tldraw chunk is warm:

1. **The server fetch.** `/c/[conversationId]` awaits conversation, nodes, credentials, skills, then edges, suggestions and attachments. Without a `loading.tsx` the router holds the *previous* page on screen for the whole round trip, so switching conversations looks like a dead click.
2. **The tldraw chunk.** `Canvas` is `dynamic(..., { ssr: false })` with no `loading`, so `next/dynamic` renders nothing while the bundle downloads — the first canvas of a session, and every share link.
3. **Store init.** Both views render `null` until the `useEffect` that calls `graph.init()` has run.

One `CanvasSpinner` covers all three, so the indicator never disappears and reappears between them. It fades in after 150ms (`delay-150 fill-mode-both`), which means a warm navigation shows nothing at all rather than a flash.

## Two things left deliberately undone

**The draft hand-off flashes it.** When the first prompt on `/c/new` streams in, the composer does `router.replace('/c/<id>')`, which mounts the `[conversationId]` segment and shows the fallback over the card that just appeared. Worth knowing that a guard would buy nothing: that navigation unmounts the old canvas either way, so suppressing the spinner leaves blank space, not the live canvas. Removing the flash for real means not doing a server navigation for the hand-off. (Only reachable once the draft branch lands.)

**`app/s/[token]` gets no `loading.tsx`.** A Suspense fallback starts the response body streaming, and `notFound()` after headers are sent is a 200 with `noindex` rather than a real 404. Share links keep their status code; their dynamic-import and store-init gaps are still covered.

## Verification

`tsc` and `eslint` clean. Driven in a browser against the dev server: navigating from `/c/new` to a conversation, `loading.tsx` was in the DOM for the full ~1s the dev server took to answer, then the canvas replaced it. Rendering the markup in place confirms it centers in the canvas column and reads as muted, not as an error state.

author: justsomehack
body:
## Summary

Two independent improvements found during the perf/memory audit. Both are measured, not estimated.

| Change | Measured |
|---|---|
| `DICOMObject.WriteTo(io.Writer)` — streaming serialisation | **532,688 → 8,400 B/op (−98.4%)**, 13.4× faster |
| wado frame retrieval bug | fixes **silent empty 200** above 512 MiB |
| wado instance retrieval streams | no full copy per multipart part |

### 1. `media`: streaming object writes

Serialising an object always went through `WriteToBytes`, which materialises the **entire object — pixel data included — in a second buffer**. `writeTag` is now split into a header write plus a value write, so `WriteTo` pushes tag headers through a small scratch buffer and hands each tag's value bytes **straight to the destination writer**.

```
write test2.dcm:  532688 -> 8400 B/op (-98.4%),  47792 -> 3557 ns/op (13.4x)
```

The streamed figure is just the scratch buffer and **does not grow with the object** — a 500 MB instance goes from ~500 MB of transient copy to ~8 KB.

`WriteToFile` now streams to the file handle rather than building the whole payload for `os.WriteFile`.

**Deflated Explicit VR Little Endian deliberately still buffers** — that syntax deflates the dataset as a unit and cannot be produced incrementally.

**Correctness contract:** `media/write_stream_test.go` asserts `WriteTo` output is **byte-for-byte identical** to `WriteToBytes` across explicit VR, implicit VR, big-endian, and the deflated fallback (2 fixtures × 5 transfer syntaxes), and that the streamed file parses back.

### 2. wado: `retrieveFrames` returned an empty 200 for large multi-frame objects — bug

The handler called `GetPixelData` per frame. That accessor sizes **and caps** its allocation across **all** frames:

```
sizePx = cols*rows*bitsa/8 (x3 if RGB) * frames
if sizePx > maxPixelDataBytes -> error       // 512 MiB
```

So any uncompressed object whose *total* pixel data exceeded 512 MiB failed on **every** frame — and the loop did `continue` on error, so the client got an **empty multipart body with HTTP 200 and nothing logged**. 512 MiB is reachable in practice: 512×512×16-bit × 1000 frames ≈ 524 MB; enhanced multi-frame CT/MR and 4D datasets hit it.

Now uses `GetDecompressedFrame` (caps **per frame**) and logs failures rather than silently skipping.

⚠️ **Behaviour change worth a reviewer's eye:** `GetPixelData` returned *raw compressed fragments* for encapsulated syntaxes; `GetDecompressedFrame` decompresses. WADO-RS frames served as `application/octet-stream` are expected to be uncompressed, so the previous behaviour was non-conformant — but this does change bytes on the wire for compressed objects.

### 3. wado: stream instances into their multipart part

`retrieveInstances` buffered each object via `WriteToBytes` before writing it; it now writes through `WriteTo`, so no full copy is held per part.

## Compatibility note

`WriteTo` is added to the public `DICOMObject` interface. That is source-breaking for any **explicit** implementer (embedders are unaffected). All three in-repo consumers — **io-scp**, **io-router**, **go-bridge** — build, vet and test green against the widened interface; io-scp's test double embeds the interface, so it needed no change.

## Testing
- Full suite green; `-race` clean on `media/` and `wado/`; `go vet` clean
- Byte-equality test across 10 file × transfer-syntax combinations
- All three consumers build, vet, and test green

## Relationship to #29
Independent of [#29](https://github.com/innovative-io/io-dicom/pull/29) and branched from `main`, so the two can merge in either order. They touch different regions of `media/dicom_object.go`.

author: sigilante
body:
## What

Adds `hoon/tests/dumb/mod/unit/state-10-to-11.hoon` — four unit arms covering the Logos kernel state-10 → state-11 migration, and specifically its **activation guard**.

`+state-10-to-11` refuses to migrate a node whose synced chain tip has already reached `ai-pow-activation-height`:

```hoon
~|  %state-10-post-ai-lineage-cannot-be-reconstructed
?>  migration-safe
```

## Why

Unlike every prior migration (pure, deterministic field-remapping that succeeds or fails identically for every node), this guard is **conditional on runtime chain state** (`highest-block-height` vs `ai-pow-activation-height`). Its failure mode is therefore only reachable for the subset of nodes that cross the activation height *before* upgrading — a case no single upgrade smoke test surfaces, and one that had no direct coverage.

(The happy-path migration ladder itself is already exercised for state-8 → 11 by `h-zoon-consensus.hoon` via the same `+load:inner:dumb` idiom; this PR adds the missing coverage for the guard's conditional specifically.)

## How

Drives the real `+load` through `+load:inner:dumb` — the same entry the runtime uses when a new kernel is swapped in over old state:

| arm | tip | expectation |
|---|---|---|
| `migrates-fresh-node` | none | migrates to `%11`, empty `block-versions` / `puzzle-asert-states` |
| `migrates-tip-below-activation` | `activation − 1` | reaches `%11` (passes the guard) |
| `refuses-tip-at-activation` | `== activation` | crashes with `%state-10-post-ai-lineage-cannot-be-reconstructed` |
| `refuses-tip-past-activation` | `> activation` | same |

The four arms are self-checking against the activation-height constant: any drift in the default flips one of them (a tip that was below activation would start crashing, or one at activation would stop).

Run:

```
roswell run-test test-state-10-to-11
```

All four pass against this branch's head; full `roswell test-dumb` is unaffected.
